small-talisman-charm.summary: Compact tier-1 special charm from Act I chests and bounties, carried in the pack to bolster a hero's resilience.
small-talisman-charm.flavor: Whittled from river-driftwood and stamped with a rough Alder Ford toll-mark by recruits hoping a pocket trinket turns aside gnoll arrows. Quartermasters rarely bother logging them, yet few frontier soldiers ever throw one away.

large-relic-charm.summary: Substantial tier-2 special charm from Acts I–II chests and bounties, offering stronger passive pack blessings.
large-relic-charm.flavor: A palm-sized tablet of veined Redmarsh slate bound in tarnished copper wire by frontier surveyors and hedge-scholars. Heavier than a belt pouch of silver, it steadies a marcher's step through bog-mist and blistering alkali glare.

grand-mystic-charm.summary: Expansive tier-3 special charm from Acts II–III chests and bounties, prized for potent passive pack power.
grand-mystic-charm.flavor: Carved from salted leviathan bone and inlaid with coastal abbey silver lines that hum faintly whenever storms gather offshore. Veterans wrap these broad tablets in heavy oilcloth to guard their markings across long coastal campaigns.

rune-of-eldun.summary: Weightless tier-1 special rune from Act I chests and bounties, used in socketing and cube transmutations.
rune-of-eldun.flavor: Scratched onto pale river-slate by apprentice rune-cutters in Thornwick's damp workshops while rain drums on the roof. Though humble in rank, an Eldun stone steadies a recruit's aim and tightens the rivets on a battered wooden shield.

rune-of-elvar.summary: Early tier-1 special rune from Act I chests and cube upgrades, prized for defensive and martial socketing.
rune-of-elvar.flavor: Hammered into shield bosses by Alder Bridge watchmen who spend long shifts catching arrows on tarred oak boards. Border smiths swear an Elvar chip keeps cheap iron rims from splitting apart under heavy gnoll hatchets in the mud.

rune-of-tyra.summary: Foundational tier-1 special rune from Act I chests and bounties, valued for arcane socketing and runewords.
rune-of-tyra.flavor: Named after a frugal border hedge-mage who hated spending silver on blue draughts in town apothecaries. Set into a staff or shield, Tyra's mark draws a steady trickle of fresh focus from every fallen raider on the field.

rune-of-neph.summary: Sturdy tier-1 special rune from Act I chests and cube transmutations, suited for heavy impact and armor craft.
rune-of-neph.flavor: A blunt, square-cut glyph favored by pike-sergeants who want charging thorn-boars shoved straight back into the ditch. Even a light handaxe fitted with Neph hits with the rude, unanswerable jolt of a slammed fortress gate.

rune-of-aeth.summary: Light tier-1 special rune from Act I chests and bounties, essential for early runewords and steady recovery.
rune-of-aeth.flavor: Chiseled into chalk-pale stone and stitched into travel cloaks by scouts who cannot afford to stop and bandage every scratch. It keeps the blood moving cleanly when freezing drizzle turns the northern tracks to axle-deep mire.

rune-of-ithos.summary: Sharp tier-1 special rune from Act I chests and cube upgrades, enhancing weapon punch and defensive channeling.
rune-of-ithos.flavor: Battle-mages prize Ithos stones during messy ditch ambushes where taking a stray hit is unavoidable. Instead of wasting a bruised rib, the glyph converts incoming blows into enough reserve mana for an immediate arcane answer.

rune-of-talgor.summary: Venom-warding tier-1 special rune from Act I chests and bounties, sought for early armor runewords and resistance.
rune-of-talgor.flavor: Steeped in bitter Fenwick bog-myrtle before firing, Talgor stones smell faintly of crushed herbs and wet peat. Soldiers marching south toward Redmarsh trade spare rations just to socket one cleanly into their travel gear.

rune-of-ralon.summary: Heat-tempered tier-2 special rune from Acts I–II chests and bounties, prized for fire wards and weapon runewords.
rune-of-ralon.flavor: Quenched in glowing charcoal ash until its carved lines shine dull orange in dark cellars and smoky trenches. Ralon runes are standard issue for frontier sappers clearing burning barricades and cinderling nests along the border.

rune-of-orthan.summary: Copper-bound tier-2 special rune from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, valued for storm wards and helm craft.
rune-of-orthan.flavor: Wrapped in thin annealed copper wire during engraving so the stone drinks stray sparks without cracking open. Quarry miners and coastal marines alike keep an Orthan glyph handy whenever thunderheads roll off the grey hills.

rune-of-thulor.summary: Frost-carved tier-2 special rune from Acts I–II chests and bounties, granting winter chill and cold resistance.
rune-of-thulor.flavor: Split from frost-rimed slate along the high northern bluffs where river fog lingers past noon. Scouts socket Thulor into heavy wool cloaks before crossing windy passes, claiming it keeps rime off their bowstrings in sleet.

rune-of-amnir.summary: Tenacious tier-2 special rune from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, built for sustained close-quarters brawls.
rune-of-amnir.flavor: Border veterans value Amnir above prettier gems because it pays its keep in ugly, drawn-out skirmishes. Hammered into a sword hilt, it steadies a bleeding grip; mounted in a shield, it leaves attackers nursing split knuckles.

rune-of-solan.summary: Balanced tier-2 special rune from Acts I–II chests and bounties, prized for consistent strikes and damage reduction.
rune-of-solan.flavor: Struck in heavy brass-toned stone by Redmarsh artificers who had no patience for erratic blows on patrol. A Solan-socketed blade hits with stubborn regularity, while armor bearing its mark blunts glancing canyon hornbow arrows.

rune-of-shaela.summary: Nimble tier-2 special rune from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, sought for swift recovery and shield runewords.
rune-of-shaela.flavor: Light as pumice and slick to the thumb, Shaela stones circulate quietly among duelists and coastal boarding marines. When a heavy club rattles your helm, this little glyph helps you regain footing before the next swing lands.

rune-of-dolur.summary: Restorative tier-2 special rune from Acts I–II chests and bounties, valued for field mending and bone runewords.
rune-of-dolur.flavor: Oakhaven surgeons once sewed Dolur chips into stretcher-canvas when clean linen ran short after bloody coastal raids. It will not reattach a lost finger, yet on long marches it keeps old cuts from festering in the salt damp.

rune-of-helva.summary: Versatile tier-3 special rune from Acts II–III chests and bounties, serving as a key binder in cube transmutations.
rune-of-helva.flavor: Oddly blank to the naked eye, Helva stones carry no immediate blessing when hammered into plain frontier iron. Quartermasters still lock them in the strongbox, knowing master rune-smiths pay silver for their binding craft.

rune-of-ioran.summary: Stout tier-3 special rune from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, lending quarry-born strength to mid-game gear.
rune-of-ioran.flavor: Quarried from deep ironstone seams where miners work by tallow light until their shoulders knot like seasoned oak. Wearing Ioran in your harness lends the stubborn heft needed to hold heavy pavises through grueling sieges.

rune-of-lumix.summary: Lucid tier-3 special rune from Acts II–III chests and bounties, prized by casters for intellect, mana, and armor craft.
rune-of-lumix.flavor: Pale as chalked vellum, Lumix stones hum softly whenever a spellbook opens nearby. Collegium clerks keep them tucked inside ink-stained cuffs to stay sharp through midnight audits and complex ward-calibrations in the field.

rune-of-kord.summary: Agile tier-3 special rune from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, favored by scouts for speed, accuracy, and evasion.
rune-of-kord.flavor: Said to be cut for a cliff-runner who outpaced three tax-cutters across wet shingle without dropping his pack. Kord runes are prized by archers and ridge-scouts who prefer not to be standing where a heavy basalt club lands.

rune-of-falkor.summary: Heavy tier-3 special rune from Acts II–III chests and bounties, adding raw martial force to weapons and armor.
rune-of-falkor.flavor: Dark-veined stones stamped with a blunt hammer-mark by Ironcamp foundrymen working beside open vents. Mercenary captains hand Falkor runes to their best breachers, knowing extra shoulder behind a warhammer opens stuck gates fast.

rune-of-lemur.summary: Coveted tier-3 special rune from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, boosting gold spoils recovered from foes.
rune-of-lemur.flavor: Every thrifty quartermaster on the Border dreams of finding a Lemur stone in the bounty chest. Though it offers no edge in a swordfight, companies that socket it always seem to pry twice as many crowns out of fallen raiders' purses.

rune-of-pulon.summary: Granite-hard tier-3 special rune from Acts II–III chests and bounties, reinforcing weapon punch and armor defense.
rune-of-pulon.flavor: Cut from dense coastal granite that has weathered a thousand winter gales without pitting. Pulon reinforces worn plate and sharpens dull steel alike, making it one of the most fiercely contested prizes in any frontier cache.

rune-of-umbra.summary: Grim tier-4 special rune from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, inflicting bleeding wounds and elemental wards.
rune-of-umbra.flavor: Dark as cooled pitch and cold even beside a smelter fire, Umbra stones leave jagged, weeping cuts when mounted in steel. Set into a shield, however, the same stark glyph drinks fire, frost, and lightning without complaint.

rune-of-malcor.summary: Ruthless tier-4 special rune from Acts III–IV chests and bounties, shutting down enemy healing and magic blasts.
rune-of-malcor.flavor: Forged in the caldera approaches where shamans and embalmers refuse to let their dead stay down. A single Malcor-marked blade halts battlefield mending, turning stubborn cultists into ordinary, manageable corpses in the ash.

rune-of-istari.summary: Seeking tier-4 special rune from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, increasing rare relic drops from enemies.
rune-of-istari.flavor: Relic-smugglers and vault-hunters trade whole chests of silver for a single Istari chip. It glows faintly near hidden armories and forgotten caches, guiding its bearer toward rare steel that ordinary patrols walk right past.

rune-of-guldan.summary: Alkali-cured tier-4 special rune from Acts III–IV chests and bounties, boosting accuracy and maximum poison wards.
rune-of-guldan.flavor: Soaked in distilled brine and sulfur fumes until the stone turns an indelible, bitter green. Veterans marching through spore-choked ruins prize Guldan for hardening their lungs against venoms that drop lesser men in three breaths.

rune-of-vexor.summary: Siphoning tier-4 special rune from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, draining mana and raising max fire wards.
rune-of-vexor.flavor: Warm as a banked forge-coal, Vexor draws stray energy out of every strike to feed hungry casters. Mounted in a cuirass or shield, it lets frontline troopers wade straight through caldera flames without blistering their skin.

rune-of-ohmar.summary: Glacial tier-4 special rune from Acts III–IV chests and bounties, adding heavy weapon force and max cold resistance.
rune-of-ohmar.flavor: Struck from pale alpine quartz that never cracks under a sledgehammer. Weapons fitted with Ohmar cleave through heavy bone and iron alike, while armor bearing its seal shrugs off glacial frost that snaps ordinary steel plates.

rune-of-loral.summary: Crackling tier-4 special rune from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, granting deadly strikes and max storm wards.
rune-of-loral.flavor: Sharp-edged and humming with bottled static, Loral turns clean hits into devastating finishing blows. Storm-coast marines also socket it into heavy shields so stray lightning arcs ground harmlessly into the wet flagstones.

rune-of-suran.summary: Deep-well tier-5 special rune from Act IV and Hard+ chests, expanding weapon damage and pinnacle mana reserves.
rune-of-suran.flavor: Indigo stones recovered from collapsed pre-schism observatories along the eastern ridge. Senior arcanists covet Suran above gold crowns, as a single stone holds enough reserve mana to sustain an entire volcanic siege barrage.

rune-of-beran.summary: Titan-breaking tier-5 special rune from Act IV and Hard+ chests, delivering crushing blows and damage reduction.
rune-of-beran.flavor: Dense as lead and scarred with ancient siege-marks, Beran is the nightmare of stone golems and armored colossi. One clean swing with a Beran-socketed maul can crack a granite guardian wide open like a dropped clay water jug.

rune-of-jahkar.summary: Unstoppable tier-5 special rune from Act IV and Hard+ chests, ignoring target defense and adding high health.
rune-of-jahkar.flavor: A merciless First-Dynasty war-glyph that refuses to acknowledge thick plate or clever parries. Soldiers who socket Jahkar into their harness seem to walk unscathed through volleys that should have pinned them to the dirt.

rune-of-chamir.summary: Rime-locked tier-5 special rune from Act IV and Hard+ chests, freezing enemies and preventing freeze on the bearer.
rune-of-chamir.flavor: Clear as glacier ice and painfully cold to bare fingers, Chamir locks foes in brittle frost on contact. Set into a tower shield, it keeps a vanguard captain moving freely even when frost-bells toll overhead in the dark crypts.

rune-of-zodar.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 special rune from Act IV and Hard+ chests, conferring supreme weapon damage and armor defense.
rune-of-zodar.flavor: The rarest stone in the Border ledgers, whispered about in taverns by veterans who have never actually seen one. Hammered into steel, Zodar elevates ordinary frontier iron into a weapon worthy of the Threshold gates itself.

sigil-of-ash.summary: Furnace-cast tier-5 boss trophy and vault key from Act IV Obsidian Caldera and Hard+ elites for Pinnacle Vault entry.
sigil-of-ash.flavor: Cast from blackened volcanic slag stamped with the furnace-mark of the caldera's inner redoubts. Warm to the touch and smelling faintly of sulfur, this heavy token serves as one of the keystones unlocking the Pinnacle Vault.

sigil-of-hollow.summary: Abbey-forged tier-5 boss trophy and vault key from Act IV Obsidian Caldera and Hard+ elites for the Pinnacle Vault.
sigil-of-hollow.flavor: Forged from cold, tarnished abbey silver etched with silent probate vows that rattle softly in still air. Recovered from the realm's fiercest guardians, this heavy token unseals one of the ancient locks guarding the Pinnacle Vault.

sigil-of-tide.summary: Brine-etched tier-5 boss trophy and vault key from Act IV Obsidian Caldera and Hard+ elites for the Pinnacle Vault.
sigil-of-tide.flavor: Salt-pitted bronze engraved with deep-current spirals salvaged from the drowned fortresses of the Iron Coast. Veterans guard this weathered token closely, knowing its weight is required to unseal the dark Pinnacle Vault.

pinnacle-writ.summary: Star-sealed tier-5 vault key and charter from Act IV Obsidian Caldera and Hard+ elites unlocking the Pinnacle Vault.
pinnacle-writ.flavor: Inscribed on indestructible pre-schism vellum and weighted with a star-iron seal that refuses to melt in volcanic heat. Bearing the final authority of the Threshold, this writ unlocks the deepest chamber of the Pinnacle Vault.

base-tarred-plank-targe.summary: Tarred tier-1 Warrior base shield from Act I racks and drops, serving as a rugged starter chassis for smithing.
base-tarred-plank-targe.flavor: Planks salvaged from broken river-barges and lashed together with iron barrel-hoops in Thornwick's muddy smithy yard. Brushed thick with pine pitch to keep river damp from swelling the wood, it turns aside gnoll hatchets long enough for a recruit to earn proper iron.

base-cracked-horn-buckler.summary: Light tier-1 Archer base shield from Act I racks and elite drops, built as a nimble early off-hand base.
base-cracked-horn-buckler.flavor: Stretched boiled hide over a split ram-horn rim that straps tightly to the forearm without fouling a bowstring draw. Fenwick hunters prize its featherlight feel when ducking thorny branches and snapping quill-fiend spines in wet brush.

base-iron-rimmed-heater.summary: Triangular tier-2 Warrior base shield found in Acts I and II, ready for sturdy border smithy upgrades.
base-iron-rimmed-heater.flavor: Curved alder planks bound in a continuous band of hammered border iron so heavy blows glance cleanly toward the mud. Alder picket veterans paint their parish badges across the face before marching out to hold contested river bridges.

base-surveyors-brass-mirror.summary: Reflective tier-2 Mage base shield from Acts I and II, suited for early arcane smithy enhancements.
base-surveyors-brass-mirror.flavor: Polished speculum brass mounted in an oak frame with sighting notches used by frontier geomancers to align roadside wayshrines. In a skirmish, its bright face catches stray sparks and steadies a caster's defensive ward-circles.

base-salt-oak-pavise.summary: Tall tier-3 Warrior base shield dropping in Acts II and III, ideal for heavy mid-campaign smithy work.
base-salt-oak-pavise.flavor: Seasoned in Redmarsh brine until the oak grain hardened like horn, then fitted with an iron ground-spike along the base. Caravan guards plant these broad shields in the alkali dust to shelter crossbowmen from canyon snipers.

base-ossuary-bone-ward.summary: Rib-braced tier-3 Necromancer base shield from Acts II and III, ready for dark-art smithy refinement.
base-ossuary-bone-ward.flavor: Assembled from bleached leviathan ribs wired onto salted leather by coastal abbey clerks who stood watch over sunken crypts. Etched probate seals along the boss rattle softly whenever restless spirits gather nearby.

base-oakhaven-galley-shield.summary: Heavy tier-4 Warrior base shield from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier naval smithy upgrades.
base-oakhaven-galley-shield.flavor: Reinforced with salt-tempered iron straps and a blunt boss designed for shoving boarders off wet gangplanks. Harborwatch marines rely on its broad coverage when advancing down piers swept by flaming pitch and arbalest bolts.

base-galvanic-copper-aegis.summary: Grounded tier-4 Mage base shield from Acts III and IV, prized for advanced arcane smithy refinement.
base-galvanic-copper-aegis.flavor: Hammered from heavy annealed copper sheet and ringed with braided grounding wire that bleeds stray lightning straight into the flagstones. Senior Collegium fellows carry these discs when auditing storm-lashed coastal wards.

base-obsidian-bulwark.summary: Massive tier-5 Warrior base shield from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for pinnacle smithy reinforcement.
base-obsidian-bulwark.flavor: Layered with dark volcanic ironstone quenched in caldera ash until the surface turned dull as cooled slag. Vanguard champions plant it in the cinders to absorb titan hammer blows that shatter ordinary steel.

base-threshold-ward-mirror.summary: Ancient tier-5 Necromancer base shield from Act IV and Hard+ drops, built for endgame dark smithing.
base-threshold-ward-mirror.flavor: Cast from pale star-silver and dark iron around a smoked quartz glass recovered from pre-schism vault doors. Arbiters marching into the Threshold carry it to turn aside eldritch curses and volcanic glare alike.

base-twisted-bog-wire-ring.summary: Rough tier-1 Warrior base ring from Act I racks and drops, offering a basic early band for smithing.
base-twisted-bog-wire-ring.flavor: Braided from salvaged iron snare-wire by Fenwick ditch-cutters who needed something tougher than copper to hold simple ward-stamps. It pinches slightly when wet, yet stays firmly on calloused knuckles through muddy brawls.

base-tallow-wax-signet.summary: Inscribed tier-1 Necromancer base ring from Act I drops and racks, suited for early mortuary smithing.
base-tallow-wax-signet.flavor: Cast from dull pewter with a flat seal-face used by lower-parish clerks to stamp tallow seals onto pauper burial rolls. Cold against the thumb, it anchors simple binding charms during drafty crypt patrols.

base-river-pebble-band.summary: Smooth tier-1 Archer base ring from Act I racks and elite drops, serving as a light early ring chassis.
base-river-pebble-band.flavor: A tiny, water-worn Alder River stone set into a simple bronze hoop by border bowmen who believed river luck kept arrows flying true. Weightless on the drawing hand, it never catches on bowstrings or quiver straps.

base-alkali-etched-band.summary: Corroded tier-2 Archer base ring found in Acts I and II, ready for desert-grade smithy upgrades.
base-alkali-etched-band.flavor: Steeped in caustic Redmarsh brine until rough geometric grooves bit deep into the bronze band. Caravan outriders wear them on their off-hand to anchor wind-reading charms against blinding salt-pan gales.

base-copper-coil-ring.summary: Wound tier-2 Mage base ring from Acts I and II, built as a conductive chassis for arcane smithing.
base-copper-coil-ring.flavor: Twisted from three turns of bright smelter copper by hedge-scholars who needed a reliable way to bleed static off their fingertips. It leaves a faint green stain on the skin while keeping early casts orderly.

base-toll-wardens-signet.summary: Heavy tier-2 Warrior base ring from Acts I and II, suited for sturdy martial smithy enhancements.
base-toll-wardens-signet.flavor: Issued to bridge-sergeants along the northern highways to stamp supply chits and reinforce basic endurance wards. Thick enough to survive a hammer blow, it often doubles as brass knuckles in tavern disputes.

base-salt-glass-ring.summary: Glassy tier-3 Mage base ring dropping in Acts II and III, prized for mid-campaign arcane smithing.
base-salt-glass-ring.flavor: Set with a shard of lightning-fused desert fulgurite that crackles faintly whenever storm-clouds gather overhead. Field arcanists trade good silver for bands that channel volatile charge without cracking.

base-probate-bailiffs-band.summary: Stamped tier-3 Necromancer base ring from Acts II and III, ready for mid-game dark smithy craft.
base-probate-bailiffs-band.flavor: Engraved with the Third Dynasty's sharpest foreclosure mark, worn by notaries who collected overdue debts in sunken salt-vaults. Even restless skeletons seem to march briskly when ordered by a hand wearing this seal.

base-harbor-chain-ring.summary: Linked tier-3 Warrior base ring from Acts II and III, built for rugged coastal smithy upgrades.
base-harbor-chain-ring.flavor: Forged from miniature iron anchor-links welded solid by Oakhaven shipwrights for boarding marines. Salt spray never pits its dark finish, and its solid weight steadies the sword-hand on pitching decks.

base-beacon-lens-signet.summary: Faceted tier-4 Archer base ring from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier precision smithing.
base-beacon-lens-signet.flavor: Mounted with a tiny chip of lighthouse prism-glass that catches distant glints through coastal fog and blowing ash. Harborwatch marksmen prize its crisp alignment when sighting targets across wide channels.

base-ossuary-seal-ring.summary: Leaden tier-4 Necromancer base ring from Acts III and IV, suited for late-game dark smithing.
base-ossuary-seal-ring.flavor: Cast from heavy abbey lead and inlaid with silver wire copied from sea-ossuary lintel wards. Coastal oath-keepers wear it to anchor necrotic conduits when calling spirits up from the deep.

base-galvanic-arc-band.summary: Charged tier-4 Mage base ring from Acts III and IV, ready for advanced elemental smithy work.
base-galvanic-arc-band.flavor: Paired rings of star-silver and annealed copper hum continuously around the finger, storing stray ambient charge between volleys. Senior fellows wear them when calibrating unstable coastal and highland wards.

base-caldera-slag-signet.summary: Scorched tier-5 Warrior base ring from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame martial smithing.
base-caldera-slag-signet.flavor: Hammered from dark meteoric iron around a trapped bead of glowing volcanic glass that stays warm in freezing mountain wind. Vanguard commanders wear it into the inner caldera as a mark of unyielding grit.

base-first-watch-oath-ring.summary: Ancient tier-5 Necromancer base ring from Act IV and Hard+ drops, built for pinnacle dark craft.
base-first-watch-oath-ring.flavor: Recovered from silent stone alcoves guarding the deep Threshold approaches, inscribed with forgotten vows of eternal vigil. Dark-art masters prize its cold authority when commanding legions in the volcanic gloom.

base-spire-keystone-band.summary: Exalted tier-5 Mage base ring from Act IV and Hard+ drops, prized for pinnacle arcane smithing.
base-spire-keystone-band.flavor: Wrought from pure star-silver aligned to pre-schism observatory charts preserved in the Spire Conclave. Senior archons rely on its quiet resonance to sustain massive spells without faltering.

base-braided-rush-charm.summary: Woven tier-1 Archer base amulet from Act I racks and drops, serving as a simple early charm chassis.
base-braided-rush-charm.flavor: Plaited from tough river-reeds and knotted around a dry goose-quill by northern hunters before stepping into misty thickets. Light as air against the collarbone, it holds basic trail-wards without rattling.

base-leaden-parish-token.summary: Stamped tier-1 Necromancer base amulet from Act I drops and racks, suited for early mortuary craft.
base-leaden-parish-token.flavor: A dull lead disc punched with a parish grave-number and hung on tarred twine by sextons working damp border ditches. Clerks etch binding marks onto its soft face to keep restless bones in line.

base-chipped-flint-gorget.summary: Rough tier-1 Warrior base amulet from Act I racks and elite drops, offering a sturdy starter neck-charm.
base-chipped-flint-gorget.flavor: A broad flake of grey river-flint bound in rawhide thongs and worn high at the throat by Thornwick levies. Crude as a stone axe, it turns aside stray briar-thorns and anchors basic endurance charms.

base-brine-vial-pendant.summary: Stoppered tier-2 Archer base amulet found in Acts I and II, ready for desert smithy enhancements.
base-brine-vial-pendant.flavor: A tiny blown-glass phial filled with bitter Redmarsh salt-water and sealed with black bitumen on a leather cord. Outriders wear it across scorching flats to anchor cooling and antivenom charms.

base-copper-plumb-amulet.summary: Weighted tier-2 Mage base amulet from Acts I and II, built as a practical base for arcane smiths.
base-copper-plumb-amulet.flavor: A pointed copper plumb-bob hung from a braided wire chain, originally used by frontier surveyors to measure ley-inclines. Hedge-arcanists discovered its steady pendulum swing helps focus spells on bumpy marches.

base-iron-ration-tag.summary: Stamped tier-2 Warrior base amulet from Acts I and II, suited for rugged martial smithy upgrades.
base-iron-ration-tag.flavor: A thick square of border pig-iron stamped with a soldier's company number and worn beneath the tunic on a hemp string. Veterans hammer protective runes straight into its scarred face between campaigns.

base-amber-fen-beetle-charm.summary: Fossilized tier-3 Necromancer base amulet from Acts II and III, ready for mid-game dark smithing.
base-amber-fen-beetle-charm.flavor: A lump of dark bog-amber enclosing an ancient marsh beetle, wired into a tarnished bronze bezel by abbey clerks. Necromancers prize its eerie stillness for anchoring curses and spirit-tethers.

base-salt-crystal-pendulum.summary: Crystalline tier-3 Mage base amulet dropping in Acts II and III, prized for mid-campaign smithing.
base-salt-crystal-pendulum.flavor: A clear six-sided halite crystal harvested from dry Third-Dynasty vaults and caged in thin silver wire. It tingles sharply in humid or static-heavy air, guiding casters through volatile elemental fights.

base-sea-wall-anchor-charm.summary: Heavy tier-3 Warrior base amulet from Acts II and III, built for sturdy coastal smithy work.
base-sea-wall-anchor-charm.flavor: Cast from salvaged harbor bronze in the shape of a miniature fluke-anchor and worn over the breastbone by Oakhaven marines. Its solid heft anchors defensive wards when holding wave-swept seawalls.

base-smoked-quartz-monocle.summary: Tinted tier-4 Archer base amulet from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier precision smithing.
base-smoked-quartz-monocle.flavor: A ground lens of dark highland quartz framed in brass on a long neck-chain so marksmen can flip it over one eye in blinding glare. Scouts use it to spot weak armor seams through coastal fog and ash.

base-ash-urn-reliquary.summary: Sealed tier-4 Necromancer base amulet from Acts III and IV, suited for late-game dark craft.
base-ash-urn-reliquary.flavor: A small lead-lined bronze cylinder packed with consecrated funeral ash from coastal abbey vaults. Senior arbiters wear it at the throat to steady necrotic channels when raising legions in hostile territory.

base-conclave-tuning-fork.summary: Resonant tier-4 Mage base amulet from Acts III and IV, ready for advanced arcane smithy refinement.
base-conclave-tuning-fork.flavor: Forged from pale star-silver alloy that rings with a pure, clear note when tapped against a staff-ferrule. Collegium fellows rely on its steady vibration to keep complex wards calibrated amid siege noise.

base-cinder-heart-talisman.summary: Smoldering tier-5 Warrior base amulet from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithing.
base-cinder-heart-talisman.flavor: A dense knot of meteoric iron cradling a live ember from the Obsidian Caldera that never cools to ash. Vanguard champions wear it into the deepest volcanic trenches, drawing stubborn heat against freezing and fiery foes alike.

base-threshold-seal-gorget.summary: Inscribed tier-5 Necromancer base amulet from Act IV and Hard+ drops, built for pinnacle dark craft.
base-threshold-seal-gorget.flavor: A curved collar of blackened star-iron etched with pre-schism lintel glyphs that hum softly near ancient vaults. Dark-art masters clasp it tight before crossing into the Threshold's silent chambers.

base-astral-prism-medallion.summary: Radiant tier-5 Mage base amulet from Act IV and Hard+ drops, prized for pinnacle arcane smithing.
base-astral-prism-medallion.flavor: Cut from a flawless pre-schism crystal mounted inside interlocking star-silver rings that spin smoothly on the chest. Senior archons rely on its immense clarity to channel endgame sorcery without strain.

base-bog-moss-poultice.summary: Herbal tier-1 all-class consumable base from Act I drops and racks, suited for early field craft.
base-bog-moss-poultice.flavor: Wads of absorbent Fenwick sphagnum moss packed with crushed willow-bark and wrapped in clean rag strips. Northern borderers keep these damp bundles tucked in dry pouches to stanch bleeding after ditch skirmishes.

base-tallow-ration-hardbread.summary: Dense tier-1 all-class consumable base from Act I drops and racks, built for basic march sustenance.
base-tallow-ration-hardbread.flavor: Twice-baked barley biscuits brushed with salted mutton tallow so they survive months in a wet saddlebag without molding. Tough enough to chip a tooth, they keep hungry levies marching when supply wagons lag behind.

base-bitter-gall-draught.summary: Astringent tier-1 Mage consumable base from Act I racks and drops, suited for early arcane craft.
base-bitter-gall-draught.flavor: Boiled from crushed oak-galls, bog-myrtle, and spring water in smoky hedge-apothecary sheds. One foul gulp clears the cobwebs of a sleepless night watch and sharpens an apprentice's focus.

base-crude-whetstone-block.summary: Coarse tier-1 Warrior consumable base from Act I drops and racks, used for basic blade upkeep.
base-crude-whetstone-block.flavor: Quarried from grey river-sandstone and grooved down the center from dressing hundreds of notched levy axes and pikes. Every veteran carries a pocket stone to keep rust and burrs off frontier iron.

base-parish-ward-scroll.summary: Humble tier-1 Necromancer consumable base from Act I racks and drops, ready for early scribe work.
base-parish-ward-scroll.flavor: A narrow slip of rough sheepskin stamped with a lower-parish boundary prayer in oak-gall ink. Sextons tuck them under coffin lids or into belt pouches to steady minor protective wards on patrol.

base-scrap-bog-iron-ingot.summary: Rough tier-1 all-class consumable base from Act I drops and racks, serving as basic smithy stock.
base-scrap-bog-iron-ingot.flavor: Smelted in small clay bloomeries from impure northern marsh-ore and hammered into hand-sized bars. Pitted with charcoal slag, it still gives village smiths enough honest metal to patch rivets and arrowheads.

base-redmarsh-saline-tonic.summary: Briny tier-2 all-class consumable base found in Acts I and II, built for harsh desert field craft.
base-redmarsh-saline-tonic.flavor: Filtered Redmarsh salt-water boiled with sour vinegar and dried desert mint to replace what a soldier sweats out under noon glare. Caravan guards ration every drop when crossing waterless alkali flats.

base-viper-antivenom-phial.summary: Distilled tier-2 Archer consumable base from Acts I and II, suited for poison-countering craft.
base-viper-antivenom-phial.flavor: Prepared by milking desert scale vipers and cooking the venom down with bitter alkali roots in stoppered green glass. Border scouts carry one wired to their quiver strap whenever snakes sun on the canyon rocks.

base-copper-filings-phial.summary: Conductive tier-2 Mage consumable base from Acts I and II, ready for early storm-ward craft.
base-copper-filings-phial.flavor: Bright copper shavings swept from smelter benches and sealed dry inside a corked glass tube. Field arcanists sprinkle the dust into chalk circles to ground stray static before casting near quartz spires.

base-cured-fen-hide-bundle.summary: Oiled tier-2 Archer consumable base found in Acts I and II, used for light armor and bow repairs.
base-cured-fen-hide-bundle.flavor: Rolled strips of supple deerhide steeped in bog-tannin and beeswax to shed rain and alkali dust alike. Hunters use them to patch torn jerkins, wrap bow-grips, and silence clinking belt buckles on the march.

base-notarized-hex-vellum.summary: Stamped tier-2 Necromancer consumable base from Acts I and II, built for probate ward craft.
base-notarized-hex-vellum.flavor: Heavy calfskin sheets pre-ruled with Third-Dynasty ledger columns and stamped with a leaden notary seal. Clerks inscribe binding clauses onto the crisp vellum before marching into haunted ruins.

base-tempered-flux-powder.summary: Mineral tier-2 all-class consumable base from Acts I and II, serving as mid-early smithy stock.
base-tempered-flux-powder.flavor: Crushed limestone, borax salt, and dry charcoal sifted together into oiled paper packets by Redmarsh smiths. Tossed onto glowing iron, it floats impurities cleanly off the metal so welds hold tight.

base-alkali-blood-restorative.summary: Fortified tier-3 all-class consumable base from Acts II and III, suited for mid-campaign remedies.
base-alkali-blood-restorative.flavor: A sharp, iron-rich draught brewed from desert succulents, boiled bone-marrow, and distilled brine. Field surgeons along the coastal road rely on it to bring exhausted, blood-drained troops back onto their feet.

base-galvanic-ether-ampoule.summary: Volatile tier-3 Mage consumable base found in Acts II and III, built for rapid arcane craft.
base-galvanic-ether-ampoule.flavor: Sealed glass bulbs filled with clear, tingling spirit charged beside plateau quartz monoliths. Snapping the neck releases a sharp smell of ozone and gives a tired caster a brisk jolt of focus.

base-bitumen-sealant-jar.summary: Tarry tier-3 Necromancer consumable base from Acts II and III, ready for mortuary preservation craft.
base-bitumen-sealant-jar.flavor: Heavy clay pots packed with black mineral pitch dredged from sunken Third-Dynasty quays. Coastal embalmers and necro-clerks brush it warm over bandages and ward-staves to seal out rot and salt damp.

base-scroll-of-iron-skin.summary: Reinforced tier-3 Warrior consumable base from Acts II and III, suited for defensive field craft.
base-scroll-of-iron-skin.flavor: Stiff vellum backed with thin canvas and inscribed with heavy earth-ward sigils by fortress artificers. Unrolled before a breach assault, it helps frontliners shrug off heavy blows without slowing down.

base-refined-harbor-steel-bar.summary: Tempered tier-3 all-class consumable base from Acts II and III, serving as solid smithy stock.
base-refined-harbor-steel-bar.flavor: Clean, slag-free steel ingots smelted in Oakhaven's coastal yards and stamped with the shipwright guild's anchor mark. Armorers prize these uniform bars for forging reliable blades and seawall plate.

base-salt-cured-sinew-coil.summary: Elastic tier-3 Archer consumable base found in Acts II and III, used for high-tension bow craft.
base-salt-cured-sinew-coil.flavor: Braided ox-tendon steeped in brine and dried taut in coastal gales until it snaps like tempered wire. Bowyers and arbalest crews rely on these coils to restring heavy prods without losing draw weight.

base-oakhaven-aqua-vitae.summary: Distilled tier-4 all-class consumable base from Acts III and IV, built for potent late-act remedies.
base-oakhaven-aqua-vitae.flavor: Triple-distilled coastal spirit infused with alpine herbs and stored in waxed oak flasks by Harborwatch surgeons. One fiery swallow numbs deep wounds and steadies trembling hands during relentless sieges.

base-leyline-spark-elixir.summary: Charged tier-4 Mage consumable base found in Acts III and IV, suited for high-tier arcane craft.
base-leyline-spark-elixir.flavor: Luminescent blue distillate brewed from crushed storm-quartz and deep spring water in Collegium field-stills. Senior arcanists carry stoppered phials into battle to keep their mana channels humming cleanly.

base-ossuary-ash-incense.summary: Consecrated tier-4 Necromancer consumable base from Acts III and IV, ready for late-game ritual craft.
base-ossuary-ash-incense.flavor: Compressed cones of bone-ash, sea-salt, and dried rue burned in bronze censers by coastal abbey arbiters. The thick, bitter smoke quiets restless spirits and strengthens necrotic tethers in deep vaults.

base-scroll-of-fissure-ward.summary: Heatproof tier-4 all-class consumable base from Acts III and IV, built for caldera survival craft.
base-scroll-of-fissure-ward.flavor: Inscribed on treated mineral paper by highland pathfinders who mapped the smoking approaches to the Obsidian Caldera. Carrying a fresh sheet helps squads endure sulfurous vents and blistering volcanic drafts.

base-meteoric-slag-chunk.summary: Dense tier-4 all-class consumable base from Acts III and IV, serving as high-grade smithy stock.
base-meteoric-slag-chunk.flavor: Heavy, pitted lumps of sky-iron pried from highland craters and partially fused with volcanic glass. Ironcamp foundrymen crack them open with sledgehammers to extract pure metal for elite weapons.

base-wyrm-scale-bundle.summary: Scaled tier-4 Archer consumable base found in Acts III and IV, used for elite light-armor craft.
base-wyrm-scale-bundle.flavor: Tied stacks of iridescent drake scales scraped clean and cured in sulfur tallow by highland hunters. Armorers lace them onto supple leather jerkins to turn aside fire and claws without adding bulk.

base-threshold-ichor-phial.summary: Potent tier-5 all-class consumable base from Act IV and Hard+ drops, built for pinnacle remedies.
base-threshold-ichor-phial.flavor: Thick, metallic distillate harvested from deep pre-schism conduits beneath the volcanic peaks and sealed in lead-stoppered crystal. A single draught sustains vanguard champions through the fiercest Threshold trials.

base-celestial-spire-distillate.summary: Exalted tier-5 Mage consumable base from Act IV and Hard+ drops, suited for endgame arcane craft.
base-celestial-spire-distillate.flavor: Pure, cold-glowing essence refined in the Spire Conclave's highest galleries using star-silver coils and snowmelt. Master arcanists guard every drop to fuel devastating endgame barrages.

base-first-watch-edict-scroll.summary: Ancient tier-5 Necromancer consumable base from Act IV and Hard+ drops, ready for pinnacle dark craft.
base-first-watch-edict-scroll.flavor: Preserved on pale, indestructible parchment recovered from the silent guardians of the inner caldera. Reading its stern pre-schism statutes binds undead servants with unbreakable discipline.

base-caldera-ember-core.summary: Incandescent tier-5 all-class consumable base from Act IV and Hard+ drops, built for volcanic craft.
base-caldera-ember-core.flavor: A fist-sized knot of crystallized magma caged in star-iron wire that pulses steadily like a living heart. Smiths and arcanists alike tap its relentless heat to temper endgame gear.

base-star-iron-ingot.summary: Refined tier-5 all-class consumable base from Act IV and Hard+ drops, serving as pinnacle smithy stock.
base-star-iron-ingot.flavor: Smelted from pure meteoric ore in Ironcamp's hottest furnaces and stamped with the forge-guild's master mark. Pale, rustproof, and unyielding, it forms the backbone of the realm's finest weapons and plate.

base-void-glass-shard.summary: Dark tier-5 Mage consumable base from Act IV and Hard+ drops, suited for endgame arcane craft.
base-void-glass-shard.flavor: Razor-edged splinters of black volcanic glass shot through with violet ley-threads from the deepest caldera fissures. Archons grind and mount them to focus spells that pierce ancient wards.

sim-dagger.summary: Light tier-1 socketed base dagger from Act I drops and gamble, dealing 1–4 damage with 1 max socket.
sim-dagger.flavor: A plain, double-edged iron utility blade carried in every border scout's boot-top for cutting cordage and finishing close grapples. With space for a single socketed stone, smiths often fit a cheap garnet into the pommel.

sim-kris.summary: Wavy tier-2 socketed base dagger from Acts I–II requiring 10 Agility, dealing 3–8 damage with 2 max sockets.
sim-kris.flavor: Forged with a sinuous flame-shaped blade that widens wounds and catches enemy parries in tight canyon brawls. Two open settings along the brass guard invite paired gems or low runes.

sim-short-sword.summary: Compact tier-1 socketed base sword from Act I requiring 10 Body, dealing 3–7 damage with 2 max sockets.
sim-short-sword.flavor: Stout, double-edged infantry sidearm built for thrusting over shield-rims in crowded northern river ditches. Simple and forgiving to wield, its fuller holds two clean sockets for early rune-work.

sim-crystal-sword.summary: Translucent tier-2 socketed base sword from Acts I–II requiring 15 Body, dealing 5–15 damage with 4 max sockets.
sim-crystal-sword.flavor: Ground from dense, smoky plateau quartz bound to a copper-wired hilt that hums faintly when swung. Fragile-looking yet wickedly sharp, its broad blade accommodates up to four sockets for ambitious artificers.

sim-broad-sword.summary: Wide-bladed tier-2 socketed base sword from Acts I–II requiring 20 Body, dealing 7–14 damage with 4 max sockets.
sim-broad-sword.flavor: Heavy basket-hilted border blade favored by veteran regulars who prefer solid cutting weight over delicate fencing. Four evenly spaced settings along the ricasso make it a favorite chassis for multi-rune blades.

sim-phase-blade.summary: Elusive tier-5 socketed base sword from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 25 Body and 35 Agility, dealing 25–35 damage with 6 sockets.
sim-phase-blade.flavor: Wrought from pale, weightless star-glass that flickers like heat-haze over volcanic stone and never dulls against basalt plate. Six open sockets let master smiths channel immense power through its edge.

sim-claymore.summary: Two-handed tier-2 socketed base greatsword from Acts I–II requiring 25 Body, dealing 9–20 damage with 4 max sockets.
sim-claymore.flavor: Long, straight northern greatsword with down-sloping quillons built for sweeping aside packs of briar-hounds and gnoll raiders. Its broad steel fuller easily accepts four sockets for heavy frontline enchantments.

sim-colossus-blade.summary: Massive tier-5 socketed base greatsword from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 45 Body and 25 Agility, dealing 45–85 damage with 6 sockets.
sim-colossus-blade.flavor: Towering meteoric-steel greatsword forged in Ironcamp's deepest yards for champions strong enough to swing a siege-beam. Six deep sockets line its heavy blade, ready for the realm's rarest high runes.

sim-hand-axe.summary: Single-handed tier-1 socketed base axe from Act I requiring 10 Body, dealing 3–6 damage with 2 max sockets.
sim-hand-axe.flavor: Balanced border hatchet equally handy for splitting camp firewood or hooking a raider's wooden buckler. Two clean settings punched behind the beard allow early upgrades without slowing the swing.

sim-berserker-axe.summary: Brutal tier-5 socketed base axe from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 35 Body and 20 Agility, dealing 24–71 damage with 6 sockets.
sim-berserker-axe.flavor: Broad-bearded caldera war-axe tempered in volcanic ash until the dark steel rings like an anvil on every blow. Six open sockets make it one of the most devastating one-handed weapons on the frontier.

sim-mace.summary: Solid tier-1 socketed base mace from Act I requiring 15 Body, dealing 3–10 damage with 2 max sockets.
sim-mace.flavor: Heavy iron head pinned onto an ash haft to cave in helmets and crack flintback carapaces without risking a snapped blade. Two sockets set into the collar hold basic gems or runes reliably.

sim-flail.summary: Chained tier-2 socketed base weapon from Acts I–II requiring 18 Body and 15 Agility, dealing 4–24 damage with 5 max sockets.
sim-flail.flavor: Spiked iron ball swinging on a short forged chain that wraps neatly around raised shields to strike the arm behind. Five open settings across the head and haft offer rare versatility for early runewords.

sim-scepter.summary: Flanged tier-2 socketed base weapon from Acts I–II requiring 15 Body, dealing 6–15 damage with 3 max sockets.
sim-scepter.flavor: Heavy bronze-shod mace carried by abbey bailiffs and frontier commanders to enforce order and crush armored foes alike. Three clean sockets along the head welcome gems or sacred runes.

sim-colossus-voulge.summary: Heavy tier-5 socketed base polearm from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 40 Body and 15 Agility, dealing 17–120 damage with 4 sockets.
sim-colossus-voulge.flavor: Massive cleaver-blade mounted on an iron-bound ash pole for halting charging titans and dread knights in narrow caldera passes. Four deep sockets allow formidable endgame rune combinations.

sim-short-bow.summary: Compact tier-1 socketed base bow from Act I requiring 10 Agility, dealing 1–5 damage with 3 max sockets.
sim-short-bow.flavor: Light northern ash bow favored by Thornwick scouts who need quick shots from dense brush and muddy ditches. Three small settings inlaid along the riser accept early gems to steady aim or add elemental bite.

sim-hydra-bow.summary: Multi-limbed tier-5 socketed base bow from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 25 Body and 45 Agility, dealing 10–68 damage with 6 sockets.
sim-hydra-bow.flavor: Complex recurve warbow reinforced with laminated horn and star-iron brackets that snap arrows forward with terrifying force. Six open sockets let master bowyers build a true endgame instrument.

sim-short-staff.summary: Simple tier-1 socketed base staff from Act I drops and gamble, dealing 2–6 damage with 2 max sockets.
sim-short-staff.flavor: Waist-high oak walking stave shod with copper ferrules for apprentice casters trekking along wet border roads. Two clean sockets near the crown hold early crystals to bolster fledgling spells.

sim-archon-staff.summary: Exalted tier-5 socketed base staff from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Body, dealing 35–65 damage with 6 sockets.
sim-archon-staff.flavor: Tall star-ironwood staff inlaid with intricate Collegium ley-channels for senior masters marching into the Obsidian Caldera. Six open sockets allow unmatched arcane customization at the anvil.

sim-bone-wand.summary: Carved tier-2 socketed base wand from Acts I–II drops and gamble, dealing 3–7 damage with 2 max sockets.
sim-bone-wand.flavor: Turned from a dense leviathan rib-bone and etched with lower-parish probate tallies for field necromancers. Two neat settings along the shaft hold gems or low runes to strengthen dark bindings.

sim-quilted-armor.summary: Padded tier-1 socketed base armor from Act I offering 8 defense and 1 absorption with 2 max sockets.
sim-quilted-armor.flavor: Layered hemp cloth stuffed with raw wool and stitched in tight diamond channels to cushion recruits against clubs and arrows. Two reinforced eyelets allow early socketed stones without tearing the fabric.

sim-leather-armor.summary: Supple tier-1 socketed base armor from Act I requiring 10 Body, granting 14 defense, 1 absorption, and 2 max sockets.
sim-leather-armor.flavor: Boiled cowhide jerkin greased with tallow so northern rain beads off the shoulders during long river watches. Light and quiet on the march, it holds two clean sockets for early defensive upgrades.

sim-breast-plate.summary: Shaped tier-2 socketed base armor from Acts I–II requiring 15 Body, offering 25 defense, 2 absorption, and 3 max sockets.
sim-breast-plate.flavor: Hammered bronze-and-iron chestplate curved to deflect frontal thrusts while leaving the legs free for muddy terrain. Three socket mounts along the sternum let smiths tailor it for desert or marsh campaigns.

sim-mage-plate.summary: Lightened tier-4 socketed base armor from Acts III–IV requiring 20 Body, granting 55 defense, 4 absorption, and 3 max sockets.
sim-mage-plate.flavor: Thin, high-carbon steel plates fluted to shave away excess weight so battle-mages and officers keep full mobility. Three precision sockets make it a prized chassis for late-act defensive runewords.

sim-archon-plate.summary: Supreme tier-5 socketed base armor from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 30 Body, delivering 95 defense, 6 absorption, and 4 sockets.
sim-archon-plate.flavor: Masterwork star-steel harness articulated so smoothly a veteran can sprint across volcanic scree without fatigue. Four open sockets provide immense protection for endgame warriors and casters alike.

sim-ring-mail.summary: Sewn tier-1 socketed base armor from Act I requiring 15 Body, providing 20 defense, 2 absorption, and 3 max sockets.
sim-ring-mail.flavor: Heavy iron rings stitched side-by-side onto a tough oxhide backing by Thornwick armorers short on riveted chain. Noisy on patrol, it still offers three solid sockets for early frontier fortifications.

sim-chain-mail.summary: Riveted tier-2 socketed base armor from Acts I–II requiring 25 Body, granting 35 defense, 3 absorption, and 3 max sockets.
sim-chain-mail.flavor: Interlocking iron mesh that drapes over the shoulders like a heavy blanket, turning aside slashing blades in close brawls. Three reinforced mounts along the chest accept gems or mid-early runes.

sim-field-plate.summary: Articulated tier-3 socketed base armor from Acts II–III requiring 35 Body, offering 50 defense, 4 absorption, and 4 max sockets.
sim-field-plate.flavor: Layered steel plates buckled over thick oiled leather for veteran regulars holding canyon passes and coastal seawalls. Four open sockets allow substantial defensive customization at the forge.

sim-full-plate.summary: Heavy tier-3 socketed base armor from Acts II–III requiring 40 Body, delivering 65 defense, 5 absorption, and 4 max sockets.
sim-full-plate.flavor: Complete harness of overlapping iron plates built to shrug off heavy arbalest bolts and stone-brute swings. Wearing it demands iron stamina, rewarded by four sockets for serious protection.

sim-sacred-armor.summary: Colossal tier-5 socketed base armor from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 50 Body, providing 120 defense, 8 absorption, and 4 sockets.
sim-sacred-armor.flavor: Monumental caldera-forged plate stamped with First-Dynasty bastion seals and lined with heatproof mineral cloth. Only the strongest champions can bear its weight, backed by four sockets for pinnacle defense.

sim-skull-cap.summary: Rounded tier-1 socketed base helm from Act I requiring 10 Body, granting 8 defense, 1 absorption, and 2 max sockets.
sim-skull-cap.flavor: Simple hammered iron bowl worn over a padded wool cap by border levies who wanted something harder than leather on their crown. Two rivets along the brow hold early socketed stones.

sim-great-helm.summary: Flat-topped tier-3 socketed base helm from Acts II–III requiring 25 Body, offering 25 defense, 3 absorption, and 3 max sockets.
sim-great-helm.flavor: Barrel-shaped steel helm enclosing the entire head behind narrow breathing holes and reinforced eye-slits. Heavy and hot inside, it shelters veterans in thick melee and holds three sockets.

sim-tiara.summary: Enchanted tier-4 socketed base helm from Acts III–IV offering 35 defense, 2 absorption, and 3 max sockets with no stat requirement.
sim-tiara.flavor: Slender crescent of salt-tempered silver inlaid with delicate ley-channels that sit weightlessly above the brow. Any class can wear it comfortably, utilizing its three sockets for late-campaign wards.

sim-diadem.summary: Regal tier-5 socketed base helm from Act IV and Hard+ offering 45 defense, 3 absorption, and 3 max sockets with no stat requirement.
sim-diadem.flavor: Wrought from pure star-silver by pre-schism master jewelers, balancing formidable arcane shielding with effortless comfort. Three open sockets make it a coveted endgame prize across every discipline.

sim-buckler.summary: Fist-held tier-1 socketed base shield from Act I requiring 5 Body, providing 5 defense, 1 absorption, and 1 max socket.
sim-buckler.flavor: Small round iron disc gripped by a central bar behind the boss, ideal for punching aside daggers and hatchets in tight alleys. A single socket in the center holds an early gem or rune.

sim-small-shield.summary: Banded tier-1 socketed base shield from Act I requiring 10 Body, granting 10 defense, 1 absorption, and 2 max sockets.
sim-small-shield.flavor: Compact ash-wood shield faced with thin iron straps for border scouts and light infantry marching through wet woods. Two neat settings flank the iron boss for simple defensive enhancements.

sim-kite-shield.summary: Elongated tier-2 socketed base shield from Acts I–II requiring 18 Body, offering 18 defense, 2 absorption, and 3 max sockets.
sim-kite-shield.flavor: Curved teardrop shield sheltering shoulder to knee against quill-fiend volleys and canyon hornbows. Three reinforced mounts along the vertical rib accept gems or early shield runewords.

sim-monarch.summary: Heavy tier-5 socketed base shield from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 35 Body, delivering 55 defense, 4 absorption, and 4 sockets.
sim-monarch.flavor: Broad, thick-rimmed caldera steel shield prized by vanguard veterans for turning aside titan blows and volcanic shrapnel. Four open sockets unlock the strongest defensive rune combinations in the realm.

sim-sash.summary: Woven tier-1 base belt from Act I offering 2 defense and 4 potion slots with no sockets or stat requirements.
sim-sash.flavor: Broad strip of coarse border wool wrapped twice around the waist with four stitched loops for early draught phials. Humble as parish homespun, it keeps basic tonics within easy reach in a fight.

sim-light-belt.summary: Supple tier-2 base belt from Acts I–II requiring 10 Body, granting 4 defense and 8 potion slots with no sockets.
sim-light-belt.flavor: Tanned calfskin belt fitted with two tiered rows of leather loops so scouts and regulars can carry eight phials through longer marches. Brass roller-buckles keep it snug without pinching.

sim-belt.summary: Studded tier-3 base belt from Acts II–III requiring 15 Body, offering 8 defense, 1 absorption, and 12 potion slots.
sim-belt.flavor: Thick oxhide girdle reinforced with iron rivets and triple-tiered pouches built for sustained desert and coastal campaigns. Twelve potion slots keep a squad well-supplied during grueling battles.

sim-plated-belt.summary: Armored tier-4 base belt from Acts III–IV requiring 25 Body, providing 14 defense, 1 absorption, and 16 potion slots.
sim-plated-belt.flavor: Overlapping steel plates riveted over heavy harness leather to guard the waist while supporting four full rows of sixteen phials. Harborwatch veterans rely on its capacity during long seawall sieges.

sim-colossus-girdle.summary: Massive tier-5 base belt from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 35 Body, delivering 25 defense, 2 absorption, and 16 potion slots.
sim-colossus-girdle.flavor: Forged from dark caldera ironstone bands buckled thick enough to turn aside low axe sweeps while carrying sixteen flasks. Built for endgame champions marching straight into the volcanic heart.

sim-small-charm.summary: Compact tier-1 base charm from Act I socketed drops and gamble, carried in the pack to bolster a hero.
sim-small-charm.flavor: A thumb-sized river pebble etched with a simple roadside wayshrine mark by northern travelers. Tucked into a belt pouch or satchel, it radiates a faint, steady warmth on wet frontier marches.

sim-large-charm.summary: Medium tier-2 base charm from Acts I–II drops and gamble, offering stronger passive potential in the pack.
sim-large-charm.flavor: A palm-length tablet of carved slate bound in annealed copper wire by Redmarsh surveyors and hedge-scholars. Heavier than a pocket coin, it holds steady protective markings across harsh terrain.

sim-grand-charm.summary: Expansive tier-3 base charm from Acts II–III drops and gamble, prized for carrying potent passive blessings.
sim-grand-charm.flavor: A broad slab of salt-cured bone and inscribed silver plate wrapped in oiled linen to protect its intricate ley-lines. Veterans guard these large relics closely inside their packs throughout late campaigns.

scroll-of-town-portal.summary: Essential tier-1 special scroll from Act I chests and bounties, opening a swift passage back to the nearest hub.
scroll-of-town-portal.flavor: Inscribed with twin anchor-glyphs in bright blue ink by Collegium wayfinders so beleaguered patrols can step straight out of a muddy ambush onto dry cobblestones. Every prudent captain keeps a spare rolled in oilskin.

scroll-of-identification.summary: Practical tier-1 special scroll from Act I chests and bounties, revealing the hidden properties of unidentified gear.
scroll-of-identification.flavor: Dusted with fine ground quartz and gall-ink that flares briefly when pressed against unfamiliar steel or wards, exposing every hidden maker's mark and curse. Quartermasters never trust loot until the scroll has spoken.

identification-scroll.summary: Standard tier-1 special scroll from Act I chests and bounties, unveiling the true stats of unknown relics.
identification-scroll.flavor: Issued in bundles by Thornwick's assay clerks so soldiers do not accidentally buckle on cursed or brittle salvage in the dark. One quick pass over a mystery blade reads its temper plain as daylight.

greater-healing-potion.summary: Restorative tier-3 special potion from Acts II–III chests and bounties, rapidly mending severe battlefield wounds.
greater-healing-potion.flavor: Brewed in heavy green glass phials using concentrated alpine willow-bark, clean cistern water, and bitter Redmarsh salts. One deep swallow pulls battered frontliners back from collapse during prolonged assaults.

greater-mana-potion.summary: Energizing tier-3 special potion from Acts II–III chests and bounties, restoring deep reserves of arcane mana.
greater-mana-potion.flavor: Distilled over charged plateau crystal and stoppered with waxed cork so the faint blue luminescence never fades in saddlebags. Senior casters rely on these flasks to sustain heavy volleys without pausing.

chipped-ruby.summary: Tier-1 special gem from Act I chests and cube upgrades, offering entry-level fiery power for socketed gear.
chipped-ruby.flavor: Rough crimson splinters pried from river-gravel and old smelter slag along the northern border. Flawed and cloudy, a chipped ruby still lends a welcome spark of hearth-heat when set into cheap iron.

flawed-ruby.summary: Tier-2 special gem from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, providing improved fiery potency for sockets.
flawed-ruby.flavor: Dull red stones fractured by hairline veins yet warm to the thumb even in freezing drizzle. Border jewelers trade them for silver pennies to give caravan blades a sharper thermal bite.

ruby.summary: Tier-3 special gem from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, delivering solid fiery strength when socketed.
ruby.flavor: Cleanly faceted crimson corundum polished in Oakhaven workshops before the evacuation stripped the lapidary benches. Mounted in steel or armor, it radiates steady heat against cold spray and marsh chill.

flawless-ruby.summary: Tier-4 special gem from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, granting high fiery power for late-act gear.
flawless-ruby.flavor: Deep pigeon-blood stone harvested near the volcanic foothills where subterranean heat cooks out every cloudy streak. Smiths handle them with iron tongs, respecting the fierce warmth trapped inside.

perfect-ruby.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 special gem from Act IV and Hard+ chests, offering maximum fiery potency for endgame sockets.
perfect-ruby.flavor: Cut with exacting symmetry so internal light burns like a trapped caldera coal without ever scorching its setting. Veterans mount perfect rubies into their finest steel before marching on the Threshold.

chipped-sapphire.summary: Tier-1 special gem from Act I chests and cube upgrades, bringing light winter chill to early socketed items.
chipped-sapphire.flavor: Pale blue pebbles washed down from northern mountain creeks and gathered by sharp-eyed ferrymen at low water. Even a tiny chip keeps a canteen cool and adds a nip of frost to a recruit's blade.

flawed-sapphire.summary: Tier-2 special gem from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, offering stronger cold potency for socketed gear.
flawed-sapphire.flavor: Clouded azure crystals traded south along the salt roads, prized by Redmarsh guards for taking the sting out of blistering noon glare. Set into a hilt, it coats strikes in brittle river-rime.

sapphire.summary: Tier-3 special gem from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, providing reliable cold power when socketed.
sapphire.flavor: Clear, deep-blue stones cut by coastal guild lapidaries to hold the crisp chill of winter gales over the Western Sea. Frontliners socket them to slow charging beasts and weather desert heat.

flawless-sapphire.summary: Tier-4 special gem from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, granting high cold potency for late-campaign items.
flawless-sapphire.flavor: Cold as glacier meltwater and free of mineral flaws, these stones frost over any damp air within an inch of their facets. Highcrest officers prize them when marching toward the scorching caldera.

perfect-sapphire.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 special gem from Act IV and Hard+ chests, delivering top cold potency for endgame sockets.
perfect-sapphire.flavor: Transmuted to crystal perfection so deep blue light pulses steadily from its core like frozen starlight. Mounted in endgame steel, it locks foes in bitter rime and laughs at volcanic fire.

chipped-topaz.summary: Tier-1 special gem from Act I chests and cube upgrades, adding light static spark to early socketed gear.
chipped-topaz.flavor: Yellowish creek-stones flecked with mica that snap faintly when rubbed against dry wool. Hedge-mages and scouts press them into cheap rings and bow-grips for a modest edge on rainy patrols.

flawed-topaz.summary: Tier-2 special gem from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, offering improved lightning potency for sockets.
flawed-topaz.flavor: Amber-tinted crystals gathered near the Quartz Plateau where dry desert wind charges every loose pebble. Set into iron, a flawed topaz tingles against the palm and sharpens static discharges.

topaz.summary: Tier-3 special gem from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, delivering solid lightning power when socketed.
topaz.flavor: Bright golden stones faceted cleanly to catch coastal storm-light and bleed stray sparks into enemy armor. Storm-channelers and treasure hunters alike keep well-cut topazes tucked in their gear.

flawless-topaz.summary: Tier-4 special gem from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, granting high lightning potency for late-act items.
flawless-topaz.flavor: Clear as bottled sunlight and humming audibly whenever thunderheads build over the harbor cliffs. Veterans socket them into weapons and helms to crack heavy plate with bright arcs.

perfect-topaz.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 special gem from Act IV and Hard+ chests, providing maximum lightning potency for endgame sockets.
perfect-topaz.flavor: Refined through patient cube transmutation until every facet blazes with trapped tempest light. Mounted in pinnacle gear, it unleashes blinding static while guiding its bearer toward rare spoils.

chipped-emerald.summary: Tier-1 special gem from Act I chests and cube upgrades, lending light marsh-venom bite to early socketed gear.
chipped-emerald.flavor: Dull green splinters dug from Fenwick peat-banks and traded by bog-cutters for dry tallow and salt. Crude as broken bottle-glass, a chipped emerald still taints a blade with lingering marsh-rot.

flawed-emerald.summary: Tier-2 special gem from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, offering stronger poison potency for socketed items.
flawed-emerald.flavor: Streaked green crystals steeped in bitter apothecary herbs until they gleam like viper eyes in lantern-light. Poachers and caravan guards favor them for wearing down tough hides over long skirmishes.

emerald.summary: Tier-3 special gem from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, providing solid poison power when socketed.
emerald.flavor: Rich forest-green stones cut with clean bevels by Oakhaven jewelers before the siege closed the trade lanes. Set into arrows or blades, an emerald delivers biting venom that saps enemy stamina.

flawless-emerald.summary: Tier-4 special gem from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, granting high poison potency for late-campaign gear.
flawless-emerald.flavor: Deep, unclouded green gems that smell faintly of crushed wormwood and sea-kelp when warmed in the hand. Marksmen and scouts socket them into endgame bows to drop armored targets swiftly.

perfect-emerald.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 special gem from Act IV and Hard+ chests, delivering top poison potency for endgame sockets.
perfect-emerald.flavor: Transmuted to jewel-like clarity, radiating a cold green sheen that turns steel edges lethal at the slightest scratch. High-tier hunters prize perfect emeralds above gold crowns on the frontier.

chipped-skull.summary: Tier-1 special socketable from Act I chests and cube upgrades, bringing grim early vitality drain to gear.
chipped-skull.flavor: A yellowed fragment of carved bone etched with lower-parish probate tallies and bound in tarnished wire. Lower-parish clerks press these grim chips into wands and rings to siphon vigor from fallen foes.

flawed-skull.summary: Tier-2 special socketable from Acts I–II chests and cube upgrades, offering stronger dark drain for sockets.
flawed-skull.flavor: Cracked and stained dark by bog-tannin, yet inscribed with neat Third-Dynasty debt clauses along the brow. Necromancers and ruthless mercenaries alike socket them to keep upright in ugly brawls.

skull.summary: Tier-3 special socketable from Acts II–III chests and cube upgrades, providing solid dark drain when socketed.
skull.flavor: Bleached clean in Redmarsh alkali sun and inlaid with thin copper wire by sunken-vault embalmers. Mounted in a hilt or shield, it drinks warmth from enemies while returning thorns to attackers.

flawless-skull.summary: Tier-4 special socketable from Acts III–IV chests and cube upgrades, granting high dark drain for late-act items.
flawless-skull.flavor: Polished smooth as old ivory and stamped with coastal abbey witness-seals across the crown. Senior arbiters and veteran reavers rely on its grim resonance during relentless late-act sieges.

perfect-skull.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 special socketable from Act IV and Hard+ chests, delivering top dark drain for endgame sockets.
perfect-skull.flavor: Fused through transmutation into dense, gleaming bone-stone that hums with cold mortuary authority. Set into endgame steel, it turns every landed blow into stolen life and mana.

rejuvenation-potion.summary: Versatile tier-2 special potion from Acts I–II chests and bounties, restoring both health and mana at once.
rejuvenation-potion.flavor: A swirling purple blend of willow-bark draught and charged quartz distillate stoppered in heavy belt glass. Border veterans save these phials for desperate ambushes when body and mind falter together.

full-rejuvenation-potion.summary: Potent tier-4 special potion from Acts III–IV chests and bounties, instantly replenishing health and mana.
full-rejuvenation-potion.flavor: Refined in Collegium field-stills from alpine herbs, star-silver filings, and pure cistern water. One fiery gulp pulls a champion straight back from the brink in the thick of endgame combat.

base-bog-iron-spatha.summary: Broad tier-1 Warrior base weapon from Act I racks and elite drops, ready for smithy upgrades.
base-bog-iron-spatha.flavor: Smelted from impure bog-ore dredged out of Fenwick ditches and hammered wide to compensate for soft northern metal. Thornwick militia carry these heavy blades on river patrols, knowing a crude edge still beats bare knuckles.

base-wardens-arming-blade.summary: Balanced tier-2 Warrior base weapon found in Acts I and II, built as a reliable chassis for smithing.
base-wardens-arming-blade.flavor: Standard sidearm issued to watch-officers along the Alder crossings before the Salt Tithe emptied the garrison racks. Its plain iron crossguard and cord-wrapped grip favor steady parries over flashy southern fencing.

base-salt-tempered-falchion.summary: Curved tier-3 Warrior base weapon dropping in Acts II and III, prized for heavy smithy upgrades.
base-salt-tempered-falchion.flavor: Quenched in Redmarsh brine and honed to a nose-heavy chopping edge that shears cleanly through dry hides and cane shields. Caravan captains favor falchions in canyon ambushes where tight rocks leave no room for long thrusts.

base-harbor-guard-estoc.summary: Piercing tier-4 Warrior base weapon from Acts III and IV, suited for high-tier smithy refinement.
base-harbor-guard-estoc.flavor: Forged with a stiff, diamond-section blade designed to punch between the riveted plates of marine armor on narrow piers. Harborwatch sentries carry them alongside heavy kite shields when holding stone seawalls against boarders.

base-cinder-vein-greatsword.summary: Endgame tier-5 Warrior base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, ready for pinnacle smithy work.
base-cinder-vein-greatsword.flavor: Streaked with dark volcanic glass that refuses to soften even when swung beside open caldera fissures. Foundry masters at Ironcamp reserve these massive blanks for veterans marching straight toward the Threshold gates.

base-peat-cleaver-hatchet.summary: Rugged tier-1 Warrior base weapon from Act I racks and drops, serving as a starter chopping base.
base-peat-cleaver-hatchet.flavor: Originally meant for splitting dry turf blocks and kindling behind northern cottages before raiders forced farmers into levy lines. Its thick iron poll doubles nicely for hammering tent pegs or denting gnoll bucklers.

base-ford-picket-francisca.summary: Weighted tier-2 Warrior base weapon from Acts I and II, built for close brawls and smithy upgrades.
base-ford-picket-francisca.flavor: Shaped with a forward-swept beard so river-watch troops can hook an enemy shield rim before driving home a follow-up cut. Many bear stamped toll-tower marks from the days when Alder crossings still paid regular wages.

base-quarry-splitting-axe.summary: Heavy tier-3 Warrior base weapon found in Acts II and III, ideal for smithing armor-breaking gear.
base-quarry-splitting-axe.flavor: Adapted from the long-handled iron wedges used to cleave black basalt along the Deep Quarry terraces. Escaped miners discovered that anything capable of splitting bedrock makes short work of an overseer's riveted mail.

base-reaver-lochaber-axe.summary: Long-hafted tier-4 Warrior base weapon from Acts III and IV, offering strong potential at the smithy.
base-reaver-lochaber-axe.flavor: Fitted with a hooked back-spike for dragging armored raiders off cliff ledges and narrow harbor gangplanks. Mercenary companies along the Iron Coast prize its reach when holding chokepoints against charging brutes.

base-caldera-jaw-greataxe.summary: Massive tier-5 Warrior base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithy upgrades.
base-caldera-jaw-greataxe.flavor: Cast with jagged, tooth-like notches along the beard that catch enemy blades and wrench them from tired hands. Smelted in Ironcamp's hottest slag-pits, it demands broad shoulders and an unyielding stance in the ash.

base-ash-knobbed-bludgeon.summary: Crude tier-1 Warrior base weapon from Act I drops and racks, offering a simple early crushing base.
base-ash-knobbed-bludgeon.flavor: Turned from a knotty northern ash sapling with its root-ball left intact and bound in scrap hoop-iron. Levy sergeants hand them out when swords run short, reminding recruits that a heavy club never needs sharpening.

base-bailiffs-iron-truncheon.summary: Solid tier-2 Warrior base weapon from Acts I and II, suitable for upgrading into sturdier maces.
base-bailiffs-iron-truncheon.flavor: Carried by Salt-Tithe enforcers to persuade reluctant farmers and debtors without spilling blood on clean ledgers. After the northern garrisons fractured, border troops claimed dozens of them for cracking flintback shells.

base-salt-crusted-pernach.summary: Flanged tier-3 Warrior base weapon dropping in Acts II and III, ready for mid-campaign smithing.
base-salt-crusted-pernach.flavor: Six blunt iron blades welded around a brine-pitted shaft let this mace bite into layered hides without glancing off. Redmarsh caravan guards grease the grip with mutton tallow to keep alkali dust from chafing their palms.

base-foundry-sledge-mace.summary: Brutal tier-4 Warrior base weapon from Acts III and IV, built for heavy smithy reinforcement.
base-foundry-sledge-mace.flavor: Borrowed straight from coastal shipwright yards where heavy iron mauls drive oak treenails into caravel keels. Swung in anger on a narrow pier, it caves in helmets and splinters tower shields with a single dull thud.

base-ember-crown-bec.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 Warrior base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, prized for endgame smithy craft.
base-ember-crown-bec.flavor: Crowned with a curved, armor-piercing fluke forged from meteoric ironstone in the highland foundries. Veterans marching into the caldera rely on its concentrated point to punch clean through dread-knight pauldrons.

base-alder-limb-flatbow.summary: Simple tier-1 Archer base weapon from Act I racks and drops, serving as a light early bow chassis.
base-alder-limb-flatbow.flavor: Shaved from straight-grained river alder by village fletchers who had to make do after yew staves were requisitioned south. It shoots cleanly at short range across wet ditches, provided the archer keeps the string dry.

base-fen-reed-longbow.summary: Tall tier-2 Archer base weapon found in Acts I and II, offering a dependable base for smithy upgrades.
base-fen-reed-longbow.flavor: Backed with braided marsh-reed fiber and rubbed dark with walnut hulls so the wood never glints in misty thickets. Greywood poachers favor its long draw for picking off targets quietly across foggy peat-cuttings.

base-salt-backed-horn-bow.summary: Composite tier-3 Archer base weapon from Acts II and III, suited for mid-game smithy enhancement.
base-salt-backed-horn-bow.flavor: Laminated with strips of bleached desert ram-horn that snap back briskly in Redmarsh's dry thermal winds. Compact enough to draw behind low canyon boulders, it delivers sharp punch against armored caravan raiders.

base-cliff-gale-selfbow.summary: Resilient tier-4 Archer base weapon from Acts III and IV, built to withstand harsh coastal smithing.
base-cliff-gale-selfbow.flavor: Carved from a single stave of salt-seasoned cliff yew that bends without cracking under howling Western Sea squalls. Oakhaven seawall marksmen oil the limbs weekly with whale fat to keep spray from swelling the grain.

base-ash-spire-warbow.summary: Supreme tier-5 Archer base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, ready for pinnacle smithy upgrades.
base-ash-spire-warbow.flavor: Reinforced with star-iron nocks and heat-cured sinew so volcanic updrafts never slacken its heavy draw weight. Only seasoned highland bowmen possess the back strength to loose full volleys from its stiff stave.

base-latched-poacher-prod.summary: Light tier-1 Archer base weapon from Act I racks and elite drops, offering a basic crossbow base.
base-latched-poacher-prod.flavor: Cobbled together from seasoned ash stocks and salvaged wagon-spring steel by northern hunters who preferred crouching in brush to drawing longbows. Its simple wooden latch clicks softly enough not to startle river game.

base-bridge-watch-latchet.summary: Sturdy tier-2 Archer base weapon found in Acts I and II, designed for steady smithy improvements.
base-bridge-watch-latchet.flavor: Issued to toll-tower sentries who needed a weapon that could stay spanned on a stone parapet through hours of cold drizzle. Short iron bolts loosed from its groove discourage bandits from testing river barricades.

base-salt-bed-gastraphetes.summary: Belly-braced tier-3 Archer base weapon from Acts II and III, built as a powerful crossbow chassis for smiths.
base-salt-bed-gastraphetes.flavor: Built with a curved belly-rest so a marksman can brace the stock against his ribs and span the stiff composite prod with both hands. Redmarsh outpost guards favor it for driving hornbow snipers off canyon ledges.

base-cranequin-sea-arbalest.summary: Geared tier-4 Archer base weapon from Acts III and IV, prized for high-tier smithy refinement.
base-cranequin-sea-arbalest.flavor: Wound by a detachable iron rack-and-pinion crank copied from Harborwatch's heavy harborwall artillery. Slow to reload on a pitching deck, it drives thick steel quarrels clean through boarding shields at sixty paces.

base-slag-spring-repeater.summary: Advanced tier-5 Archer base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithy upgrades.
base-slag-spring-repeater.flavor: Topped with a slotted ironwood magazine that drops fresh bolts onto the track with every pull of the lever. Ironcamp artificers tempered the spring in volcanic ash so it snaps reliably amid choking caldera grit.

base-charred-birch-twig.summary: Humble tier-1 Mage base weapon from Act I racks and drops, serving as a basic starter wand chassis.
base-charred-birch-twig.flavor: Snapped from a lightning-scorched silver birch beside a northern wayshrine and whittled smooth at the grip. Hedge-apprentices rely on these plain twigs to focus their first sparks without singeing their fingers.

base-tallied-bone-pointer.summary: Notched tier-2 Necromancer base weapon from Acts I and II, ready for dark smithy enhancements.
base-tallied-bone-pointer.flavor: Filed from a bleached ox-rib and scored with neat probate tally-marks by lower-parish clerks auditing pauper graves. Tapping a coffin lid with its pointed tip calls overdue debtors back into reluctant service.

base-brine-etched-spire-rod.summary: Etched tier-3 Mage base weapon found in Acts II and III, built for mid-game arcane smithing.
