base-brine-etched-spire-rod.flavor: Soaked in concentrated Redmarsh salt-brine after engraving so pale crystalline veins trace every ley-channel along the shaft. Field arcanists prize its crisp conduction when casting across dry, static-heavy flats.

base-gravetide-ash-baton.summary: Weathered tier-4 Necromancer base weapon from Acts III and IV, suited for advanced smithy upgrades.
base-gravetide-ash-baton.flavor: Lathed from grey driftwood hauled out of flooded coastal crypts where sea-salt preserves bone and timber alike. Abbey oath-keepers carry these batons to steady restless spirits and reinforce skeletal ranks.

base-threshold-key-scepter.summary: Exalted tier-5 Mage base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, designed for pinnacle smithy craft.
base-threshold-key-scepter.flavor: Capstoned with a notched ward-bit modeled after the ancient tectonic locks beneath the Obsidian Caldera. Senior archons wield these scepters at the front, channeling fierce ley-currents without wavering.

base-driftwood-crook-staff.summary: Crooked tier-1 Mage base weapon from Act I racks and elite drops, offering a simple early staff base.
base-driftwood-crook-staff.flavor: Fished from an Alder River logjam and cured beside a tavern hearth until light enough for long muddy marches. Country tutors lean on the hooked top when crossing slick stones and use it to trace basic ward-circles.

base-surveyors-plumb-staff.summary: Graduated tier-2 Mage base weapon from Acts I and II, built as a practical base for smithy upgrades.
base-surveyors-plumb-staff.flavor: Marked in brass-inlaid inches and fitted with a hanging lead bob so border geomancers could measure ditch-grades and ley-drift on the march. In a pinch, the copper-shod tip channels sharp arcane bolts cleanly.

base-fen-abbey-crosier.summary: Hooked tier-3 Necromancer base weapon from Acts II and III, ready for mid-campaign smithing.
base-fen-abbey-crosier.flavor: Borne by parish arbiters who walked the mist-choked causeways tallying drowned travelers and unpaid estate liens. Its tarnished bronze crook anchors binding runes that keep raised servants steady under fire.

base-galvanic-coil-stave.summary: Copper-wound tier-4 Mage base weapon from Acts III and IV, prized for high-tier smithy refinement.
base-galvanic-coil-stave.flavor: Wrapped from ferrule to crown in heavy annealed copper coils that hum audibly whenever storm-clouds gather over the coast. Collegium fellows use them to bleed excess charge harmlessly into the flagstones.

base-pyre-warden-pillar.summary: Imposing tier-5 Necromancer base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithing.
base-pyre-warden-pillar.flavor: Hoop-bound ironwood blackened over caldera vents until the grain hardened like slate against volcanic heat. Marching into the inner redoubts, dark-art masters plant its heavy butt in the ash to anchor their legions.

base-rust-pitted-seax.summary: Short tier-1 Archer base weapon from Act I racks and drops, serving as a humble early blade chassis.
base-rust-pitted-seax.flavor: Single-edged frontier utility knife worn horizontal across the lower back by Thornwick scouts and ditch-cutters. Pitted by river damp and whetted on creek stones, it handles camp chores and close ambushes alike.

base-cobblers-awl-blade.summary: Slender tier-2 Archer base weapon found in Acts I and II, suited for light smithy enhancements.
base-cobblers-awl-blade.flavor: Ground down from a broken harness-maker's piercing iron and fitted with a waxed horn handle for a non-slip grip. Scouts prize its narrow triangular point for slipping quietly between leather laces and mail links.

base-salt-flat-stiletto.summary: Needle-pointed tier-3 Archer base weapon from Acts II and III, ready for mid-game smithing.
base-salt-flat-stiletto.flavor: Tempered in Redmarsh brine until the slender steel turned dull grey and refused to glint under the white desert sun. Canyon raiders carry them tucked inside their boots for silent strikes when bows are too slow.

base-harbor-pilots-dirk.summary: Serrated tier-4 Archer base weapon from Acts III and IV, built for high-tier smithy upgrades.
base-harbor-pilots-dirk.flavor: Notched along the spine for sawing through fouled hemp rigging and wet anchor-lines during coastal boarding fights. Oakhaven pilots wear them on greased baldric straps so salt spray never locks the blade in its sheath.

base-cinder-glass-kriss.summary: Wavy-bladed tier-5 Necromancer base weapon from Act IV and Hard+ drops, ready for endgame smithing.
base-cinder-glass-kriss.flavor: Knapped from dark volcanic glass and set into a meteoric-iron hilt etched with Third-Dynasty foreclosure seals. Every cut leaves a jagged, weeping wound that feeds dark rituals in the gloom of the caldera.

base-boiled-hide-coif.summary: Supple tier-1 Archer base helmet from Act I racks and drops, offering a light starter headpiece.
base-boiled-hide-coif.flavor: Shaped over a wooden block in hot tallow and beeswax until the cowhide stiffened enough to turn aside glancing briars and sleet. Northern scouts favor its snug fit because it never rattles against a bowstring.

base-hemp-padded-arming-cap.summary: Quilted tier-1 Warrior base helmet from Act I racks and drops, providing basic early head padding.
base-hemp-padded-arming-cap.flavor: Stuffed with raw hemp tow and stitched in tight vertical channels by Thornwick tailors to cushion recruits against clubs and falling branches. Cheap and washable, it serves as the first defense for border levies.

base-riveted-nasal-spangen.summary: Banded tier-2 Warrior base helmet found in Acts I and II, ready for sturdy smithy upgrades.
base-riveted-nasal-spangen.flavor: Assembled from four curved iron plates joined by riveted bands and a blunt nose-guard that shields the bridge of the face. Border smiths favor this pattern because any village anvil can hammer out a replacement plate.

base-peat-dyed-trapper-hood.summary: Camouflaged tier-2 Archer base helmet from Acts I and II, built as a practical scouting chassis.
base-peat-dyed-trapper-hood.flavor: Boiled in dark bog-water and alder bark until the heavy wool matched the exact dull brown of wet Fenwick sedge. Pulling the deep cowl forward hides a hunter's pale face from watchtowers and pack beasts alike.

base-brimstone-chapel-de-fer.summary: Wide-brimmed tier-3 Warrior base helmet from Acts II and III, suited for mid-campaign smithing.
base-brimstone-chapel-de-fer.flavor: Hammered with a broad, sloping brim that sheds desert sun, canyon rockfall, and hot pitch-splashes alike without blocking peripheral sight. Redmarsh caravan sergeants swear by its airy comfort on blistering marches.

base-assayers-copper-circlet.summary: Conductive tier-3 Mage base helmet found in Acts II and III, ready for arcane smithy refinement.
base-assayers-copper-circlet.flavor: Hammered from pure annealed copper and stamped with Border Mint calibration marks along the inner brow. Field arcanists wear it to ground stray static while measuring heat and ley-strain across unstable ruins.

base-sea-wall-sallet.summary: Sloped tier-4 Warrior base helmet from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier smithy upgrades.
base-sea-wall-sallet.flavor: Drawn with a sweeping rear tail that protects the neck from downward boarding axes and plunging coastal arbalest bolts. Harborwatch marines polish the steel with whale oil so salt spray beads off cleanly.

base-ossuary-scribe-miter.summary: Mitered tier-4 Necromancer base helmet from Acts III and IV, built for advanced dark-art smithing.
base-ossuary-scribe-miter.flavor: Stiffened with salted linen and lined with lead-foil inscriptions copied from coastal abbey probate rolls. Senior oath-keepers wear these austere caps when presiding over haunted vaults and restless dead.

base-caldera-forged-armet.summary: Enclosed tier-5 Warrior base helmet from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithy work.
base-caldera-forged-armet.flavor: Sealed with a hinged visor and reinforced gorget-rim hammered from dark volcanic steel in Ironcamp's hottest sheds. Inside its narrow sight-slits, vanguard veterans march unblinking through blinding cinder-snow.

base-crown-ember-coronet.summary: Radiant tier-5 Mage base helmet from Act IV and Hard+ drops, ready for pinnacle smithy craft.
base-crown-ember-coronet.flavor: Wrought from star-iron and set with tiny, glowing caldera cinders caged in pale silver wire above the brow. Senior archons wear it into the Threshold chambers to steady their focus against overwhelming heat.

base-patched-canvas-doublet.summary: Worn tier-1 Archer base chest armor from Act I racks and drops, serving as a light early coat.
base-patched-canvas-doublet.flavor: Stitched from heavy sailcloth scraps and reinforced at the shoulders with old saddle-leather by thrifty border hunters. Repeated patching makes it stiff as board, yet it turns aside thorns and light arrows well enough.

base-mortuary-linen-tunic.summary: Drab tier-1 Necromancer base chest armor from Act I drops and racks, offering a basic early robe.
base-mortuary-linen-tunic.flavor: Cut from coarse, unbleached parish shroud-linen and belted with rough hemp cord for clerks working damp crypt-rows. Pockets sewn along the lining hold chalk stubs, tallow ends, and stamped bone tallies.

base-fen-scale-hauberk.summary: Overlapping tier-2 Warrior base chest armor from Acts I and II, ready for sturdy smithy upgrades.
base-fen-scale-hauberk.flavor: Small, tongue-shaped iron scales laced onto greased deerhide so river-mud washes off easily after bog patrols. Thornwick armorers favor scale coats because a trooper can replace a bent plate beside a campfire.

base-salt-cured-jerkin.summary: Tough tier-2 Archer base chest armor found in Acts I and II, built for agile smithy refinement.
base-salt-cured-jerkin.flavor: Steeped in Redmarsh brine and dried in hot desert wind until the oxhide hardened without losing its supple flex. Caravan scouts rely on it to shrug off brush-thorns, viper strikes, and blowing alkali grit.

base-redmarsh-lamellar-coat.summary: Laced tier-3 Warrior base chest armor from Acts II and III, suited for mid-campaign smithing.
base-redmarsh-lamellar-coat.flavor: Rows of narrow ironstone plates laced together with rawhide thongs so heat vents freely between the overlapping bands. Desert regulars prize lamellar over solid breastplates that bake the wearer under noon glare.

base-wardstone-scholar-coat.summary: Insulated tier-3 Mage base chest armor from Acts II and III, ready for arcane smithy upgrades.
base-wardstone-scholar-coat.flavor: Lined with braided copper filaments and oiled wool to shield traveling Collegium fellows from plateau static storms. Deep inner pockets keep chalk-slates and quartz prisms dry through dust and sudden squalls.

base-oakhaven-plate-cuirass.summary: Fluted tier-4 Warrior base chest armor from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier smithing.
base-oakhaven-plate-cuirass.flavor: Hammered in Oakhaven's naval yards from salt-tempered steel shaped to deflect heavy boarding pikes and canyon crossfire. Every strap is double-riveted with brass so seawater never rots the harness mid-campaign.

base-scriptorium-funeral-pall.summary: Somber tier-4 Necromancer base chest armor from Acts III and IV, built for late-game dark craft.
base-scriptorium-funeral-pall.flavor: Tailored from dark, bitumen-treated wool embroidered with silent probate vows along the wide sleeves and hem. Coastal arbiters wear these solemn vestments when binding restless spirits in flooded sea-vaults.

base-obsidian-bastion-plate.summary: Colossal tier-5 Warrior base chest armor from Act IV and Hard+ drops, ready for pinnacle smithing.
base-obsidian-bastion-plate.flavor: Layered with thick caldera ironstone plates quenched in volcanic ash until the steel turned dark as cooled lava. Sealed inside this harness, vanguard champions endure blows that flatten ordinary fortifications.

base-leyline-conduit-vestment.summary: Channeling tier-5 Mage base chest armor from Act IV and Hard+ drops, prized for endgame smiths.
base-leyline-conduit-vestment.flavor: Woven with star-silver thread traced into intricate Collegium ley-circuits across the chest and shoulders. Senior archons rely on its disciplined weave to sustain relentless barrages inside the Obsidian Caldera.

base-split-rawhide-mitts.summary: Coarse tier-1 Warrior base gloves from Act I racks and drops, offering basic early hand protection.
base-split-rawhide-mitts.flavor: Sliced from thick, unsplit oxhide with separate thumb-stalls so northern levies can grip heavy pikes and axes in freezing drizzle. Crude stitching rubs the knuckles raw at first, yet they keep frostbite out of the fingers.

base-ink-stained-fingerless.summary: Open-tipped tier-1 Necromancer base gloves from Act I drops and racks, suited for early scroll work.
base-ink-stained-fingerless.flavor: Woolen half-gloves stained permanently black at the cuffs from dipping iron nibs into oak-gall inkwells. Lower-parish clerks wear them in drafty crypts to keep their palms warm while leaving fingertips free to turn pages.

base-greased-archers-tab-gloves.summary: Reinforced tier-2 Archer base gloves from Acts I and II, built for steady smithy enhancements.
base-greased-archers-tab-gloves.flavor: Patched with thick, tallow-rubbed leather pads across the drawing fingers so heavy bowstrings release cleanly without blistering. Border bowmen guard them closely, knowing a split finger ends a marksman's usefulness.

base-riveted-scale-cuffs.summary: Plated tier-2 Warrior base gloves from Acts I and II, ready for sturdy mid-early smithy upgrades.
base-riveted-scale-cuffs.flavor: Overlapping iron scales tacked onto stiffened wrist-guards to turn aside sliding blades during close shield-wall brawls. Thornwick smiths rivet them loose enough for a trooper to clench a sword-hilt without cramping.

base-alkali-proof-gauntlets.summary: Sealed tier-3 Warrior base gloves from Acts II and III, suited for harsh desert smithy upgrades.
base-alkali-proof-gauntlets.flavor: Cured in boiled vinegar and mineral pitch so caustic Redmarsh brine cannot eat through the stitching or stiffen the fingers. Caravan veterans wear them when hauling iron chains and clearing alkali ditches.

base-copper-sewn-conduit-gloves.summary: Grounded tier-3 Mage base gloves found in Acts II and III, built for arcane smithy refinement.
base-copper-sewn-conduit-gloves.flavor: Stitched along every finger-seam with fine annealed copper wire that channels stray sparks safely down the sleeve. Plateau arcanists rely on them when handling fractured quartz wardstones during static gales.

base-harbor-riggers-grips.summary: Tarred tier-4 Archer base gloves from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier smithy upgrades.
base-harbor-riggers-grips.flavor: Roughened with pine rosin and salt-cured sharkskin palms so wet halyards, boarding hooks, and heavy arbalest stocks never slip. Oakhaven seawall crews wear them through winter squalls without losing their hold.

base-bone-knuckle-grips.summary: Bone-studded tier-4 Necromancer base gloves from Acts III and IV, ready for late-game dark craft.
base-bone-knuckle-grips.flavor: Studded with polished finger-bones wired onto dark abbey leather, clacking softly whenever the wearer traces binding sigils. Coastal necro-arbiters use them to anchor stubborn spirits in flooded reliquaries.

base-slag-forged-crushers.summary: Crushing tier-5 Warrior base gloves from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithy work.
base-slag-forged-crushers.flavor: Articulated steel gauntlets quenched in caldera slag until the knuckles hardened like anvil faces. Vanguard breachers wear them to grip scorching greatsword hilts and batter down iron-bound fortress gates.

base-ember-weave-handwraps.summary: Heatproof tier-5 Mage base gloves from Act IV and Hard+ drops, prized for pinnacle smithy craft.
base-ember-weave-handwraps.flavor: Spun from pale mineral fiber and star-silver thread that refuses to scorch even while channeling raw volcanic fire. Senior hearth-archons wrap them tight before stepping into the roaring heat of the caldera.

base-bog-clogged-clogs.summary: Thick-soled tier-1 Warrior base boots from Act I racks and drops, offering basic early footwear.
base-bog-clogged-clogs.flavor: Hollowed from seasoned alder blocks with nailed leather uppers so northern levies can stand watch in ankle-deep ditch water without rotting their feet. Clumsy on rocky hills, they keep mud out better than thin shoes.

base-tallow-rubbed-buskins.summary: Greased tier-1 Archer base boots from Act I racks and drops, built for quiet early trail movement.
base-tallow-rubbed-buskins.flavor: Ankle-high calfskin boots greased thick with mutton fat to shed morning dew and river drizzle on early patrols. Fenwick poachers lace them snug around the shin so wet brush never catches on loose flaps.

base-hobnailed-ford-boots.summary: Studded tier-2 Warrior base boots found in Acts I and II, ready for sturdy smithy enhancements.
base-hobnailed-ford-boots.flavor: Driven full of broad-headed iron nails across the soles to grip mossy river boulders and slick timber bridge planks. Alder picket veterans swear a hobnailed boot holds firm even when a shield-wall shoves back.

base-fen-stalker-moccasins.summary: Broad-soled tier-2 Archer base boots from Acts I and II, suited for agile smithy improvements.
base-fen-stalker-moccasins.flavor: Stitched without heavy heels from oiled deerhide so scouts distribute their weight evenly across soft peat and wet reeds. Greywood trackers use them to slip past patrol routes without leaving deep prints.

base-salt-crust-waders.summary: Brine-proof tier-3 Archer base boots from Acts II and III, built for mid-campaign smithy work.
base-salt-crust-waders.flavor: Knee-high boots cured in vinegar and mineral pitch to keep caustic alkali brine from eating through the seams. Redmarsh outriders wear them across salt-pans and tidal flats where ordinary leather cracks in days.

base-plated-sabaton-boots.summary: Armored tier-3 Warrior base boots found in Acts II and III, ready for heavy smithy upgrades.
base-plated-sabaton-boots.flavor: Overlapping steel lames riveted over thick hobnailed leather to protect the instep from falling stones and low axe sweeps. Caravan regulars march steadily in them across jagged canyon scree without bruising.

base-cliff-grip-greaves.summary: Hook-toed tier-4 Archer base boots from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier smithy refinement.
base-cliff-grip-greaves.flavor: Armed with iron toe-hooks and roughened cork soles that bite into wet coastal granite and slick ship rigging alike. Oakhaven cliff-runners rely on them when scaling sea-crags in driving spray.

base-crypt-dust-slippers.summary: Silent tier-4 Necromancer base boots from Acts III and IV, built for advanced dark-art smithing.
base-crypt-dust-slippers.flavor: Felt-soled and bound in salted burial linen so coastal abbey clerks can walk flooded stone vaults without waking dormant horrors. Dry crypt-ash clings permanently to the stitched cuffs.

base-molten-tread-sabatons.summary: Ashen tier-5 Warrior base boots from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithy upgrades.
base-molten-tread-sabatons.flavor: Thick caldera-iron soles insulated with layered mineral cloth so vanguard troopers can cross glowing slag fissures without blistering. Heavy as anvils, they anchor a fighter firmly amid volcanic tremors.

base-threshold-step-boots.summary: Star-bound tier-5 Mage base boots from Act IV and Hard+ drops, prized for pinnacle smithy craft.
base-threshold-step-boots.flavor: Embroidered with pale silver ward-lines that hum quietly against hot basalt flagstones, keeping the bearer's stride light and cool. Senior archons wear them across the inner caldera without tiring.

base-hemp-rope-girdle.summary: Knotted tier-1 Necromancer base belt from Act I racks and drops, offering a basic early waist slot.
base-hemp-rope-girdle.flavor: Braided from coarse border hemp and dipped in beeswax so damp crypt-air cannot rot the fibers. Lower-parish clerks loop bone tallies, chalk pouches, and small inkhorns directly onto its sturdy knots.

base-tanned-oxhide-strap.summary: Oxhide tier-1 Warrior base belt from Act I racks and drops, providing a sturdy starter belt chassis.
base-tanned-oxhide-strap.flavor: Cut thick from oak-tanned oxhide with a heavy iron tongue-buckle hammered out in Thornwick's smithy yard. It supports the weight of a sword-scabbard and ration pouch without stretching in wet weather.

base-toll-collectors-pouch-belt.summary: Compartmented tier-2 Archer base belt from Acts I and II, ready for practical smithy upgrades.
base-toll-collectors-pouch-belt.flavor: Rigged with four buttoned leather pockets originally designed for sorting silver florins, copper slugs, and stamped bridge chits. Border archers discovered the pouches hold spare arrowheads and bow-wax just as neatly.

base-iron-studded-war-sash.summary: Kidney-braced tier-2 Warrior base belt found in Acts I and II, built for durable smithy improvements.
base-iron-studded-war-sash.flavor: Wide boiled-leather kidney belt studded with flat iron discs to protect the lower back during close melee brawls. Veteran pikemen cinch it tight before long marches to keep heavy mail from dragging on the shoulders.

base-salt-caravan-bandolier.summary: Slung tier-3 Archer base belt from Acts II and III, suited for mid-campaign smithy enhancements.
base-salt-caravan-bandolier.flavor: Worn diagonally across the chest with brass-capped loops for phials, spare bowstrings, and quick-draw daggers. Redmarsh outriders rely on its balanced layout when fighting from narrow canyon ledges.

base-assayers-scale-girdle.summary: Calibrated tier-3 Mage base belt found in Acts II and III, ready for arcane smithy refinement.
base-assayers-scale-girdle.flavor: Hung with tiny brass counterweights and copper-wire loops used by Collegium fellows to balance ley-foci in the field. Steady weight around the waist helps casters keep their posture true during long incantations.

base-harbor-masters-cinch.summary: Bronze-clasped tier-4 Warrior base belt from Acts III and IV, engineered for high-tier smithy upgrades.
base-harbor-masters-cinch.flavor: Buckled with a massive cast-bronze anchor clasp that doubles as a counterweight for heavy naval broadswords. Harborwatch officers wear these wide cinches when commanding seawall defenses in howling gales.

base-probate-seal-sash.summary: Inscribed tier-4 Necromancer base belt from Acts III and IV, built for advanced dark-art smithing.
base-probate-seal-sash.flavor: Draped in dark salted wool stamped with leaden Third-Dynasty foreclosure seals along the hanging ends. Coastal arbiters cinch it over their robes when auditing restless vaults and binding undead cohorts.

base-caldera-plate-girdle.summary: Articulated tier-5 Warrior base belt from Act IV and Hard+ drops, forged for endgame smithy work.
base-caldera-plate-girdle.flavor: Overlapping bands of dark caldera steel riveted onto heat-cured drake hide to guard the waist against low sweeps and slag-spray. Vanguard champions buckle it tight before marching into the inner redoubts.

base-ember-core-cincture.summary: Cinder-clasped tier-5 Mage base belt from Act IV and Hard+ drops, prized for pinnacle smithy craft.
base-ember-core-cincture.flavor: Clasped with a caged shard of glowing caldera cinder that radiates steady warmth without scorching the surrounding star-silk. Senior archons rely on its quiet resonance to anchor high-order spells at the Threshold.

spiked-cudgel.summary: Crude tier-1 Warrior mace from Act I requiring 4 Body, delivering consistent 3 damage in early border brawls.
spiked-cudgel.flavor: Turned from a knotty ash fence-post and studded with square horseshoe nails by Thornwick levies short on proper swords. It lacks balance or finesse, yet a solid swing across a gnoll's shield-arm still settles most roadside arguments.

flanged-mace.summary: Riveted tier-2 Warrior mace from Acts I–II requiring 8 Body, dealing 5–6 crushing damage against armored foes.
flanged-mace.flavor: Six iron flanges welded around a stout oak shaft allow this hammer to bite into riveted mail without glancing off. Border sergeants favor it when marching against flintbacks and shielded raiders who laugh at light slashing blades.

heavy-morningstar.summary: Spiked tier-3 Warrior mace from Acts II–III requiring 11 Body, dealing 8–9 damage with a slight accuracy edge.
heavy-morningstar.flavor: Cast with a bristling iron head in Redmarsh's pit-forges for veterans tired of bouncing blades off basalt carapaces. Heavy enough to numb the wielder's wrist after a long shift, it turns shielded formations into dented scrap.

steel-warhammer.summary: Balanced tier-4 Warrior mace from Acts III–IV requiring 14 Body, delivering 12–13 impact damage and accuracy.
steel-warhammer.flavor: Forged with a flat crushing face and a curved rear beak for punching cleanly through Oakhaven and Iron Pact plate alike. Harborwatch breachers carry them over their shoulders when storming barricaded piers and stone gatehouses.

obsidian-greatmaul.summary: Massive tier-5 Warrior mace from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 17 Body, dealing 16–18 damage with improved accuracy.
obsidian-greatmaul.flavor: Bound with jagged slabs of caldera volcanic glass wedged into a heavy meteoric-iron frame by Ironcamp smiths. Each blow lands with tectonic weight, shattering golem joints and dread-knight pauldrons in a shower of sparks.

flint-stiletto.summary: Slender tier-1 dagger for both classes in Act I requiring 4 Agility, offering 1–2 damage and sharp accuracy.
flint-stiletto.flavor: Knapped from dark grey river-flint and lashed into a greased willow grip by Fenwick poachers who lacked iron coinage. Too fragile for parrying heavy axes, it slips quietly through leather laces when an ambush goes sideways.

steel-rondel.summary: Narrow tier-2 dagger for both classes in Acts I–II requiring 7 Agility, dealing 3–4 damage with high accuracy.
steel-rondel.flavor: Fitted with twin circular iron guards to keep a wet hand from sliding onto the triangular blade during close grappling. Caravan outriders tuck them behind their belts for finishing downed sand raiders in narrow canyon passes.

duelist-poignard.summary: Refined tier-3 dagger for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 10 Agility, delivering 5–7 damage and accuracy.
duelist-poignard.flavor: Tempered in Oakhaven's guild workshops for ship-officers and scouts who fight in cramped companionways where longswords catch on beams. Its stiff spine probes neatly between mail links without bending under pressure.

main-gauche.summary: Parrying tier-4 dagger for both classes in Acts III–IV requiring 13 Agility, dealing 7–10 damage with accuracy.
main-gauche.flavor: Built with a wide knuckle-bow and notched ricasso designed to catch enemy blades and wrench them aside in tight quarters. Coastal marine captains favor its crisp balance when boarding hostile galleys in heavy chop.

shadow-dirk.summary: Lethal tier-5 dagger for both classes from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Agility, dealing 11–14 damage with accuracy.
shadow-dirk.flavor: Acid-etched to a dull slate finish that swallows torchlight and caldera glare alike without casting a single glint. Carried by highland scouts and threshold infiltrators, its needle-fine point finds soft seams in the heaviest dark-iron plate.

two-handed-claymore.summary: Heavy tier-1 Warrior greatsword from Act I requiring 5 Body, sweeping 3–5 damage across early frontier skirmishes.
two-handed-claymore.flavor: Forged with a plain iron crossguard and a long cord-wrapped grip so northern timber-fellers could swing it like a splitting axe. Clumsy in narrow ditches, it still clears breathing room fast when briar-hounds crowd the line.

bastard-greatsword.summary: Versatile tier-2 Warrior greatsword from Acts I–II requiring 9 Body, dealing 6–8 damage on border campaigns.
bastard-greatsword.flavor: Long enough to demand two hands for heavy cleaves yet balanced neatly near the hilt for sustained road marches. Veteran caravan guards strap them across their backs when escorting salt wagons through Redmarsh passes.

flamberge.summary: Flame-bladed tier-3 Warrior greatsword from Acts II–III requiring 12 Body, dealing 9–12 damage with accuracy.
flamberge.flavor: Hammered with undulating wave-edges that send jarring vibrations down an opponent's weapon shaft upon every parry. Field surgeons along the Iron Coast dread treating the ragged, weeping cuts left by a swinging flamberge.

executioner-blade.summary: Broad tier-4 Warrior greatsword from Acts III–IV requiring 15 Body, delivering 13–17 damage and improved accuracy.
executioner-blade.flavor: Squared at the tip and weighted forward so every downward stroke falls with the pitiless authority of a headsman's axe. Originally carried by Southern Crown judicial bailiffs, several ended up in vanguard hands after the retreats.

dreadnought-zweihander.summary: Colossal tier-5 Warrior greatsword from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 18 Body, dealing 18–24 damage with accuracy.
dreadnought-zweihander.flavor: Poured from tempered meteoric steel with wide parrying lugs forged halfway up the ricasso to trap enemy polearms. Only the strongest frontier champions can wield it through an entire caldera siege without faltering.

willow-wand.summary: Supple tier-1 Mage wand from Act I requiring 4 Mind, adding 8 bonus mana to support apprentice spellcasting.
willow-wand.flavor: Peeled from a riverbank willow branch and dried over a smoky tavern hearth until light as a goose quill. Country hedge-mages favor willow because it conducts small sparks easily even when soaked by northern drizzle.

yew-wand.summary: Seasoned tier-2 Mage wand from Acts I–II requiring 7 Mind, expanding maximum mana by 16 for longer skirmishes.
yew-wand.flavor: Turned from dense churchyard yew heartwood and rubbed dark with beeswax and linseed oil. Lower-parish clerks and traveling scholars prize yew wands for holding a steady arcane charge across dry desert marches.

amber-focus-wand.summary: Resin-capped tier-3 Mage wand from Acts II–III requiring 10 Mind, granting 24 bonus mana for mid-campaign battles.
amber-focus-wand.flavor: Capped with a polished lump of bog-amber bound in annealed copper wire to anchor stray ley-currents cleanly. It tingles faintly against the thumb whenever static storms gather over the plateau or coastal cliffs.

crystal-siphon-wand.summary: Faceted tier-4 Mage wand from Acts III–IV requiring 13 Mind, providing 36 bonus mana for sustained spell volleys.
crystal-siphon-wand.flavor: Ground from clear quartz crystals harvested along high alpine seams and mounted in tarnished star-silver fittings. Senior arcanists rely on its crisp channeling to keep defensive wards active amid heavy siege fire.

astral-archon-wand.summary: Masterwork tier-5 Mage wand from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Mind, adding 50 bonus mana for pinnacle sorcery.
astral-archon-wand.flavor: Inlaid with pre-schism star-charts fine enough to require a jeweler's glass to trace cleanly. Wielded by high-order fellows at the Threshold, it draws deep reserves of ambient power straight out of the volcanic gloom.

ash-shortbow.summary: Compact tier-1 bow for both classes in Act I requiring 4 Agility, dealing 1–3 damage with a small accuracy bonus.
ash-shortbow.flavor: Shaped from straight-grained northern ash by Thornwick fletchers who needed cheap, reliable bows for watchtower recruits. Short enough to shoot from behind low brush, it keeps early raiders honest across river ditches.

recurve-bow.summary: Horn-backed tier-2 bow for both classes in Acts I–II requiring 7 Agility, dealing 3–6 damage with improved accuracy.
recurve-bow.flavor: Laminated with boiled ox-horn and sinew so the tips snap forward cleanly without needing a six-foot stave. Caravan outriders favor recurves for shooting swiftly around narrow boulders in Redmarsh canyon ambushes.

composite-war-bow.summary: Stiff tier-3 bow for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 10 Agility, delivering 6–9 damage and solid accuracy.
composite-war-bow.flavor: Built from layered yew, horn, and fish-glue cured in dry coastal sheds to resist warping in salt spray. Stringing it requires bracing the lower limb behind a boot-heel, yet its arrows punch deep into brigandine.

heavy-arbalest.summary: Steel-prodded tier-4 crossbow for both classes in Acts III–IV requiring 13 Agility, dealing 9–14 damage with accuracy.
heavy-arbalest.flavor: Fitted with an iron foot-stirrup and a heavy steel prod originally designed for Oakhaven's granite seawalls. Slow to span in open mud, it looses short iron quarrels capable of cracking basalt armor at long range.

windpiercer-greatbow.summary: Towering tier-5 bow for both classes from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Agility, dealing 12–17 damage with accuracy.
windpiercer-greatbow.flavor: Six feet of seasoned mountain yew reinforced with star-iron nocks to withstand the howling thermal drafts of the caldera. Marksmen who master its brutal draw weight can thread shafts through driving cinder-snow.

steel-kite-shield.summary: Teardrop tier-3 Warrior shield from Acts II–III requiring 11 Body, offering sturdy defense and a slight accuracy edge.
steel-kite-shield.flavor: Tapered toward the base to shelter a trooper's lead leg while leaving the sword-arm clear for clean counter-thrusts. Harborwatch regulars paint their company badges over the iron boss before marching out the gate.

aegis-of-the-citadel.summary: Fortress-grade tier-5 Warrior shield from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 17 Body, adding 30 bonus health for frontliners.
aegis-of-the-citadel.flavor: Hammered from thick caldera-tempered steel with a reinforced brow-lip that deflects falling slag and overhead mauls alike. Carrying it through volcanic ash requires immense stamina, yet nothing breaks a line behind it.

novice-glass-focus.summary: Simple tier-1 Mage off-hand focus from Act I requiring 4 Mind, providing 8 bonus mana for early spellcasting.
novice-glass-focus.flavor: A palm-sized disc of thick green bottle-glass bound in a soldered tin ring so an apprentice can hold it while gesturing. Crude bubbles mar the surface, yet it still gathers enough stray charge for an extra spark.

chiseled-quartz-focus.summary: Ground tier-2 Mage off-hand focus from Acts I–II requiring 7 Mind, expanding maximum mana by 16 on frontier marches.
chiseled-quartz-focus.flavor: Shaped with six flat facets from cloudy desert crystal to steady erratic ley-currents in dry air. Traveling arcanists keep it wrapped in oiled wool inside their satchels so gravel dust does not scratch the faces.

astral-sphere.summary: Orbital tier-3 Mage off-hand focus from Acts II–III requiring 10 Mind, granting 25 bonus mana for mid-campaign play.
astral-sphere.flavor: A smoky glass globe ringed by two pivoted brass hoops that align automatically with local magnetic drift. Coastal navigators and battle-mages alike prize its calm, steady weight when casting through thick sea-fog.

radiant-spell-mirror.summary: Polished tier-4 Mage off-hand focus from Acts III–IV requiring 13 Mind, providing 36 bonus mana for senior casters.
radiant-spell-mirror.flavor: Silvered speculum metal mounted in an engraved bronze frame that catches ambient light even in pitch-dark crypts. Casters angle its face toward incoming hexes to steady their focus and deepen their arcane reserve.

eye-of-the-cosmos.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 Mage off-hand focus from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Mind, adding 50 bonus mana for endgame sorcery.
eye-of-the-cosmos.flavor: Cut from a dark, flawless pre-schism lens that reveals faint threads of ley-fire pulsing beneath volcanic bedrock. Only archons marching into the Threshold possess the mental discipline to bear its constant hum.

steel-basinet.summary: Pointed tier-3 Warrior helm from Acts II–III requiring 10 Body, deflecting overhead blows in sustained engagements.
steel-basinet.flavor: Drawn to a steep conical peak so downward axe-strokes and falling stones glance harmlessly off the shoulders. Oakhaven armorers rivet a quilted leather aventail around the neck to keep cold spray off the collar.

dread-crest-helm.summary: Imposing tier-5 Warrior helm from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Body, granting 25 bonus health for frontline veterans.
dread-crest-helm.flavor: Forged from blackened caldera steel with a ridged central comb built to turn away heavy siege-hammers. Sealed behind its narrow eye-slits, a veteran commander can march straight into sulfur smoke without flinching.

apprentice-circlet.summary: Delicate tier-1 Mage helm from Act I requiring 4 Mind, providing 8 bonus mana to support early arcane studies.
apprentice-circlet.flavor: A simple band of annealed copper hammered thin enough to sit lightly over a damp wool hood without pinching the temples. First-year Collegium students wear them daily to keep stray sparks from singeing their hair.

sage-cowl.summary: Draped tier-3 Mage helm from Acts II–III requiring 9 Mind, adding 16 bonus mana for casters on long campaigns.
sage-cowl.flavor: Tailored from heavy indigo wool lined with silver-stitched linen to shut out howling desert wind and battlefield din. Scholars pull the deep hood forward when reciting complex wards amid choking dust and smoke.

archmage-diadem.summary: Regal tier-5 Mage helm from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Mind, delivering 32 bonus mana for high-order spellcraft.
archmage-diadem.flavor: Wrought from pale star-silver set with a single cold quartz prism that hums cleanly against the brow. Reserved for senior Conclave masters, it steadies thought even at the edge of the roaring volcanic caldera.

stalker-hood.summary: Shadowed tier-3 helm for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 9 Agility, sharpening accuracy in rough terrain.
stalker-hood.flavor: Stitched from oil-darkened rawhide with a stiffened peak that shields a marksman's eyes from midday desert glare and driving rain. Scouts favor its snug fit because loose cloth never snags on low canyon branches.

shadow-mask.summary: Concealing tier-5 helm for both classes from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Agility, adding strong strike accuracy.
shadow-mask.flavor: Cured black leather fitted with smoked-mica eye-slits and a charcoal-filtered mouthguard against sulfur fumes. Highland scouts wear it through blinding cinder-snow, sighting targets cleanly without coughing once.

interlocking-ring-mail.summary: Layered tier-3 Warrior chest armor from Acts II–III requiring 11 Body, built to turn aside heavy slashing attacks.
interlocking-ring-mail.flavor: Heavy flat iron rings woven four-in-one over boiled oxhide so blades cannot wedge between the links. Redmarsh caravan veterans oil the seams with vinegar-tallow to keep alkali dust from grinding the metal thin.

gothic-full-plate.summary: Fluted tier-5 Warrior chest armor from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 17 Body, granting 40 bonus health for elite troops.
gothic-full-plate.flavor: Corrugated steel plates hammered in Ironcamp's hottest yards to channel glancing blows away from vital joints. Sealed inside this harness, a vanguard captain advances like an iron wall through thick volcanic ash.

studded-leather-armor.summary: Studded tier-2 chest armor for both classes in Acts I–II requiring 6 Agility, balancing protection with mobility.
studded-leather-armor.flavor: Thick cowhide reinforced with rows of blunt iron studs that catch sliding dagger-points without adding plate weight. Border outriders and poachers wear it on long patrols where speed matters just as much as ribs.

hardened-brigandine.summary: Plate-lined tier-3 chest armor for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 10 Agility, offering flexible durability.
hardened-brigandine.flavor: Hundreds of small tinned steel plates riveted inside tough coastal canvas dyed dull grey-green. It bends smoothly with the waist when climbing wet cliffs or drawing a heavy warbow while turning away stray arrows.

wyrmscale-cuirass.summary: Scaled tier-5 chest armor for both classes from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Agility, prized for elite protection.
wyrmscale-cuirass.flavor: Overlapping drake scales laced onto supple volcanic-cured leather with braided star-silver wire. Light enough for a scout to sprint across loose basalt scree yet tough enough to turn aside heavy iron halberds.

weaver-robe.summary: Sturdy tier-2 Mage chest armor from Acts I–II requiring 7 Mind, adding 12 bonus mana for traveling spellcasters.
weaver-robe.flavor: Loomed from tight-spun border wool treated with beeswax so freezing river-mist beads off the shoulders instead of soaking in. Traveling arcanists stitch copper-wire charms into the hem to steady their focus daily.

mystic-velvet-mantle.summary: Plush tier-4 Mage chest armor from Acts III–IV requiring 12 Mind, providing 22 bonus mana for late-act encounters.
mystic-velvet-mantle.flavor: Heavy coastal velvet lined with silvered silk that insulates the wearer from biting sea-gales and stray static discharges. Senior fellows wore these mantles while auditing harbor wards before the great evacuation.

steel-greaves.summary: Hinged tier-4 Warrior boots from Acts III–IV requiring 13 Body, guarding shins and ankles in heavy melee combat.
steel-greaves.flavor: Articulated steel shin-guards strapped over thick hobnailed leather boots so low sweeps and snapping beast-jaws find nothing but iron. Harborwatch marines wear them when holding narrow, blood-slick stone seawalls.

juggernaut-war-greaves.summary: Bulwark tier-5 Warrior boots from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Body, adding 25 bonus health for steadfast defenders.
juggernaut-war-greaves.flavor: Reinforced with thick caldera ironstone toe-caps and heavy ankle braces built to anchor a trooper against titan shockwaves. Clanking loudly across basalt flagstones, they refuse to slip in deep ash or molten grit.

tracker-treads.summary: Supple tier-3 boots for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 9 Agility, granting steady footing and slight accuracy.
tracker-treads.flavor: Stitched with roughened rawhide soles that grip wet boardwalks, loose canyon scree, and slippery ship decks alike. Scouts prize their quiet stride when slipping past sand-raider pickets or coastal night watchmen.

windrunner-striders.summary: Feather-light tier-5 boots for both classes from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Agility, adding bonus strike accuracy.
windrunner-striders.flavor: Cured from thin drake-hide and lined with layered felt so highland scouts skim across ash-drifts without making a sound. Even on steep volcanic ridges, their notched soles keep every sudden lunge and shot balanced.

scholar-slippers.summary: Soft tier-2 Mage boots from Acts I–II requiring 6 Mind, providing 8 bonus mana for casters on long road marches.
scholar-slippers.flavor: Felt-lined leather shoes favored by Collegium clerks and rural tutors who spend hours pacing cold stone floors while memorizing verses. Copper thread stitched into the heels bleeds off stray static charge quietly.

astral-walkers.summary: Star-woven tier-5 Mage boots from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Mind, granting 24 bonus mana for endgame spellcasters.
astral-walkers.flavor: Embroidered with pale silver ley-threads that hum softly above hot volcanic stone, insulating the soles from blistering heat. Senior archons wear them across the Threshold flagstones without ever tiring on the march.

titan-war-gauntlets.summary: Crushing tier-5 Warrior gloves from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Body, adding accuracy to heavy endgame weapon blows.
titan-war-gauntlets.flavor: Forged from dense caldera iron with spiked knuckle-bars built to shatter shields and steady massive two-handed hilts. Even when smeared with soot and oil, their ribbed leather palms never lose their iron grip.

studded-bracers.summary: Guard tier-2 gloves for both classes in Acts I–II requiring 6 Agility, protecting wrists from bowstring slap and blades.
studded-bracers.flavor: Stiffened cowhide cuffs dotted with flat iron studs worn by border archers and light infantry alike. They keep heavy bowstrings from bruising the forearm while turning aside glancing daggers in close ditch brawls.

reinforced-vambraces.summary: Splinted tier-3 gloves for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 9 Agility, offering solid defense and slight accuracy.
reinforced-vambraces.flavor: Narrow strips of tempered steel riveted lengthwise over oiled leather so the wrist bends freely while forearms stay shielded. Boarding marines and ridge-scouts rely on them when parrying axes in tight ship spaces.

shadowstrike-grips.summary: Rosin-dusted tier-5 gloves for both classes from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Agility, adding strong strike accuracy.
shadowstrike-grips.flavor: Supple black hide stitched with fine wire along the knuckles and dusted with pine rosin for an unbreakable hold on bowstaves or dirks. Highland infiltrators prize them for crisp releases in freezing ash wind.

novice-wraps.summary: Linen tier-1 Mage gloves from Act I requiring 4 Mind, adding 6 bonus mana to support beginner frontier spellcraft.
novice-wraps.flavor: Strips of unbleached border linen wound snugly around the palms and wrists to keep fingers warm during rainy northern patrols. Apprentice casters trace tiny chalk sigils across the knuckles before early skirmishes.

velvet-channelers.summary: Silk-lined tier-4 Mage gloves from Acts III–IV requiring 12 Mind, granting 16 bonus mana for advanced spellcasting.
velvet-channelers.flavor: Tailored from deep indigo velvet with silver-threaded fingertips that guide intricate somatic gestures without catching. Senior Collegium fellows wear them when channeling volatile elemental volleys near the coast.

archon-handwraps.summary: Runic tier-5 Mage gloves from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Mind, delivering 24 bonus mana for pinnacle sorcery.
archon-handwraps.flavor: Woven from star-silver filaments and fine mineral cloth that stays cool even while hurling volcanic fire across basalt trenches. Only master arcanists possess the focus to handle raw ley-charge through bare-feeling wraps.

copper-band.summary: Plain tier-1 ring for both classes in Act I requiring 3 Spirit, granting 12 bonus health on early border patrols.
copper-band.flavor: Hammered from salvaged smelter scrap by Thornwick apprentices and stamped with a tiny river-wave mark. Cheap enough for a recruit's first pay-chit, it keeps a soldier's pulse steady in freezing northern rain.

bone-ring.summary: Carved tier-1 ring for both classes in Act I requiring 3 Spirit, adding 12 bonus mana for early frontier casters.
bone-ring.flavor: Filed from a bleached river-stag antler by lower-parish clerks who traded tallow stubs for simple protective trinkets. Light and cold against the skin, it anchors just enough spare mana for an extra early bolt.

ring-of-valor.summary: Stamped tier-3 ring for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 8 Spirit, symbolizing steady resolve under heavy fire.
ring-of-valor.flavor: Awarded by provincial marshals to soldiers who held breached bridges and canyon passes without breaking ranks. The heavy bronze band bears deep scratches from shield-rims and sword-hilts across two campaigns.

ring-of-the-scribe.summary: Signet tier-3 ring for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 8 Spirit, worn by clerks and field scholars on duty.
ring-of-the-scribe.flavor: Engraved with a flat notary face once used to press warm wax onto caravan waybills and abbey probate rolls. Traveling scholars wear it to keep their thoughts orderly amid noisy camps and shifting border wards.

ring-of-the-champions.summary: Heavy tier-5 Warrior ring from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 14 Spirit, adding 35 bonus health and strike accuracy.
ring-of-the-champions.flavor: Forged from meteoric iron and inlaid with a single crimson cinder-garnet for veterans who survived the burning harbor. Its solid weight steadies every sword-stroke against the armored horrors of the deep caldera.

ring-of-the-high-archon.summary: Star-silver tier-5 Mage ring from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 14 Spirit, granting 40 bonus mana for endgame casting.
ring-of-the-high-archon.flavor: Set with a tiny, flawless diamond shard that pulses cold blue whenever deep ley-currents surge nearby. Senior Conclave archons prize it for keeping vast reserves of power ready during prolonged Threshold sieges.

signet-of-unbroken-vigor.summary: Balanced tier-5 ring for both classes from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 14 Spirit, adding 20 health and 20 mana.
signet-of-unbroken-vigor.flavor: Twisted from twin bands of cold silver and dark caldera iron to bridge physical endurance with arcane focus. Veterans marching into the volcanic heart wear it to sustain both steel and sorcery without faltering.

clay-talisman.summary: Humble tier-1 amulet for both classes in Act I requiring 3 Spirit, worn as a basic charm on northern border roads.
clay-talisman.flavor: Pressed from grey Alder riverbank clay and stamped with a crude Radiant Light sunburst before baking in a tavern hearth. Levies wear them on hemp strings, hoping a bit of parish luck turns aside stray gnoll arrows.

bronze-locket.summary: Hinged tier-1 amulet for both classes in Act I requiring 3 Spirit, granting 15 bonus health on early campaigns.
bronze-locket.flavor: Tarnished green around the clasp and dented from riding beneath an iron gorget through wet border skirmishes. Inside sits a folded scrap of parish prayer-vellum and a pinch of dried willow-bark for road luck.

astral-medallion.summary: Etched tier-3 amulet for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 8 Spirit, adding 15 bonus mana on frontier marches.
astral-medallion.flavor: Cast from pale pewter-silver engraved with coastal tide-rings that shimmer faintly in overcast weather. Abbey watchers and field casters wear it to steady their reserve when crossing mist-choked stone causeways.

bloodstone-pendant.summary: Crimson-flecked tier-3 amulet for both classes in Acts II–III requiring 9 Body, granting 40 bonus maximum health.
bloodstone-pendant.flavor: A heavy cabochon of dark green jasper shot through with iron-red veins, mounted in a rough quarry-iron bezel. Pit-fighters and caravan guards swear its steady weight against the chest keeps wounded men upright.

prismatic-choker.summary: Multi-stone tier-4 amulet for both classes in Acts III–IV requiring 11 Spirit, providing 15 bonus mana in late acts.
prismatic-choker.flavor: Strung with alternating chips of quartz, opal, and star-silver wire that split harsh glare into tiny colored sparks. Senior officers and arcanists wear it tight at the throat to keep their focus sharp in battle.

heart-of-the-colossus.summary: Titan-forged tier-5 Warrior amulet from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Body, adding 60 bonus health for frontliners.
heart-of-the-colossus.flavor: Bound in heavy meteoric iron around a dense core of magnetic lodestone pried from an awakened highland guardian. Resting warm against the sternum, it lends a veteran champion the stubborn endurance of living stone.

medallion-of-the-celestial-spire.summary: Exalted tier-5 Mage amulet from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 16 Mind, granting 50 bonus mana for pinnacle sorcery.
medallion-of-the-celestial-spire.flavor: Struck in pure star-silver for senior envoys of the Spire Conclave who mediated imperial decrees across the realm. Its delicate geometric rings hum with cold authority, feeding vast reserves of power to its bearer.

scroll-of-shield-bash.summary: Martial tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II libraries requiring 6 Body, teaching a heavy stunning shield strike.
scroll-of-shield-bash.flavor: Illustrated with blunt charcoal sketches by a Thornwick pike-sergeant who tired of watching recruits hide passively behind oak boards. Driving the iron boss straight into an enemy's jaw buys precious seconds in any melee.

scroll-of-cleave-arc.summary: Sweeping tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II sanctums requiring 6 Body, teaching a wide multi-target melee slash.
scroll-of-cleave-arc.flavor: Copied onto coarse vellum by Greywood timber-fellers turned militia, adapting the broad horizontal swing used to clear tangled brush. One committed arc keeps packs of briar-hounds from swarming a trooper's flanks.

scroll-of-hamstring-cut.summary: Tactical tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II libraries requiring 6 Body, teaching a low strike that slows foes.
scroll-of-hamstring-cut.flavor: Notes scribbled by Redmarsh caravan guards who learned that chasing fast sand raiders in heavy mail is a fool's errand. A quick low cut behind the knee drops a nimble skirmisher to a limp before he can slip away.

scroll-of-sunder-plate.summary: Breaching tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III libraries requiring 7 Body, teaching strikes that strip enemy armor.
scroll-of-sunder-plate.flavor: Compiled by Deep Quarry miners and harbor breachers who studied exactly where rivets shear under angled heavy blows. Once mastered, it lets a trooper peel back thick iron plating so lighter allies can finish the target.

scroll-of-grit-through-pain.summary: Stubborn tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II sanctums requiring 6 Body, teaching veterans to endure heavy wounds.
scroll-of-grit-through-pain.flavor: Less a scholarly treatise than a battered set of breathing drills passed around campfires after bloody bridge stands. Learning to lock the jaw and ignore cracked ribs keeps a soldier standing when lesser troops fold.

scroll-of-whirlwind-maul.summary: Relentless tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 8 Body, teaching a spinning area attack.
scroll-of-whirlwind-maul.flavor: Sketched by a scarred boarding captain who once held a narrow galley deck alone against a dozen press-gang cutthroats. Turning momentum into an unbroken circle of steel punishes any pack foolish enough to surround you.

scroll-of-executioners-blow.summary: Decisive tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV sanctums requiring 8 Body, teaching a lethal finishing strike.
scroll-of-executioners-blow.flavor: Recorded in terse, clinical ink by former Crown judicial officers who knew how to end a duel in one clean downward cut. When an enemy's guard finally falters, this technique leaves no margin for recovery or mercy.

scroll-of-bodkin-shot.summary: Piercing tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II libraries requiring 6 Agility, teaching armor-penetrating arrow fire.
scroll-of-bodkin-shot.flavor: Drawn with neat trajectory diagrams by Alder Ford toll-bowmen tired of watching broadheads bounce off iron bucklers. Adjusting draw-anchor and shaft-angle drives narrow steel points straight through riveted chainmail.

scroll-of-volley-of-reeds.summary: Rapid tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 7 Agility, teaching a wide shower of arrows.
scroll-of-volley-of-reeds.flavor: Adapted from Fenwick marsh-hunters who loosed fanned shafts into rising flocks of river-fowl at dawn. Applied to packed canyon passes, it turns a clear stretch of trail into a rattling hailstorm of ash and goose-fletching.

scroll-of-heartseeker.summary: Unerring tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 8 Agility, teaching a deadly precision shot.
scroll-of-heartseeker.flavor: Annotated by Oakhaven's finest seawall snipers who practiced picking off moving targets from pitching harbor towers. Holding breath until the pulse slows lets an archer thread an arrow straight into a vital gap.

scroll-of-cinder-lance.summary: Focused tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II libraries requiring 6 Mind, teaching a piercing bolt of condensed fire.
scroll-of-cinder-lance.flavor: Drafted by Collegium field-mages who needed to scorch enemy shamans hiding behind friendly pike-walls without singeing their own troops. Tightening the flame into a narrow spear punches cleanly through armored ranks.

scroll-of-brine-frost.summary: Biting tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 7 Mind, teaching salt-chilled freezing magic.
scroll-of-brine-frost.flavor: Developed in Redmarsh outposts where arcanists noticed brackish salt-water freezes into a far nastier, clinging rime than fresh river-mist. Cast over hot basalt or plate, it locks iron joints stiff in seconds.

scroll-of-static-arc.summary: Sparking tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II libraries requiring 6 Mind, teaching quick chain-lightning discharge.
scroll-of-static-arc.flavor: Copied from notes taken beside Greywood's vitrified kilns, where stray ward-charge taught hedge-mages how to snap bright arcs from fingertip to iron helm. Wet border armor makes the lesson considerably sharper.

scroll-of-peat-gas-blast.summary: Volatile tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 7 Mind, teaching explosive bog-vapor ignition.
scroll-of-peat-gas-blast.flavor: Inspired by Fenwick peat-cutters who accidentally blew the roof off a drying shed with a dropped tallow lantern. Summoning and igniting a pocket of marsh gas scatters tight formations in a foul, concussive flash.

scroll-of-siphon-ley.summary: Draining tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II libraries requiring 6 Mind, teaching casters to draw ambient mana.
scroll-of-siphon-ley.flavor: Written in neat Collegium shorthand for frontier scouts and battle-mages stationed far from well-tuned library wards. Tapping shallow ley-threads beneath the mud keeps a caster armed when blue draughts run dry.

scroll-of-vitrify.summary: Scorching tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 8 Mind, teaching intense heat that fuses sand.
scroll-of-vitrify.flavor: Studied from the glassy slag-heaps of burned border kilns where extreme arcane fire melted stone and metal into brittle green crust. Unleashed on the battlefield, it turns loose earth and armor alike into jagged glass.

scroll-of-marrow-dart.summary: Sharp tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II sanctums requiring 6 Spirit, teaching pale bone-splinter projectiles.
scroll-of-marrow-dart.flavor: Inscribed with bone-ash ink by lower-parish probate clerks who kept sharp awls and spare femurs tucked inside their cassocks. Flicking a splinter forward with grave-mana punches neatly through boiled ox-leather.

scroll-of-grave-chill.summary: Cold tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II libraries requiring 6 Spirit, teaching sepulchral frost that slows foes.
scroll-of-grave-chill.flavor: Copied in damp coastal abbey crypts where stone-cold drafts seep through cracked mortar year-round. Wrapping an enemy in the lifeless chill of an open vault numbs sword-arms and slows charging raiders to a crawl.

ash-staff.summary: Tier-2 Mage weapon from Acts I and II requiring 8 Mind, expanding maximum mana to fuel early elemental volleys.
ash-staff.flavor: Cut from pale grey ash along the Alder bluffs and seasoned over slow charcoal fires so the wood never warps in marsh fog. Hedge-casters trade half a month's stipend for a straight stave that holds steady charge through wet campaigns.

rune-staff.summary: Acts II–III tier-3 Mage weapon requiring 11 Mind, boosting maximum mana for mid-campaign arcane barrages.
rune-staff.flavor: Carved with neat geometric channels along the upper shaft by Collegium fellows who needed a reliable conduit on frontier marches. Copper wire bound beneath the grip bleeds off stray sparks before they blister the caster's knuckles.

star-staff.summary: High-tier Mage weapon from Acts III–IV requiring 14 Mind, offering a substantial mana pool for senior casters.
star-staff.flavor: Inlaid with slender strips of pale star-silver that hum softly whenever coastal storms or caldera tremors disturb the ley-lines. Only seasoned arcanists have the discipline to keep its bright discharge from draining their reserves early.

thorn-staff.summary: Endgame tier-5 Mage weapon from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 17 Mind, granting massive mana for pinnacle spells.
thorn-staff.flavor: Hewn from dark, iron-hard briarwood rooted near the volcanic plateau where ordinary timber turns to charcoal in days. Veterans prize its stubborn balance, channeling heavy barrages across smoking basalt trenches without faltering.

wooden-buckler.summary: Light tier-1 Warrior shield from Act I requiring 4 Body, offering basic frontline protection for new recruits.
wooden-buckler.flavor: Stitched together from seasoned oak barrel-staves and rimmed with scrap hide in Thornwick's crowded repair sheds. It will not stop a siege-maul, yet it turns aside gnoll hatchets and quill-fiend spines well enough to earn its keep.

iron-shield.summary: Sturdy tier-2 Warrior shield from Acts I–II requiring 8 Body, built to absorb heavier blows on border marches.
iron-shield.flavor: Hammered from thick border pig-iron and backed with tarred ash planks so wet river-mud cannot rot the leather arm-straps. Levy sergeants issue these shields to men holding bridge approaches where retreat is off the table.

tower-shield.summary: Heavy tier-3 Warrior shield from Acts II–III requiring 12 Body, sheltering frontliners from dense arrow volleys.
tower-shield.flavor: Tall enough to cover a kneeling trooper from chin to shin, reinforced with riveted cross-bars that rattle loudly on steep trails. Moving uphill with twelve pounds of iron on one arm builds broad shoulders or breaks your spirit.

knight-shield.summary: Acts III–IV tier-4 Warrior shield requiring 15 Body, engineered for veteran officers holding contested breaches.
knight-shield.flavor: Forged in Oakhaven's shipwright yards from salt-tempered steel curved to deflect heavy halberds and falling masonry alike. Its embossed rim bears scars from boarding actions, canyon ambushes, and burning harbor piers.

leather-cap.summary: Simple tier-1 helm for both classes in Act I requiring 3 Body, offering light head protection on early patrols.
leather-cap.flavor: Boiled in mutton tallow and stitched with waxed hemp by Thornwick cobblers when iron helmets went south with the Salt Tithe. It keeps freezing rain out of your eyes and takes the worst sting out of a glancing club.

iron-helm.summary: Tier-2 Warrior helm from Acts I–II requiring 7 Body, shielding the skull against overhead blows in close brawls.
iron-helm.flavor: Shaped from two riveted halves of dark border iron with a blunt nasal bar that narrows the wearer's view to a grim slit. Recruits complain that it rings like a church bell when struck, though nobody ever dies from ringing ears.

steel-helm.summary: Durable tier-4 Warrior helm from Acts III–IV requiring 12 Body, built for heavy frontline fighting in late acts.
steel-helm.flavor: Drawn smoothly over a rounded anvil so crossbow bolts and falling rubble slide cleanly off the crown without catching. Harborwatch marines pad the inside with salted wool to keep the steel from chafing during twelve-hour shifts.

scholar-hat.summary: Light tier-2 Mage helm from Acts I–II requiring 6 Mind, granting extra maximum mana for traveling arcanists.
scholar-hat.flavor: Wide-brimmed felt stiffened with beeswax to keep northern drizzle off smudged spellbooks and ink-stained notes. Hedge-tutors stitch tiny copper-wire loops inside the crown to hold a spare drop of ambient charge on long roads.

wizard-hat.summary: Pointed tier-4 Mage helm from Acts III–IV requiring 12 Mind, expanding maximum mana for casters on late marches.
wizard-hat.flavor: Tailored from dense indigo wool lined with silver thread that hums quietly whenever hostile wards flare nearby. Senior fellows of the Conclave wear them pulled low against blowing ash, caring nothing for how crooked the point looks.

padded-jerkin.summary: Basic tier-1 chest armor for both classes in Act I requiring 4 Body, providing light padding against early threats.
padded-jerkin.flavor: Stuffed with raw sheep's wool and horsehair between layers of coarse, unbleached canvas that smells like a wet barn in the rain. It stops thin arrows and briar-hound teeth well enough until a soldier can afford proper mail.

chain-mail.summary: Acts I–II tier-2 Warrior chest armor requiring 9 Body, offering solid iron links for sustained melee engagements.
chain-mail.flavor: Thousands of tiny iron rings punched and riveted by hand during long northern winters, weighing down the shoulders like a wet sack of oats. Veterans wear thick quilted tunics underneath so the links do not pinch skin when struck.

plate-armor.summary: Heavy tier-4 Warrior chest armor from Acts III–IV requiring 14 Body, forged for frontliners facing elite foes.
plate-armor.flavor: Articulated steel breast and back plates buckled tight over oiled leather straps, built to turn away heavy axes and canyon fire. Wearing twenty-four pounds of iron in desert heat or highland ash tests every ounce of grit a trooper owns.

cloth-robe.summary: Coarse tier-1 Mage chest armor from Act I requiring 4 Mind, providing a small mana bonus for novice casters.
cloth-robe.flavor: Spun from rough border flax and dyed dull grey so mud stains from wet ditch-marches barely show along the hem. Apprentices sew extra pockets into the sleeves for chalk stubs, dried herbs, and spare copper coins.

mage-robe.summary: Copper-threaded tier-3 Mage chest armor from Acts II–III requiring 9 Mind, granting solid mana for mid-campaign play.
mage-robe.flavor: Woven with fine copper filaments that steady a caster's focus amid Redmarsh static storms and coastal gales. The broad cuffs shed sparks cleanly, though seasoned arcanists still keep a damp rag tucked into their sash.

star-robe.summary: Star-woven tier-5 Mage chest armor from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Mind, delivering high mana reserves for archons.
star-robe.flavor: Embroidered with pale star-silver ley-diagrams that glow faintly against the dark volcanic gloom of the caldera approaches. Only senior Conclave masters could commission vestments woven to channel such relentless pressure.

sandals.summary: Strapped tier-1 boots for both classes in Act I requiring 3 Agility, offering minimal weight for swift footwork.
sandals.flavor: Simple strapped rawhide soles favored by dry-weather couriers and frugal hedge-scholars who hate heavy cobbler bills. They dry quickly beside a campfire, though wading through Fenwick peat in them is an invitation to misery.

leather-boots.summary: Durable tier-2 boots for both classes in Acts I–II requiring 6 Agility, built for muddy roads and rocky trails.
leather-boots.flavor: Knee-high cowhide greased liberally with tallow and stitched with thick waxed thread so seams hold through axle-deep mire. Every veteran on the Border judges a new recruit first by whether he keeps his boot-soles dry.

iron-boots.summary: Hobnailed tier-3 Warrior boots from Acts II–III requiring 10 Body, anchoring armored fighters in contested choke points.
iron-boots.flavor: Articulated steel plates riveted over thick leather vamps with hobnailed soles that bite cleanly into wet flagstones and loose scree. They clank loudly on stone stairs, yet nobody ever kicks a trooper out of line while he wears them.

swift-boots.summary: Agile tier-4 boots for both classes in Acts III–IV requiring 12 Agility, tailored for rapid movement across hazards.
swift-boots.flavor: Cut from supple, salt-cured hide with layered felt soles that muffle footsteps on coastal granite and volcanic ash alike. Scouts and skirmishers trade good silver for a pair that lets them outrun ambushes without tiring.

ring-of-might.summary: Iron-forged tier-2 ring from Acts I–II for both classes requiring 6 Spirit, worn by fighters seeking martial vigor.
ring-of-might.flavor: Hammered from thick, unadorned border iron and stamped with a blunt fist-mark by Thornwick smiths who wasted no time on filigree. Mercenaries slip it over calloused knuckles before marching out to hold contested river crossings.

ring-of-grace.summary: Tier-2 ring for both classes from Acts I–II requiring 6 Spirit, favored by scouts and agile frontier skirmishers.
ring-of-grace.flavor: Twisted from slender strands of annealed bronze and silver wire that sit light as a reed against the finger. Bowmen and ridge-runners claim it steadies the wrist when loosing arrows across gusty canyon passes and wet boardwalks.

ring-of-insight.summary: Quartz-set tier-2 ring from Acts I–II for both classes requiring 6 Spirit, prized by scholars and casters on patrols.
ring-of-insight.flavor: Set with a flat chip of clear river-quartz polished smooth by lower-parish scribes who spent nights auditing damp tax-rolls. Wearing it seems to clear the fog of a wet march, keeping incantations sharp under pressure.

ring-of-calm.summary: Pewter-cast tier-2 ring from Acts I–II for both classes requiring 6 Spirit, helping borderers keep steady nerves.
ring-of-calm.flavor: Cast from dull pewter salvaged from a quiet roadside chapel and rubbed smooth by anxious thumbs over decades of watch-shifts. Veterans wear it when entering flooded crypts or dark bogs where whispers test a soldier's grit.

great-ring-of-might.summary: Star-iron tier-4 ring from Acts III–IV for both classes requiring 11 Spirit, forged for champions leading assaults.
great-ring-of-might.flavor: Heavy star-iron band reinforced with raised ribs that leave deep marks on anyone careless enough to take a backhand blow. Highcrest officers award these rings to breachers who refuse to yield ground against stone titans.

great-ring-of-grace.summary: Tier-4 ring for both classes from Acts III–IV requiring 11 Spirit, tailored for elite marksmen and swift duelists.
great-ring-of-grace.flavor: Balanced with microscopic silver counterweights by Oakhaven jewelers before the evacuation closed the guild workshops. Wearers move with crisp, unhurried precision even while dodging crossfire on slick harbor flagstones.

great-ring-of-insight.summary: Engraved tier-4 ring from Acts III–IV for both classes requiring 11 Spirit, channeling arcane clarity for casters.
great-ring-of-insight.flavor: Engraved with interlocking Collegium ley-rings fine enough to require a magnifying lens to read. Senior arcanists rely on its quiet resonance to keep complex barrages orderly amid volcanic smoke and deafening siege drums.

great-ring-of-calm.summary: Salt-blessed tier-4 ring from Acts III–IV for both classes requiring 11 Spirit, anchoring resolve against late horrors.
great-ring-of-calm.flavor: Blessed in the coastal abbeys with sea-salt and cold silver wire so neither eldritch dread nor volcanic tremors shake the bearer's pulse. Even standing before the Threshold's silent guards, its wearer breathes steady and slow.

ember-charm.summary: Kiln-baked tier-2 amulet from Acts I–II for both classes requiring 5 Spirit, carrying a spark of hearth-warmth.
ember-charm.flavor: A small clay disc baked with crushed furnace clinker and hung on a tarred hemp cord by northern kiln-workers. It feels faintly warm beneath a wet wool shirt, taking the edge off river drizzle and stray cinderling sparks.

frost-charm.summary: Tier-2 amulet for both classes from Acts I–II requiring 5 Spirit, holding the crisp chill of northern winter air.
frost-charm.flavor: Carved from pale river-slate bound in thin tin wire, always cool against the sternum even when marching into Redmarsh glare. Caravan guards tuck it under their jerkins to weather blistering noon heat along the alkali flats.

storm-charm.summary: Copper-bound tier-2 amulet from Acts I–II for both classes requiring 5 Spirit, grounding stray static on marches.
storm-charm.flavor: Cobbled together by plateau surveyors who grew tired of having their hair stand on end whenever storm-clouds gathered over the monoliths. The braided copper tingles softly before lightning strikes, giving a welcome second to duck.

stone-charm.summary: Bridge-stone tier-2 amulet from Acts I–II for both classes requiring 5 Spirit, lending earthen steadiness on rough ground.
stone-charm.flavor: A smooth, heavy pebble taken from the foundation trench of Alder Bridge and pierced with an iron drill. Ferrymen and pikemen wear it on leather thongs, swearing it keeps a man planted firmly when mud turns slick underfoot.

life-charm.summary: Herbal tier-3 amulet from Acts II–III for both classes requiring 8 Body, granting 30 bonus health for long marches.
life-charm.flavor: Filled with dried willow-bark, bitter rue, and red iron-clay sealed inside a soldered bronze capsule by field apothecaries. Mercenaries prize it during long desert and coastal campaigns where clean bandages are worth silver.

mind-charm.summary: Tier-3 amulet for both classes from Acts II–III requiring 8 Mind, adding 25 bonus mana for sustained spellcasting.
mind-charm.flavor: A faceted sliver of smoked quartz suspended in a brass frame that catches lantern-light without glare. Traveling scholars wear it over their robes to keep a spare well of focus ready when ambushes interrupt long marches.

ward-charm.summary: Silver-etched tier-4 amulet from Acts III–IV for both classes requiring 10 Spirit, woven with protective late-game seals.
ward-charm.flavor: Inscribed with overlapping abbey and Collegium defense glyphs on a heavy disc of salt-tempered silver. Veterans marching toward the Obsidian Caldera keep it tucked tight beneath their gorgets to blunt hostile curses and ash.

healing-draught.summary: Herbal tier-1 potion from Act I supply drops and quartermasters, restoring 65 health in the heat of combat.
healing-draught.flavor: Brewed in Thornwick back-rooms from boiled willow-bark, red marsh-moss, and sharp vinegar to keep it from souring in saddlebags. It tastes like rusty ditch-water, yet one quick swallow closes shallow cuts and steadies weak knees.

greater-healing-draught.summary: Potent tier-3 potion found in Acts II–III supplies and loot sacks, restoring 180 health during heavy engagements.
greater-healing-draught.flavor: Distilled by Oakhaven field surgeons using concentrated alpine herbs and clean cistern water sealed in thick green glass. A single bottle can pull a bleeding frontliner back from the brink when the infirmary tents are miles away.

mana-draught.summary: Standard tier-1 potion from Act I quartermasters and belt drops, replenishing arcane reserves for early casters.
mana-draught.flavor: Steeped from crushed river-quartz dust and bitter blue fen-berries until the liquid glows faintly in dim lantern-light. Apprentice mages grimace at the chalky aftertaste, yet never march out the gate without two phials on their belt.

greater-mana-draught.summary: Concentrated tier-3 potion from Acts II–III supplies, restoring substantial mana reserves during prolonged battles.
greater-mana-draught.flavor: Refined in Collegium field-stills using charged plateau crystal and distilled brine that tingles sharply against the tongue. Senior arcanists guard every stoppered flask closely when holding narrow passes against endless waves.

elixir-of-body.summary: Rare tier-4 potion from Acts III–IV quartermasters and loot sacks, bolstering physical might for tough encounters.
elixir-of-body.flavor: Thick as dark molasses and fortified with powdered ironstone and boiled ox-marrow by Ironcamp alchemists. One draught warms the chest like hot coals, lending a trooper the stubborn heft needed to trade blows with basalt brutes.

elixir-of-agility.summary: Distilled tier-4 potion from Acts III–IV supplies and loot, sharpening reflexes and speed for high-stakes skirmishes.
elixir-of-agility.flavor: Distilled from coastal gale-weed and sharp highland spirits that clear the head in a single blistering gulp. Scouts and marksmen save these clear phials for moments when outrunning crossfire or landing rapid volleys decides survival.

elixir-of-mind.summary: Potent tier-4 potion found in Acts III–IV supplies, expanding mental clarity and arcane command in critical fights.
elixir-of-mind.flavor: Infused with fine star-silver filings and bitter night-blooming herbs harvested along the misty cliffs above Oakhaven. A single sip sweeps away battle-fatigue, leaving ley-geometry crisp and unmistakable in the caster's thoughts.

elixir-of-spirit.summary: Tier-4 potion from Acts III–IV quartermasters and loot, fortifying inner resolve and spiritual endurance.
elixir-of-spirit.flavor: Prepared in quiet coastal abbey cellars from consecrated sea-salt, myrrh, and deep spring water. Veterans drink it before marching into haunted vaults or volcanic gloom, finding their pulse steady regardless of what waits ahead.

scroll-of-fire-bolt.summary: Tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 4 Mind, teaching a reliable single-target fire spell.
scroll-of-fire-bolt.flavor: Copied on cheap sheepskin with soot-black ink by traveling pyromancers who needed an affordable way to light wet brush and scatter wolves. Reading the final syllable turns the parchment to harmless ash in your fingers.

scroll-of-fireball.summary: Wax-sealed tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV sanctums requiring 6 Mind, teaching explosive fire magic.
scroll-of-fireball.flavor: Sealed with red wax stamped with the Collegium's combustion glyph and kept inside a tin tube to prevent accidental sparks in dry baggage trains. Once memorized, it lets a caster turn tight canyon bottlenecks into roaring furnaces.

scroll-of-flame-burst.summary: Compact tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III libraries requiring 5 Mind, teaching a close-range burst of fire.
scroll-of-flame-burst.flavor: Favored by hedge-mages who learned the hard way that briar-hounds rarely wait politely at long range. The terse margin notes advise planting both heels firmly before snapping the wrist to push enemies back in a ring of sparks.

scroll-of-ignite.summary: Sapper's tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 4 Mind, teaching lingering fire damage over time.
scroll-of-ignite.flavor: Written in sharp, angular shorthand by Redmarsh sappers who wanted a cleaner way to torch dry barricades and pitch-soaked wrappings. Even a modest spark clings stubbornly to wool and dry leather once the target catches flame.

scroll-of-frost-bolt.summary: Chilled tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 4 Mind, teaching a bolt that slows advancing foes.
scroll-of-frost-bolt.flavor: Inscribed with pale blue gall-ink on vellum cured in winter river-water so the sheet always feels damp to the thumb. Northern arcanists rely on it to chill charging beasts stiff long enough for pikemen to brace their spears.

tome-of-ice-storm.summary: Heavy tier-4 learning tome from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 9 Mind, teaching a wide hailstorm that batters enemies.
tome-of-ice-storm.flavor: Bound in salted seal-hide with brass corner-clasps to keep coastal damp from swelling the thick rag pages. Mastering its dense diagrams lets a caster summon freezing sleet that shreds formations and numbs sword-arms alike.

scroll-of-chain-frost.summary: Coastal tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV sanctums requiring 6 Mind, teaching frost that leaps between targets.
scroll-of-chain-frost.flavor: Developed by Oakhaven storm-channelers watching freezing spray leap from wave to wave along the granite breakwater. When enemies crowd shoulder-to-shoulder in narrow coastal alleys, a single cast chills the entire pack.

scroll-of-healing.summary: Abbey tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III academies requiring 5 Mind, teaching an essential restorative spell.
scroll-of-healing.flavor: Copied endlessly by abbey novices and frontier medics because clean linen always runs out faster than arrows. It will not regrow a severed limb, yet it knits torn muscle cleanly enough to keep a vanguard company fighting.

tome-of-healing-rain.summary: Water-stained tier-4 learning tome from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 9 Mind, teaching area healing for the squad.
tome-of-healing-rain.flavor: A heavy, water-stained volume preserved from a sunken coastal chapel where monks tended shipwrecked sailors through winter gales. Calling down its gentle, silver-lit mist restores battered companies right in the middle of a siege.
