scroll-of-lightning.summary: Foil-lined tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 5 Mind, teaching fast lightning against armor.
scroll-of-lightning.flavor: Stiffened with thin copper foil along the rollers so the parchment does not scorch when unsealed in dry desert air. Frontline casters prize it for cracking flintback shells and heavy plate that shrug off ordinary arrows.

tome-of-chain-lightning.summary: Storm-cliff tier-4 learning tome from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 9 Mind, teaching arcing lightning across groups.
tome-of-chain-lightning.flavor: Compiled on the storm-lashed cliffs above Harborwatch by scholars studying how lightning dances across wet iron rigging. In battle, one sharp cast turns an enemy's tight iron shield-wall into its own deadliest hazard.

scroll-of-haste.summary: Courier's tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III libraries requiring 5 Mind, teaching a swiftness buff for allies.
scroll-of-haste.flavor: Written in hurried, slanted script by a courier-mage who hated slogging through Redmarsh mud at a foot-soldier's pace. Once learned, it lightens heavy iron boots and hurries tired sword-arms through critical siege breaches.

scroll-of-gale.summary: Squall-bound tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 5 Mind, teaching wind that scatters enemies.
scroll-of-gale.flavor: Kept rolled inside a hollow sea-bird bone by coastal scouts who knew the value of a sudden squall at your back. Unbinding the verse hurls a sharp gust across narrow stone bridges, throwing charging raider packs off their stride.

scroll-of-wind-ward.summary: Parapet tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III academies requiring 4 Mind, teaching a barrier against missiles.
scroll-of-wind-ward.flavor: Sketched with swirling air-currents by Oakhaven wall-arcanists tired of ducking hornbow volleys on exposed parapets. Wrapping a squad in brisk, shifting drafts turns incoming arrows and quills aside into the flagstones.

scroll-of-rock-throw.summary: Quarryman's tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 4 Mind, teaching blunt earth damage.
scroll-of-rock-throw.flavor: A plain, unpretentious formula favored by Deep Quarry geomancers who saw no poetry in magic when a flying chunk of granite solved the problem. It hits with crude physical weight that ignores most elemental wards on the field.

tome-of-stone-curse.summary: Slate-bound tier-4 learning tome from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 9 Mind, teaching petrifying earth magic.
tome-of-stone-curse.flavor: Carved onto thin, slate-bound leaves because ordinary parchment kept stiffening into brittle mineral dust in the author's satchel. Mastering its heavy syllables lets a caster turn charging brutes into helpless grey statues.

scroll-of-stone-skin.summary: Limestone tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 5 Mind, teaching a ward that boosts armor.
scroll-of-stone-skin.flavor: Dusted with crushed quarry limestone that leaves grey fingerprints on everything the reader touches. Cast over a frontliner's gambeson, it stiffens wool and leather until blades rebound as if striking dressed granite.

scroll-of-poison-cloud.summary: Marsh-gas tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III libraries requiring 5 Mind, teaching a lingering toxic cloud.
scroll-of-poison-cloud.flavor: Distilled from Fenwick marsh-gas notes and sealed in oiled bladder-skin so the sheet does not rot the rest of a mage's pack. Unrolling it upwind lets a caster clear narrow trenches without risking a single sword-stroke.

tome-of-quake.summary: Seismic tier-5 learning tome from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 11 Mind, teaching earth magic that shakes the field.
tome-of-quake.flavor: Recovered from cracked highland observatories where ancient scholars charted the tectonic faults beneath Thornvael. Speaking its deep, resonant chords splits cobblestones and drops heavy infantry flat in the volcanic ash.

scroll-of-blessing.summary: Chaplain's tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III academies requiring 5 Mind, teaching a ward that empowers allies.
scroll-of-blessing.flavor: Inscribed in neat abbey hand with gold-ochre ink, carried by chaplains who marched beside northern levies through sleet and mud. A quiet benediction steadies trembling spear-hands and sharpens dull frontier iron in battle.

scroll-of-weaken.summary: Probate tier-3 learning scroll from Acts II–III sanctums requiring 4 Mind, teaching a hex that saps enemy strength.
scroll-of-weaken.flavor: Borrowed from lower-parish probate clerks who knew how a stamped forfeiture notice takes the fight out of even the loudest bully. Cast on a charging brute, it turns heavy swings sluggish and clumsy within a few seconds.

tome-of-resurrect.summary: Pinnacle tier-5 learning tome from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 13 Mind, teaching high magic to restore fallen allies.
tome-of-resurrect.flavor: Locked for generations inside coastal abbey vaults under triple iron seals to keep reckless novices from meddling with the dead. Only a master of rare discipline can call a comrade back across the threshold without paying in blood.

scroll-of-corpse-burst.summary: Mortuary tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV academies requiring 6 Mind, teaching corpse-detonating dark magic.
scroll-of-corpse-burst.flavor: Scratched onto cured pigskin with bone-ash ink by rogue mortuary clerks who saw no reason a dead raider should stop working for the company. Detonating one fallen body scatters packed ranks faster than a siege powder keg.

scroll-of-meditation.summary: Early tier-2 learning scroll from Acts I–II sanctums requiring 3 Mind, teaching techniques to speed mana recovery.
scroll-of-meditation.flavor: The first scroll handed to country hedge-scholars who kept exhausting themselves after two sparks in the rain. Learning to quiet the pulse and draw ambient charge cleanly keeps a caster useful through long border patrols.

leather-gloves.summary: Calfskin tier-1 gloves for both classes in Act I requiring 3 Agility, protecting hands from rope-burn and cold.
leather-gloves.flavor: Stitched from supple calfskin by Thornwick harness-makers with reinforced palms for gripping wet spear-hafts and bowstrings. Nothing fancy sits on the cuffs, just honest protection against blisters and freezing river chill.

iron-gauntlets.summary: Scale-riveted tier-2 Warrior gloves from Acts I–II requiring 8 Body, shielding knuckles and wrists in close brawls.
iron-gauntlets.flavor: Overlapping iron scales riveted onto thick oxhide mitts so a trooper can parry a glancing axe without losing fingers. They clatter against shield-rims and make untying wet boot-laces a grim test of a soldier's patience.

steel-gauntlets.summary: Articulated tier-4 Warrior gloves from Acts III–IV requiring 13 Body, granting heavy protection and an accuracy edge.
steel-gauntlets.flavor: Articulated finger-plates tempered in Oakhaven's yards so veteran swordsmen keep full wrist-snap even inside heavy iron. The roughened leather palms lock onto greatsword hilts through sweat, sea-spray, and volcanic ash.

silk-gloves.summary: Featherweight tier-3 Mage gloves from Acts II–III requiring 9 Mind, adding 6 bonus mana without encumbering gestures.
silk-gloves.flavor: Imported from southern looms before the war and lined with fine copper thread to smooth out rapid finger-weaves. Weightless as dry cobwebs, they keep a caster's hands nimble while holding a tidy spare reserve of mana.

mithril-gale-buckler.summary: Light tier-3 Warrior shield from Acts II–III requiring 10 Body, offering swift deflection without heavy bulk.
mithril-gale-buckler.flavor: Hammered from rare, pale alloy recovered from pre-schism highland veins, light enough to turn aside arrows with a flick of the wrist. Boarding marines prize it on narrow gangplanks where heavy tower shields drag men overboard.

adamantium-needle.summary: Precision tier-4 Warrior weapon from Acts III–IV requiring 13 Agility, dealing 6–9 damage with high accuracy.
adamantium-needle.flavor: Forged from dark, unyielding star-metal ground to a slender rapier point that slips straight through mail links and visor slits. Duelists and harbor officers pay small fortunes for a blade that never bends, chips, or dulls.

dragon-leather-mantle.summary: Tough tier-4 chest armor for both classes in Acts III–IV requiring 13 Agility, balancing protection with mobility.
dragon-leather-mantle.flavor: Cured from the thick, scarred hide of highland drakes using sulfur ash and fish oil so the scales stay supple under heavy movement. Scouts and nimble fighters wear it to shrug off sparks and claws without slowing down.

tome-of-meteor.summary: Iron-bound tier-5 learning tome from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 14 Mind, teaching devastating celestial fire magic.
tome-of-meteor.flavor: Bound in blackened iron plates to keep its scorching vellum leaves from igniting adjacent books on the shelf. Mastering its astronomical calculations lets an archon call down white-hot stone straight onto fortified formations.

scroll-of-inferno.summary: Asbestos tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV sanctums requiring 8 Mind, teaching a sustained jet of roaring flame.
scroll-of-inferno.flavor: Written with soot-ink on treated asbestos-paper salvaged from Ironcamp's smelter archives. Once memorized, it lets a caster sweep narrow canyon trails with an unbroken torrent of white-hot furnace heat until enemies break.

tome-of-blizzard.summary: Lead-sealed tier-5 learning tome from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 13 Mind, teaching a relentless freezing tempest.
tome-of-blizzard.flavor: Preserved in a lead-lined chest atop the northernmost watchtower where winter winds howl ten months of the year. Unsealing its frost-rimed pages grants command over howling sleet that buries entire enemy cohorts in ice.

tome-of-thunderstorm.summary: Storm-watcher's tier-5 learning tome from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 12 Mind, teaching sky-wrath against foes.
tome-of-thunderstorm.flavor: Copied by Spire Conclave storm-watchers during the worst gales ever recorded over the Western Sea. Calling upon its charged verses turns the sky overhead into an anvil, dropping jagged lightning bolts across the battlefield.

scroll-of-iron-skin.summary: Sheet-iron tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV sanctums requiring 9 Mind, teaching defensive armor-hardening magic.
scroll-of-iron-skin.flavor: Etched onto thin, flexible sheet-iron rather than vellum because ordinary paper curled under the weight of the ward. Cast before a breach assault, it turns a soldier's gambeson as unyielding as hammered anvil-steel.

scroll-of-acid-rain.summary: Corrosive tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV libraries requiring 8 Mind, teaching acid rain that eats armor.
scroll-of-acid-rain.flavor: Inspired by the bitter alkali squalls of Redmarsh that strip paint from wagons and pit iron buckles in a single afternoon. Unbinding its sour verses dissolves heavy shields and forces plated troops out of fortified cover.

scroll-of-mana-burn.summary: Inquisitor's tier-4 learning scroll from Acts III–IV academies requiring 9 Mind, teaching magic that drains enemy mana.
scroll-of-mana-burn.flavor: Compiled by Collegium inquisitors tasked with shutting down rogue arcanists during the Schism. One sharp snap of its counter-sigil empties an enemy caster's mana well and leaves him nursing a blinding, helpless headache.

tome-of-time-warp.summary: Paradoxical tier-5 learning tome from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 15 Mind, teaching rare astral manipulation of tempo.
tome-of-time-warp.flavor: Recovered from a sealed pre-schism vault where dust motes hung frozen in mid-air for centuries. Only the sharpest minds can read its paradoxical margin-notes without losing track of the hours slipping silently past.

woodcutter-handaxe.summary: Tier-1 Warrior axe from Act I requiring 4 Body, dealing 1–4 damage for recruits and militia on early patrols.
woodcutter-handaxe.flavor: Pulled straight from a Greywood logging shed and wedged onto a fresh ash handle when the Salt Tithe left the armory empty. It splits kindling and gnoll bucklers with the same blunt, unpretentious northern border thud.

bearded-battleaxe.summary: Hooked tier-2 Warrior axe from Acts I–II requiring 8 Body, delivering 3–7 damage suited for catching enemy shields.
bearded-battleaxe.flavor: Forged with an extended lower bit so a trooper can hook the top rim of an enemy shield, yank it down, and follow through with the backswing. Border veterans prize its honest weight in muddy, crowded northern ditch brawls.

tempered-war-axe.summary: Brine-quenched tier-3 Warrior axe from Acts II–III requiring 11 Body, dealing 5–11 damage with added accuracy.
tempered-war-axe.flavor: Quenched carefully in brine and oil by Oakhaven smiths so the broad edge bites deep into brigandine without chipping on rivets. Balanced for one-handed work alongside a heavy kite shield on long, grueling coastal campaigns.

crescent-broadaxe.summary: Swept-blade tier-4 Warrior axe from Acts III–IV requiring 14 Body, delivering 8–16 damage and accuracy for shock troops.
crescent-broadaxe.flavor: Swept into a wide, wicked curve modeled after boarding axes used to chop through ships' rigging and barricades alike. One full-shouldered swing shears through layered leather and splintered oak shields effortlessly.

berserker-decapitator.summary: Caldera-forged tier-5 Warrior axe from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 17 Body, dealing massive 11–22 damage with accuracy.
berserker-decapitator.flavor: Hammered from dark caldera ironstone with a brutal, nose-heavy profile built purely for splitting heavy plate in a single blow. Only broad-shouldered veterans can swing it through an entire highland siege without tiring.

sq73-lighthouse-fresnel-lens.summary: Harbor Pilot's Act III frontier quest offering 610 gold and 1060 XP to recover a drowned lighthouse prism.
sq73-lighthouse-fresnel-lens.flavor: Without its faceted brass-bound lens, the Harborwatch beacon throws barely enough light to clear the breakwater. Pilots refuse to run overloaded caravels through the fog until someone dives into the flooded vaults and hauls the heavy glass back.

sq74-shingle-spit-beacons.summary: Salt Corporal's Act III frontier quest paying 660 gold and 1150 XP to plant tide-stakes along the shingle spit.
sq74-shingle-spit-beacons.flavor: At dusk the narrow gravel bar disappears under two feet of gray chop, swallowing supply carts that stray ten paces off the crown. Hammering tarred marker-stakes into the wet stones before the swell rises saves both mules and boots.

sq75-orchard-gallows-axes.summary: Mudlark Pip's Act III frontier quest awarding 700 gold and 1220 XP for felling blighted coastal cider trees.
sq75-orchard-gallows-axes.flavor: Pip has no love for orchards, especially ones that grab passersby by the collar and drop sour spores into the rain-barrels. Bring sharp axes, keep your back to the stone wall, and leave nothing standing taller than a knee.

sq76-capstan-grease-drums.summary: Riverlock Keeper's Act III frontier quest granting 730 gold and 1280 XP to recover bronze gears for Twin-Lock.
sq76-capstan-grease-drums.flavor: Salt spray chews through ordinary iron teeth in a single winter, leaving the canal floodgates jammed half-open. The keeper needs cast bronze pinions salvaged from the lower shed before the freshwater basin drains into the sea.

sq77-vane-ledger-strongbox.summary: Warden Lyra's Act III frontier quest offering 765 gold and 1340 XP to seize Baron Vane's smuggling ledgers.
sq77-vane-ledger-strongbox.flavor: Lyra has suspected for months that Oakhaven's grain shortages were walking out the back gate on Vane's private barges. Bringing her the ironbound strongbox gives the garrison all the proof it needs to confiscate the Baron's stores.

sq78-culverin-sponge-rods.summary: Harbor Firewarden's Act III frontier quest paying 800 gold and 1400 XP to haul ramrods to the culverin wall.
sq78-culverin-sponge-rods.flavor: Firing a hot bronze gun without swabbing the bore turns the crew into red mist on the next load. Raiders burned the forward tool-wagon, leaving the seawall gunners desperate for fresh sheepskin sponge-rods.

sq79-obsidian-glass-blades.summary: Ash-Scout's Act IV frontier quest awarding 860 gold and 1500 XP for harvesting sharp volcanic glass from the coves.
sq79-obsidian-glass-blades.flavor: Where magma met cold mountain runoff, the stone cooled into brittle black sheets sharper than any guild razor. Scouts lash slivers onto arrow-shafts and field knives that slice cleanly through thick leather.

sq80-highcrest-trench-stakes.summary: Commander Rowan's Act IV frontier quest granting 920 gold and 1620 XP to plant iron obstacles along Highcrest.
sq80-highcrest-trench-stakes.flavor: Timber barricades catch fire the moment a cinderhorn breathes on them, so Rowan ordered heavy iron spikes bolted into crossed frames. Dragging them into the ash-drifts under sniper fire is ugly work, yet it breaks charges cold.

sq81-capacitor-ground-wires.summary: Siege Sapper's Act IV frontier quest paying 1000 gold and 1750 XP to ground the crackling West Spire.
sq81-capacitor-ground-wires.flavor: Stray static arcing off the shattered beacon tower has already cooked two mules and melted a sergeant's helm-buckle. Pegging thick copper cables straight into the basalt drains the charge so sappers can approach safely.

sq82-sallyport-slag-craters.summary: Greystone Sentry's Act IV frontier quest offering 1070 gold and 1880 XP to fill smoking craters on the glacis.
sq82-sallyport-slag-craters.flavor: Hostile mortar shells punched waist-deep pits right outside the sallyport, turning every counter-charge into a broken-ankle trap. Hauling gravel baskets out into the crossfire keeps the garrison's exit road passable.

sq83-ashveil-charred-grimoires.summary: Penitent Elias's Act IV frontier quest awarding 1150 gold and 2000 XP to salvage grimoires from the summit stair.
sq83-ashveil-charred-grimoires.flavor: When the renegade arcanists fled up Ashveil Gorge, half their pack-mules bolted and spilled bound folios across the smoking steps. Elias wants the surviving pages gathered before sulfur rain turns the ink to mud.

sq84-unquenched-slag-billets.summary: Foundry Stoker's Act IV frontier quest granting 1210 gold and 2120 XP to haul hot billets from the Unquenched Jaw.
sq84-unquenched-slag-billets.flavor: High-grade caldera ironstone cools too brittle unless hauled straight from the pit while still glowing dull cherry. Tongs, thick leather aprons, and fast boots are the only things standing between a stoker and blistered ribs.

sq85-portcullis-counterweights.summary: Commander Rowan's Act IV frontier quest paying 1280 gold and 2240 XP to jam the Magnetic Narrows gate.
sq85-portcullis-counterweights.flavor: If the Iron Pact drops the middle iron grate behind our vanguard, the canyon turns into an iron coffin. Wedging stone blocks into the counterweight shafts keeps the road open until the last cart clears.

sq86-drawbridge-chain-oil.summary: Siege Sapper's Act IV frontier quest offering 1340 gold and 2360 XP to free rusted chains over the magma moat.
sq86-drawbridge-chain-oil.flavor: Volcanic grit welds iron links solid in three days flat unless kept slick with heavy mineral grease. Reaching the winch-house means crossing narrow stone ledges while hot updrafts singe your cloak.

sq87-three-roads-signal-horns.summary: Commander Rowan's Act IV frontier quest awarding 1410 gold and 2480 XP to recover brass horns at Three-Roads Watch.
sq87-three-roads-signal-horns.flavor: Thick ash-fog swallows lantern light within twenty paces, leaving brass war-horns as the only reliable way to coordinate flanking columns. Rowan needs the garrison's long horns rescued from the overrun outer pickets.

sq88-anchor-seal-censers.summary: Threshold Penitent's Act IV frontier quest granting 1500 gold and 2600 XP to bring consecrated ash to the seals.
sq88-anchor-seal-censers.flavor: Even seasoned veterans feel their knees go weak near the ancient Anchor Seals where ley-pressure hums through the soles of their boots. Burning abbey ash in the bronze censers steadies the air and quiets restless wards.

sq-m07-frozen-survey.summary: Act I side quest in m07 from Surveyor Hal, rewarding 80 gold and 150 XP for recovering his brass theodolite.
sq-m07-frozen-survey.flavor: Hal dropped his prized sighting instrument in a freezing ditch when gnoll scouts broke out of the treeline. Without its graded brass rings, Thornwick's engineers are stuck guessing bridge spans by eye.

sq-m10-dwarven-paychest.summary: Act I side quest in m10 from Foreman Durn, paying 110 gold and 180 XP to retrieve a locked miners' paychest.
sq-m10-dwarven-paychest.flavor: Dwarven drainage crews never leave silver behind willingly, which tells you how fast the undervault galleries flooded. The iron chest still sits chained to a stone pillar, waiting for someone tough enough to haul it dry.

sq-m25-aquifer-valves.summary: Act III side quest in m25 from Well-Wright Maren, awarding 150 gold and 240 XP to open cliff relief valves.
sq-m25-aquifer-valves.flavor: Trapped steam beneath the coastal basalt is cracking Oakhaven's freshwater cisterns like eggshells. Turning the rusted bronze wheels along the cliff face vents the pressure before the whole terrace heaves.

sq-m26-spotter-mirrors.summary: Act III side quest in m26 from Scout Captain Corin, offering 170 gold and 270 XP to smash enemy signal mirrors.
sq-m26-spotter-mirrors.flavor: Renegade spotters perched on the moorland rocks flash range-codes straight down to their artillery crews. Shattering their polished brass reflectors blinds the guns and lets our infantry cross in one piece.

sq-m27-laudanum-crates.summary: Act III side quest in m27 from Surgeon Sera, granting 190 gold and 300 XP to salvage a stranded apothecary cart.
sq-m27-laudanum-crates.flavor: Amputating shattered limbs with nothing stronger than watered ale breaks even the toughest veteran's nerve. Sera needs the intact laudanum crates pulled out of the ditch before raiders smash the glass.

sq-m28-harbor-charts.summary: Act III side quest in m28 from Harbor Pilot Venn, paying 210 gold and 330 XP to loot a drowned chart-room.
sq-m28-harbor-charts.flavor: Oilskin depth-charts showing every submerged reef outside Oakhaven still hang inside the Sunken Citadel's flooded tower. Grab them before salt water eats the ink, or the evacuation fleet sails blind.

sq-m29-dropped-quivers.summary: Act III side quest in m29 from Gate Warden Lyra, awarding 230 gold and 360 XP to gather quivers on the trail.
sq-m29-dropped-quivers.flavor: Retreating bowmen shed heavy war-quivers along the canyon switchbacks to outrun the rising tide. Good ash arrows with steel bodkins are too scarce to leave rotting in the shingle.

sq-m30-orchard-well.summary: Act III side quest in m30 from Sapper Tobb, offering 250 gold and 390 XP to cap a hidden orchard spring.
sq-m30-orchard-well.flavor: Besieging raiders have been watering their pack-mules at an unmarked spring tucked behind the stone terraces. Plugging the shaft with quicklime and rubble forces them to haul brine from the shore.

sq-m31-toll-strongbox.summary: Act III side quest in m31 from Quartermaster Bram, granting 280 gold and 420 XP to seize the bridge-warden's ledger.
sq-m31-toll-strongbox.flavor: Corrupt canal mercenaries skimmed silver off every grain barge entering Harborwatch for six straight months. Bram wants their toll-book back so the garrison can claw back every stolen florin.

sq-m32-binding-anchors.summary: Act III side quest in m32 from Arcanist Orin, paying 310 gold and 450 XP to shatter ancient anchor pylons.
sq-m32-binding-anchors.flavor: Cracked stone obelisks ringing the highland cairn still leak erratic earth-charge into the awakened colossus. Knocking them flat cuts the titan off from the mountain's ley-veins.

sq-m33-blackmail-writs.summary: Act III side quest in m33 from Captain Mara, awarding 340 gold and 480 XP to burn Baron Vane's debt writs.
sq-m33-blackmail-writs.flavor: Vane kept half Oakhaven's ship-captains compliant by threatening to foreclose on their families' dry-docks. Tossing his notarized parchments into a brazier buys more loyalty than a chest of crowns.

sq-m34-salvage-manifest.summary: Act III side quest in m34 from Master Gunner Rolf, offering 370 gold and 510 XP to reclaim stolen cannon parts.
sq-m34-salvage-manifest.flavor: Rival mercenary companies stripped bronze trunnions and elevating screws off two disabled harbor guns during the confusion. Rolf wants his hardware back before the seawall takes another assault.

sq-m35-drydock-winches.summary: Act III side quest in m35 from Shipwright Odo, granting 400 gold and 540 XP to save an unfinished evacuation brig.
sq-m35-drydock-winches.flavor: Her hull is caulked and her mast is stepped, yet arsonists are closing in on the slipway chains. Freeing the drydock winches lets the tide float her clear before fire-pots turn her to ash.

sq-m36-beacon-cairns.summary: Act IV side quest in m36 from Pathfinder Joren, paying 430 gold and 570 XP to mark safe trails in the ash.
sq-m36-beacon-cairns.flavor: Fresh cinder-snow buries old wagon ruts in an hour, hiding deep thermal cracks beneath a smooth gray crust. Stacking painted basalt cairns along the firm spine keeps the main column from losing horses.

sq-m37-grounded-rods.summary: Act IV side quest in m37 from Artificer Kel, awarding 460 gold and 600 XP to salvage copper conductors.
sq-m37-grounded-rods.flavor: Pure annealed copper is harder to find in the highlands than gold plate, and the shattered signal beacons are full of it. Pry the heavy rods loose while the towers are still smoking.

sq-m38-mortar-barrels.summary: Act IV side quest in m38 from Mason-Sergeant Vane, offering 490 gold and 640 XP to haul quicklime to the breach.
sq-m38-mortar-barrels.flavor: Greystone's curtain wall is trembling under stonebreaker hits, and dry stone stacked without mortar topples at the first shove. Rolling heavy lime barrels up the ramp keeps the battlements standing.

sq-m39-dropped-codices.summary: Act IV side quest in m39 from Archivist Selene, granting 520 gold and 680 XP to gather Malrik's scattered folios.
sq-m39-dropped-codices.flavor: As Malrik sprinted toward the summit portal, loose vellum sheets tore free of his satchel and blew into the rocks. Selene wants every diagram recovered before enemy scouts burn the evidence.

sq-m40-leysalt-stores.summary: Act IV side quest in m40 from Sapper Captain Dax, paying 550 gold and 720 XP to flood enemy ley-salt magazines.
sq-m40-leysalt-stores.flavor: Barrels of crystalline ley-salt feed the Iron Pact's heavy mana-cannons across the twin crags. Cracking the cistern pipes into their storage cellars turns lethal ordnance into harmless wet slush.

sq-m41-golem-cores.summary: Act IV side quest in m41 from Smith-Master Tor, awarding 580 gold and 760 XP to extract lodestone cores.
sq-m41-golem-cores.flavor: Inside every fallen basalt brute sits a fist-sized heart of dense magnetic ore worth a fortune at the anvil. Tor pays handsomely for intact cores pried out of the canyon wreckage.

sq-m42-slag-sluices.summary: Act IV side quest in m42 from Engineer Hollis, offering 610 gold and 800 XP to choke the magma feeders.
sq-m42-slag-sluices.flavor: Iron Pact defenders flood the outer moat trenches with fresh molten slag whenever our sappers bring up ladders. Dropping the iron sluice-gates starves the channels until they crust over hard enough to cross.

sq-m43-signal-towers.summary: Act IV side quest in m43 from Captain Mara, granting 640 gold and 840 XP to cut hostile relief signal flags.
sq-m43-signal-towers.flavor: Three wooden flag-masts overlooking the junction coordinate enemy reserve marches across the valley. Hacking down their halyards leaves the besieging columns stumbling blind in the smoke.

sq-m44-warden-tablets.summary: Act IV side quest in m44 from Archivist Selene, paying 660 gold and 860 XP to inspect the Threshold steles.
sq-m44-warden-tablets.flavor: Tall slate slabs lining the inner chamber record the exact terms of the ancient balance between stone and fire. Reading every face before stepping onto an altar ensures you know what you are signing.

sq-m45-fractured-resonators.summary: Act IV side quest in m45 from Arcanist Orin, awarding 680 gold and 880 XP to steady the marble resonators.
sq-m45-fractured-resonators.flavor: Cracked tuning pillars along the Crown Vault's flank are throwing wild stasis pulses that freeze friend and foe alike. Wedging copper shims into their bases calms the room long enough to fight cleanly.

sq-m46-quench-braziers.summary: Act IV side quest in m46 from Sapper Captain Dax, offering 700 gold and 900 XP to smother the oath-braziers.
sq-m46-quench-braziers.flavor: Four towering iron bowls burning volcanic pitch feed the ambient heat inside the Furnace Heart. Dumping ash-sacks over their grates knocks the temperature down before your armor starts glowing.

field-ashbrook-watchman.summary: Act I gate-sentry stationed along the southern frontier approaches, watching the foggy road toward Ashbrook.
field-ashbrook-watchman.flavor: Joren has spent six wet months squinting into the drizzle from a leaking wooden box, counting supply carts that never return. He trusts hot tallow, dry bowstrings, and very little else.

field-ford-tollkeeper.summary: Act I tax-clerk stationed near the Alder River crossings, keeping stubborn track of border tariffs and chains.
field-ford-tollkeeper.flavor: Even with gnolls howling across the shallows, Clerk Oswin refuses to close his inkpot until every wagon's weight is entered in the daybook. Border soldiers mock him, yet he always knows who passed through last.

field-fen-peatcutter.summary: Act I bog guide working the soggy Fenwick turf-ditches, familiar with every safe plank and mire-pocket.
field-fen-peatcutter.flavor: Mara reads dark water the way city clerks read vellum, spotting sunken cart-tracks and wisp-traps twenty paces ahead. She carries a long iron-shod turf spade that doubles nicely as a polearm.

field-ravenwatch-runner.summary: Act I frontier scout carrying dispatches between Thornwick, Craghorn Ridge, and Ravenwatch Keep.
field-ravenwatch-runner.flavor: Talia travels light with two dry pairs of wool socks and a brass whistle looped around her neck. She knows every goat-track off the main highway, which is the only reason she is still breathing.

field-greywood-sawyer.summary: Act I lumberjack working the Greywood timber camps, supplying palisade logs and planks for Thornwick.
field-greywood-sawyer.flavor: Dobb smells permanently of fresh pine resin and wet sawdust, with forearms thick as mill-axles. He has little patience for southern bailiffs who confiscate his best oak beams while leaving the local roof leaking.

field-warden-hale.summary: Act II outpost-scout patrolling the Redmarsh trails, keeping watch on canyon passes and desert markers.
field-warden-hale.flavor: Transferred south when the northern line thinned, Hale traded his wool cloak for vinegar-cured linen and a scarred canteen. He speaks rarely, wastes no water, and checks every horizon twice before moving.

field-miner-tomas.summary: Act II quarry foreman overseeing the stepped basalt terraces and timber pit-props of the Deep Quarry.
field-miner-tomas.flavor: Grey ironstone dust sits permanently in the creases around Tomas's eyes. He knows the exact groan a ceiling beam makes ten seconds before a collapse, and he guards his crew's tools like silver.

field-alkali-drover.summary: Act II caravan teamster hauling freight across the treacherous salt-pans and corduroy roads of Redmarsh.
field-alkali-drover.flavor: Drover Vane curses his mules with affectionate precision and keeps two spare axles lashed beneath every wagon bed. Anyone who has dragged salt-pork through alkali mud without losing a wheel earns respect.

field-wardstone-surveyor.summary: Act II field geomancer monitoring the fractured quartz obelisks and static storms of the high plateau.
field-wardstone-surveyor.flavor: Nira carries a satchel full of copper wire, plumb-bobs, and cracked chalk-slates, measuring ley-drift while sand whips across her spectacles. She blames sloppy southern maintenance for every storm on the flats.

field-cistern-guard.summary: Act II well-guard stationed along the desert watering posts, protecting scarce aquifers from raiders and taint.
field-cistern-guard.flavor: Kell stands ten-hour shifts beside brackish stone troughs with a loaded crossbow resting across his knees. In Redmarsh, guarding clean water makes you more popular than a priest and twice as likely to be shot.

field-salt-corporal.summary: Act III marine non-commissioned officer holding the wet coastal approaches and shingle spits near Oakhaven.
field-salt-corporal.flavor: Corporal Brenn barks orders loud enough to carry over breaking surf and never lets a recruit sit down in wet boots. Three seasons of boarding actions left him with a crooked nose and iron discipline.

field-harbor-pilot.summary: Act III coastal navigator guiding evacuation vessels through fogbanks, boom-chains, and jagged shingle reefs.
field-harbor-pilot.flavor: Maren knows every hidden rock and rip-tide between Oakhaven and the Western Rim by the color of the foam alone. Ship-captains who ignore her hand-signals usually end up swimming back to shore.

field-oakhaven-surgeon.summary: Act III field medic tending wounded borderers and refugees along the coastal roads and chapel infirmaries.
field-oakhaven-surgeon.flavor: Apothecary Linn keeps her needles boiled in sour wine and her voice flat even when cannon shot rattles the roof tiles. She measures a battle not in banners captured, but in clean linen spent.

field-riverlock-keeper.summary: Act III canal engineer maintaining the heavy sluice-gates and freshwater channels feeding Harborwatch.
field-riverlock-keeper.flavor: Orin wears tallow-stained coveralls and carries a heavy iron wrench tucked through his belt like a sword. He treats the twin floodgates like temperamental horses that only obey a firm hand.

field-harbor-firewarden.summary: Act III dock-captain coordinating fire-buckets, pitch stores, and seawall gun crews along the war-docks.
field-harbor-firewarden.flavor: Cole's eyebrows have been singed off twice fighting burning timber barges, yet he still refuses to leave the piers. Give him a bucket line and clear flagstones, and he will hold back an inferno.

field-ash-scout.summary: Act IV highland pathfinder charting safe basalt trails through the sulfur fissures and cinder-snow of the caldera.
field-ash-scout.flavor: Riven wraps wet linen around his nose and tests every smooth ash-drift with a six-foot ironwood pole before stepping forward. Few scouts survive a week near Highcrest without developing his quiet paranoia.

field-siege-sapper.summary: Act IV demolitionist specializing in breaching basalt walls, grounding spires, and sabotaging enemy magazines.
field-siege-sapper.flavor: Garr smells permanently of sulfur, blasting powder, and scorched leather, and he grins widest when a wall starts leaning. Regular infantry give him ten paces of elbow room whenever he opens his pack.

field-greystone-sentry.summary: Act IV wall-guard holding the battered pumice-mortar battlements of Greystone Bastion against Iron Pact sieges.
field-greystone-sentry.flavor: Watchman Varo sleeps sitting upright with his helmet strapped on, waking instantly whenever siege-golem footsteps vibrate through the stone. He has lost count of the assaults, yet his pike-point stays sharp.

field-threshold-penitent.summary: Act IV ash-marked archivist keeping solemn record of the ancient inscriptions and seals near the caldera heart.
field-threshold-penitent.flavor: Sola traded her abbey robes for scorched wool and a brass rubbing-box, determined that someone should remember what stood beneath the mountain before the fire takes it. Her hands are stained black with charcoal.

field-foundry-stoker.summary: Act IV smith-mate tending the roaring volcanic bellows and slag-troughs of Ironcamp's forward forge-yards.
field-foundry-stoker.flavor: Brann works stripped to a heavy leather apron even in freezing highland wind, shoveling glowing ironstone billets with tireless rhythm. He insists cold steel is just lazy metal waiting to be woken up.

field-alder-ferryman.summary: Act I river ferryman operating the flatboats and rope-crossings along the rain-swollen Alder bends.
field-alder-ferryman.flavor: Hobb charges two coppers for a dry crossing and double if your horse kicks the gunwale. He has ferried tax bailiffs, smugglers, and gnoll-hunters alike without ever asking a single unnecessary question.

field-border-peddler.summary: Act I wandering peddler hauling dry socks, flint, and salted eels along the muddy northern tracks.
field-border-peddler.flavor: Bram pushes a squeaking handcart straight through warzones because soldiers always pay better than farmers when their boots fall apart. He claims he has no politics beyond honest copper and dry roads.

field-willow-deserter.summary: Act I former regular hiding along the willow banks after walking away from a Salt-Tithe enforcement column.
field-willow-deserter.flavor: Corporal Vane still wears his patched uniform coat with the brass Crown buttons ripped clean off. He insists he signed up to fight raiders, not to burn northern grain barns for southern clerks.

field-ford-herbalist.summary: Act I rural herbalist gathering willow-bark, bitter rue, and bog-moss along the damp river bluffs.
field-ford-herbalist.flavor: Mother Tilda has outlived three bailiffs and two border wars by knowing which weeds cure trench-fever and which ones sour a bully's stew. Even superstitious levies tip their caps when she passes.

field-cairn-pilgrim.summary: Act I traveling pilgrim of the Radiant Light walking the muddy shrine-roads between northern parishes.
field-cairn-pilgrim.flavor: Brother Aldous carries a worn ash staff and a tin cup, stopping at every roadside boundary stone to brush away moss and say a quiet blessing. He refuses to hurry, even when wolves howl nearby.

field-bridge-tinker.summary: Act I itinerant tinker mending cracked kettles, loose rivets, and bent buckles near the river bridges.
field-bridge-tinker.flavor: Pip can patch a split leather strap or solder a leaking canteen in five minutes flat using nothing but a charcoal pot and wire scraps. Soldiers treat him better than most lieutenants.

field-peat-cutter.summary: Act II bog-edge peat-cutter harvesting fuel blocks along the damp transition into the Redmarsh flats.
field-peat-cutter.flavor: Digger Marn spends his days slicing black turf into neat bricks to dry in the harsh southern wind. He knows every sinkhole along the ditch and never trusts ground that looks too green.

field-fen-hermit.summary: Act II solitary hermit living in a stilted reed-hut on the brackish fringes of Redmarsh.
field-fen-hermit.flavor: Old Reed-Eyes stopped coming into town ten years ago after a tax clerk tried to assess his fishing net. He trades sharp warnings and dried marsh-herbs to travelers who remember to knock politely.

field-leech-apothecary.summary: Act II traveling apothecary breeding alkali leeches and brewing bitter antitoxins for desert patrols.
field-leech-apothecary.flavor: Master Corvus carries a wicker basket full of glass jars that slosh ominously whenever he walks. His remedies taste like boiled copper and vinegar, yet they pull viper venom out faster than prayer.

field-dike-surveyor.summary: Act II frontier cartographer charting sinking embankments and shifting brine-channels across the wastes.
field-dike-surveyor.flavor: Fenwick's ink-stained sleeves and brass dividers never leave his side, even when sand-raiders prowl the ridges. He insists a bad map kills more soldiers than a dull sword ever could.

field-bog-scavenger.summary: Act II resourceful scavenger combing overturned supply wagons and alkali flats for salvageable iron.
field-bog-scavenger.flavor: Raker Nell carries a long hooked pole and a burlap sack, prying intact buckles, horseshoes, and unbroken bottles out of the mud before the brine eats them. Nothing goes to waste on her watch.

field-marsh-flagellant.summary: Act II wandering zealot preaching harsh penance along the sun-baked roads of Redmarsh.
field-marsh-flagellant.flavor: Penitent Garr walks barefoot across salt-crust that blisters ordinary hides, muttering warnings about the coming heat. Caravan guards give him wide berth, though his grim prophecies rarely miss the mark.

field-wreck-diver.summary: Act III coastal salvager swimming out to shattered hulls wedged along the shingle reefs at low tide.
field-wreck-diver.flavor: Diver Sal holds her breath longer than any marine in Harborwatch and carries a weighted iron pry-bar strapped to her thigh. She knows the exact worth of brass ship-fittings and dry powder kegs.

field-salt-raker.summary: Act III coastal salt-worker scraping coarse white crystals from tidal evaporation pans outside Oakhaven.
field-salt-raker.flavor: Raker Orin's hands are cracked white from brine and sun, yet his quiet labor keeps the evacuation fleet's beef barrels from rotting at sea. He watches the horizon more closely than any lookout.

field-escaped-oarsman.summary: Act III former galley-slave who broke his chains and swam ashore from the hostile blockade fleet.
field-escaped-oarsman.flavor: Kaelo still wears a sawed-off iron cuff around his left ankle as a reminder never to surrender alive. He knows the blockade's patrol timings and gladly points coastal guns straight at his old captors.

field-cliff-falconer.summary: Act III coastal scout using trained sea-hawks to spot approaching raiders and blockade sails through fog.
field-cliff-falconer.flavor: Warden Mirella wears a scarred rawhide gauntlet and whistles sharp notes that carry cleanly against the gale. Her birds see through coastal haze far better than any brass spyglass.

field-net-mender.summary: Act III veteran fisherman repairing hemp nets and rigging ropes along Oakhaven's lower coves.
field-net-mender.flavor: Old Barto's knees gave out years ago, yet his fingers still tie knots faster than a young marine can draw a knife. He listens quietly to every rumor drifting off the docks.

field-lighthouse-keeper.summary: Act III steadfast keeper tending the oil-lamps and brass reflectors of the coastal warning beacons.
field-lighthouse-keeper.flavor: Keeper Torin smells permanently of whale oil and salt spray, climbing two hundred granite steps twice a night without complaint. As long as his wick burns, lost ships still have a chance.

field-ash-collector.summary: Act IV highland laborer shoveling volcanic cinder off supply roads and fortress roofs near Ironcamp.
field-ash-collector.flavor: Sweeper Dax laughs that his job never runs out of work, since the caldera dumps two fresh inches of grey grit every morning. Beneath the soot, he knows every hidden cellar door in camp.

field-disgraced-scribe.summary: Act IV former Collegium archivist who marched inland to copy ancient Threshold texts before they burn.
field-disgraced-scribe.flavor: Scribe Malen lost his faculty stipend for arguing with senior magisters over the Schism. Now he crouches behind basalt walls with a tin inkhorn, preserving forbidden history one shaky page at a time.

field-siege-deserter.summary: Act IV battle-hardened veteran who walked away from the Iron Pact after seeing their ruthless tactics.
field-siege-deserter.flavor: Sergeant Thorne carries twenty years of frontier scars and a battered halberd stripped of its former banner. He fights quietly now, asking only for honest company and a clean death.

field-cinder-apothecary.summary: Act IV highland healer treating sulfur burns, ash-cough, and siege wounds along the caldera approaches.
field-cinder-apothecary.flavor: Sister Vesper mixes cooling clay poultices with melted alpine snow to soothe blistered skin. Soldiers joke that her bedside manner is colder than her salves, yet nobody argues when she patches them up.

field-relic-smuggler.summary: Act IV daring smuggler slipping rare star-iron and pre-schism trinkets out of contested caldera ruins.
field-relic-smuggler.flavor: Vex knows every dry culvert and blind ledge between Highcrest and the Outer Rampart. He sells to anyone with hard crowns, insisting that relics do no good buried under fifty feet of lava.

field-mad-prophet.summary: Act IV scorched seer wandering the volcanic bluffs, chanting riddles about the Crown and the Furnace.
field-mad-prophet.flavor: Old Cinder-Tongue stared into a glowing fissure too long and came back speaking in broken verse about headless kings and iron thrones. Sentries toss him hardbread mostly to keep him from shouting at night.

rusty-sword.summary: Tier-1 Warrior weapon requiring 4 Body, dealing modest 2–3 physical damage in early Act I skirmishes.
rusty-sword.flavor: Pulled from a damp Thornwick militia barrel and wiped down with an oily rag before muster. The fuller is pitted brown with three winters of neglect, yet it still beats meeting a border gnoll with bare fists.

iron-sword.summary: Tier-2 Warrior weapon (Acts I–II) requiring 8 Body, offering 4–6 damage and a small accuracy boost.
iron-sword.flavor: Plain, honest border iron hammered out by town smiths when real steel stays locked in southern depots. Properly whetted before a march, it holds a clean edge through boiled leather and gnoll shields alike.

steel-sword.summary: Tier-3 Warrior weapon (Acts II–III) requiring 11 Body, delivering 7–9 damage and improved strike accuracy.
steel-sword.flavor: Tempered evenly over charcoal beds in Oakhaven's yards so the blade flexes without snapping on heavy plate. Veteran sergeants prize its crisp balance during long bridge stands and boarding fights.

knight-sword.summary: Tier-4 Warrior weapon (Acts III–IV) requiring 14 Body, providing 10–13 damage and strong combat accuracy.
knight-sword.flavor: Broad-fullered and counterweighted with a heavy faceted pommel designed for armored officers of the Vanguard Company. It cuts cleanly through mail links and turns aside heavy halberds without nicking.

thorn-blade.summary: Tier-5 endgame Warrior weapon from Act IV and Hard+ requiring 17 Body, dealing 14–18 damage with high accuracy.
thorn-blade.flavor: Forged from dark, meteoric border steel etched with subtle briar-veins along the ricasso. Balanced for veteran commanders facing dread knights and titans, every swing lands with lethal, unyielding authority.

oak-staff.summary: Tier-1 Mage weapon from Act I requiring 5 Mind, granting 4 bonus mana and light 0–1 melee damage.
oak-staff.flavor: Cut from a seasoned northern oak branch and capped with a cheap brass ferrule to keep the butt from splitting on gravel. Apprentice casters lean on it during wet marches and channel their first sparks through its grain.

cdx-m39.summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked by inspecting a charred silk blindfold on the portal stairs in Flight of Malrik.
cdx-m39.flavor: Collegium navigators sometimes bind their eyes with smoked silk to read raw ley-currents without being dazzled by volcanic glare. Dropped in haste on the upper steps of Ashveil Gorge, this scorched strip hints at how desperately its wearer ran.

cdx-m40.summary: Act IV relic codex unlocked via a spiked bronze barrel inside the northern crag bastion during Twofold Assault.
cdx-m40.flavor: Cast thick enough to survive twenty heartbeats of sustained arcane pressure before the breech turns cherry-red and threatens its own crew. Iron Pact gunners treat these bronze tubes with nervous respect, keeping wet sandbags piled beside every carriage.

cdx-m41.summary: Act IV place codex unlocked by checking iron filings on the middle portcullis in Gauntlet of Iron.
cdx-m41.flavor: Natural lodestone veins run so dense through these canyon walls that loose belt-knives rattle in their sheaths as you march past. Quartermasters warn heavy infantry to double-check their boot nails before crossing the narrow bridge.

cdx-m42.summary: Act IV place codex unlocked by inspecting severed winch chains in the Center gatehouse of Outer Rampart.
cdx-m42.flavor: Massive iron chains dipped in tallow once raised the drawbridges over the glowing moat channels below the basalt wall. Seeing links thick as a blacksmith's wrist sheared clean through tells any sapper that the defenders expected no retreat.

cdx-m43.summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked via a scorched powder-convoy manifest on the western road in Three-Roads Siege.
cdx-m43.flavor: Half the ink is blistered away, yet the surviving tally shows kegs of blasting powder, spare axles, and winter salt bound for the highland junction. Whoever holds Three-Roads Watch holds the last supply artery feeding the caldera front.

cdx-m44.summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked by inspecting a notched spear-butt beside the central dais in Threshold Choice.
cdx-m44.flavor: The Silent Praetor Phalanx answers no trumpet and speaks no challenge, standing motionless in pale armor until an intruder crosses the inner flagstones. Every deep notch along their spear-butts marks a century of unbroken subterranean duty.

cdx-m45.summary: Act IV relic codex unlocked at the star-etched marble altar rim in Crown of Order, detailing an ancient symbol of law.
cdx-m45.flavor: Pale stonework engraved with pre-schism star-geometry radiates a cold, austere stillness that quiets even the distant rumble of the caldera. Archivists debate whether the altar was built to preserve a realm or merely freeze it in place.

cdx-m46.summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked by inspecting a cracked slag breastplate near the Obsidian Throne in Ember Reckoning.
cdx-m46.flavor: Before modern factions fought over tolls and salt, the First Warden stood watch over the furnace depths in armor poured from volcanic iron. The fractured plate bears no heraldry, only the scorched marks of an impossible vigil.

tavern-rumors.summary: Collection of forty frontier rumors overheard across the hubs, offering clues, gossip, and warnings from the Border.
tavern-rumors.flavor: Half of what you hear over watered ale in Thornwick or vinegar-brine in Redmarsh is drunken invention, and the other half might keep you alive tomorrow. Smart commanders listen quietly, buy one round, and check every rumor against the mud.

chronicle-act-1.summary: Canonical Act I chronicle triggered at Blood at the Ford, opening the frontier campaign across the wet northern border.
chronicle-act-1.flavor: Rain drums steadily against the palisade timbers of Thornwick while gnoll horns echo across the Alder shallows. What begins as a desperate border skirmish soon pulls the Vanguard Company into a tangled ledger of burned mints and unpaid tithes.

chronicle-act-2.summary: Canonical Act II chronicle triggered at Redmarsh Border, marking the march from sunken mires into scorching alkali wastes.
chronicle-act-2.flavor: Beyond Ashbrook Gate the northern grass dies abruptly into blinding red clay and salt-crusted flats. Caravans creak south on the promise of mountain water, guarded by mercenaries who trust their canteens far more than imperial seals.

chronicle-act-4.summary: Canonical Act IV chronicle triggered at Heartland March, introducing the final ascent into the Obsidian Caldera.
chronicle-act-4.flavor: Behind the vanguard lies the gray Western Sea; ahead rises a horizon lit by sulfur vents and black basalt peaks. In the thin, ash-choked air of the highlands, old grievances burn away until only iron and resolve remain.

chronicle-ending-a.summary: Canonical Act IV chronicle for the Path of Order, recording the culmination of the Threshold trial in Crown of Order.
chronicle-ending-a.flavor: Cold marble light meets the roaring heat of the caldera as an ancient standard of law is tested to its breaking point. Whatever emerges from the quiet vault will decide whether Thornvael's scarred valleys ever know a calm morning again.

chronicle-ending-b.summary: Canonical Act IV chronicle for the Path of Ember, recording the fiery culmination of the Threshold trial in Ember Reckoning.
chronicle-ending-b.flavor: Where pale statutes fail, raw volcanic fire offers a harsher, simpler answer forged in white-hot steel and absolute will. Stepping toward the furnace altar means trading fragile peace for a dominion that refuses to bend.

ending-warrior-sovereign.summary: Act IV Warrior campaign epilogue reflecting how a frontline commander shapes the Border after the Threshold.
ending-warrior-sovereign.flavor: A soldier who has held muddy bridges, salt ditches, and burning piers learns to measure peace in solid walls and dry granaries. When the horns finally fall silent, the iron weight of command still rests squarely on broad shoulders.

ending-archer-horizon.summary: Act IV Archer campaign epilogue tracing the frontier path of a marksman after the caldera campaign concludes.
ending-archer-horizon.flavor: Scouts and bowmen never sit comfortably behind palace curtains once the roads clear. With the smoke lifting off the passes, a keen eye naturally turns toward the far ridgeline, checking the wind and counting what lies beyond.

ending-mage-equilibrium.summary: Act IV Mage campaign epilogue detailing how an arcanist balances the fractured ley-lines of the realm.
ending-mage-equilibrium.flavor: Collegium formulas rarely survive contact with a dying continent, yet someone must recalibrate the wards once the tremors subside. Chalk, copper wire, and quiet patience become the tools of a new, hard-won equilibrium.

ending-necromancer-probate.summary: Act IV Necromancer campaign epilogue chronicling how a clerk of bone and debt settles the realm's final accounts.
ending-necromancer-probate.flavor: War leaves behind more than broken walls—it leaves thousands of unclosed ledgers and restless dead waiting for a proper signature. Armed with wax seal and brass scale, the probate arbiter finally brings order to the silent rolls.

sq01-tollhouse-audit.summary: Act I side quest from Captain Garrick in Thornwick, rewarding gold and experience for recovering a lost tollhouse strongbox.
sq01-tollhouse-audit.flavor: Garrick hates losing payroll silver almost as much as he hates losing ground to gnolls. Somewhere in the burned timbers near the river crossing sits a heavy ironbound box whose padlock refuses to yield to ordinary bandits.

sq02-bile-of-the-fen.summary: Act I side quest from Alchemist Marta in Thornwick, paying gold and experience for harvesting potent marsh bile.
sq02-bile-of-the-fen.flavor: Marta's apothecary shelves are nearly bare, and wounded levies need poultices that actually bite back against bog-fever. She needs fresh, foul ingredients scraped from creatures that prefer to keep their insides to themselves.

sq03-broken-picket.summary: Act I side quest offered by Captain Garrick in Thornwick, awarding gold and experience for clearing a compromised picket line.
sq03-broken-picket.flavor: A forward watch-post went silent before dawn without firing a single flare or blowing a horn. Garrick wants boots on the trail to find out what broke the line and sweep the ridge clean before raiders dig in.

sq04-night-cargo.summary: Act I side quest from Ferryman Fenwick in Thornwick, offering gold and experience for tracking missing river freight.
sq04-night-cargo.flavor: Fenwick knows every snag and sandbar on the Alder, which is why he smells foul play when a loaded flatboat vanishes in calm fog. Someone is moving contraband off the books under cover of the curfew.

sq05-the-quartermasters-ledger.summary: Act I side quest from Smith Hobb in Thornwick, rewarding gold and experience for retrieving a missing supply book.
sq05-the-quartermasters-ledger.flavor: Without a stamped tally, Hobb cannot prove how much pig-iron the Salt Tithe took and how much the bailiffs simply pocketed. Finding the lost ledger in the mud could keep the town forge running another month.

sq06-glass-in-the-thicket.summary: Act I side quest from Alchemist Marta in Thornwick, granting gold and experience for gathering vitrified glass shards.
sq06-glass-in-the-thicket.flavor: Strange green splinters have been turning up in the brush near the old kilns, sharp enough to slice through boot leather. Marta suspects the fused slag holds residual ward-charge useful for stabilizing field tonics.

sq07-the-canyon-audit.summary: Act II side quest from Quartermaster Bram in Redmarsh, rewarding gold and experience for accounting lost canyon supplies.
sq07-the-canyon-audit.flavor: Bram refuses to write off three missing wagon-loads of salt-pork without seeing the splinters himself. Someone has to hike into the sun-baked passes, count the wreckage, and drag back whatever the sand raiders left behind.

sq08-rubbings-in-blood.summary: Act II side quest from Scholar Zahra in Redmarsh, paying gold and experience for copying defaced wardstone inscriptions.
sq08-rubbings-in-blood.flavor: Zahra cannot fix the plateau's fractured monoliths without knowing the exact reverse glyphs carved into their bases. Getting close enough to take clean rubbings means wading through crackling static and irritable desert beasts.

sq09-the-bitter-well.summary: Act II side quest from Water-Seller Tull in Redmarsh, awarding gold and experience for investigating a fouled oasis well.
sq09-the-bitter-well.flavor: Tull's customers are already paying silver for muddy brine, and now the main aquifer tastes like copper rot and toad-bile. If the source of the taint is not cleared soon, Redmarsh will have a riot before sundown.

sq10-granary-smokers.summary: Act II side quest from Quartermaster Bram in Redmarsh, offering gold and experience for stopping arsonists targeting grain.
sq10-granary-smokers.flavor: Dry timber stilts and alkali dust burn like tinder if a single fire-pot lands under the granary floor. Bram wants the raiders' pitch-runners hunted down in the ditches before Redmarsh's last flour sacks go up in smoke.

sq11-canopic-tar.summary: Act II side quest from Scholar Zahra in Redmarsh, rewarding gold and experience for recovering Third-Dynasty bitumen.
sq11-canopic-tar.flavor: Ancient embalmers sealed their salt-vaults with a mineral pitch far tougher than modern wagon-grease. Zahra needs fresh samples from the sunken quays to test whether it can insulate cracked quartz conduits.

sq12-empty-waterskins.summary: Act II side quest from Water-Seller Tull in Redmarsh, granting gold and experience for salvaging lost caravan canteens.
sq12-empty-waterskins.flavor: Out on the alkali flats, a stitched goatskin without leaks is worth more than a decorative dagger. Tull pays good coin for intact skins recovered from stranded convoys before the desert sun bakes them brittle.

sq13-the-triage-wagon.summary: Act III side quest from Healer Sera in Oakhaven, paying gold and experience for rescuing a stranded medical cart.
sq13-the-triage-wagon.flavor: A covered cart packed with clean linen, bone-saws, and willow-bark broke an axle on the coastal road while raiders closed in. Sera refuses to abandon the supplies when her infirmary tents are already overflowing.

sq14-the-mountain-convoy.summary: Act III side quest from Shipwright Kors in Oakhaven, awarding gold and experience for securing highland timber deliveries.
sq14-the-mountain-convoy.flavor: You cannot lay a caravel keel out of rotten driftwood, and Kors needs seasoned ironwood beams hauled down from the upper ridge. Clearing the ambushes along the logging grade keeps the slipways hammering.

sq15-the-bell-tower-picket.summary: Act III side quest from Warden Lyra in Oakhaven, rewarding gold and experience for reclaiming a coastal lookout tower.
sq15-the-bell-tower-picket.flavor: With fog rolling thick off the Western Sea, a blind harbor is a dead harbor. Lyra needs the high bell-tower swept clear of hostile scouts so her watchmen can spot approaching sails and fires.

sq16-low-tide-salvage.summary: Act III side quest from Mudlark Pip in Oakhaven, offering gold and experience for looting wrecks before the tide turns.
sq16-low-tide-salvage.flavor: Pip knows every broken hull wedged along the shingle flats, though he prefers letting someone in iron armor deal with the salt crabs. Grab the brass fittings while the mud is exposed, or swim for them.

sq17-silencing-the-orchard.summary: Act III side quest from Healer Sera in Oakhaven, granting gold and experience for culling blighted coastal trees.
sq17-silencing-the-orchard.flavor: Blighted cider trees along the upper terrace have begun dropping toxic spores straight into the town's rain-barrels. Sera needs axes and fire taken to the twisted grove before the harbor garrison falls sick.

sq18-pitch-for-the-fire-ships.summary: Act III side quest from Shipwright Kors in Oakhaven, paying gold and experience for securing barrels of naval pitch.
sq18-pitch-for-the-fire-ships.flavor: Old hulks packed with tar and dry oakum are the cheapest way to break a hostile blockade at the harbor mouth. Kors needs every intact cask hauled out of the contested coastal yards before raiders torch them.

sq19-iron-on-the-wall.summary: Act IV side quest from Commander Rowan in Ironcamp, awarding gold and experience for reinforcing battered ramparts.
sq19-iron-on-the-wall.flavor: Greystone's curtain wall has taken enough basalt boulders to rattle every tooth in the garrison. Rowan needs heavy iron tie-plates carried up to the breach before the next Iron Pact cohort arrives.

sq20-the-unquenched-jaw.summary: Act IV side quest from Forgemaster Vok in Ironcamp, rewarding gold and experience for hunting a fiery foundry threat.
sq20-the-unquenched-jaw.flavor: Something big and red-hot has been nesting inside the abandoned slag-pit, chewing through Vok's best ironstone ore. Clear out the beast so the foundrymen can relight the main bellows without losing an arm.

sq21-the-burnt-syllabus.summary: Act IV side quest from Penitent Elias in Ironcamp, offering gold and experience for recovering charred arcane texts.
sq21-the-burnt-syllabus.flavor: Even heretical Collegium notes contain useful warnings when you are marching straight into a volcanic sanctuary. Elias wants the half-burned folios gathered from the ash-drifts before the wind scatters them.

sq22-thunder-on-the-glacis.summary: Act IV side quest from Commander Rowan in Ironcamp, granting gold and experience for silencing enemy bombardment.
sq22-thunder-on-the-glacis.flavor: Hostile siege engines dug in along the outer slope are chewing up the approach road day and night. Rowan pays well for a quick raid that spikes the barrels and scatters the crews.

sq23-slag-trench-convoy.summary: Act IV side quest from Forgemaster Vok in Ironcamp, paying gold and experience for escorting ore through volcanic flats.
sq23-slag-trench-convoy.flavor: Meteoric iron does not walk itself up to the anvil, and the mule trains hauling billets across the slag trenches keep losing guards. Keep the carts rolling so Highcrest's smiths never run dry.

sq24-the-choir-in-the-nave.summary: Act IV side quest from Penitent Elias in Ironcamp, awarding top gold and experience for quieting a haunted inner hall.
sq24-the-choir-in-the-nave.flavor: A cold, rhythmic droning echoes up from a collapsed subterranean nave near the Threshold, rattling the nerves of every sentry on watch. Elias asks for steel and resolve to lay the restless chorus to rest.

sq25-weir-eel-traps.summary: Act I side quest from Ferryman Fenwick in Thornwick, rewarding gold and experience for salvaging iron from river weirs.
sq25-weir-eel-traps.flavor: When gnolls tore apart the willow eel-traps down at the bend, half a dozen good iron chains went straight into the mud. Fenwick wants them dragged back before the current buries them for good.

sq26-cold-hearth-coal.summary: Act I side quest from Smith Hobb in Thornwick, paying gold and experience for hauling fresh coal to the town forge.
sq26-cold-hearth-coal.flavor: Wet alder wood makes plenty of smoke and almost no heat, which is useless for hammering out pike-heads. Hobb needs dry charcoal sacks recovered from the abandoned timber camps before his fire dies.

sq27-rue-for-the-grey-itch.summary: Act I side quest from Alchemist Marta in Thornwick, offering gold and experience for gathering medicinal border herbs.
sq27-rue-for-the-grey-itch.flavor: Standing knee-deep in cold river muck gives half the garrison a blistering rash that ruins a soldier's grip. Marta needs fresh bitter rue clipped from the dry bluffs to boil down a proper salve.

sq28-broken-axle-on-alder-road.summary: Act I side quest from Captain Garrick in Thornwick, awarding gold and experience for salvaging a wrecked supply cart.
sq28-broken-axle-on-alder-road.flavor: A loaded ration wagon snapped its rear beam half a mile south of the palisade, spilling oats and iron nails into the ditch. Garrick wants the freight hauled back before briar-hounds claim it.

sq29-salt-crust-beacons.summary: Act II side quest from Warden Hale in Redmarsh, rewarding gold and experience for relighting desert trail markers.
sq29-salt-crust-beacons.flavor: Alkali fog turns the salt-pans into a white blindfold where a patrol can walk in circles until its water runs out. Hale needs the oil-pots along the outer ridge scraped clean and lit again.

sq30-jawbone-wind-chimes.summary: Act II side quest from Scholar Zahra in Redmarsh, paying gold and experience for studying bone wards on the flats.
sq30-jawbone-wind-chimes.flavor: Desert hexers string bleached animal jaws across canyon mouths to rattle warnings whenever patrols pass beneath. Zahra wants several intact chimes collected so she can trace their resonant markings.

sq31-brine-barrel-reckoning.summary: Act II side quest from Water-Seller Tull in Redmarsh, offering gold and experience for recovering stolen water casks.
sq31-brine-barrel-reckoning.flavor: Raiders slipped past the lower stilts at night and rolled four iron-hooped barrels straight into the reeds. Tull does not care how many bandits you drop, so long as the staves come back unsplit.

sq32-vinegar-for-highgate.summary: Act II side quest from Quartermaster Bram in Redmarsh, awarding gold and experience for delivering sour brine-purifiers.
sq32-vinegar-for-highgate.flavor: Highgate's cisterns are growing green scum in the noon heat, and plain boiled water no longer sits right in the gut. Bram needs jugs of sharp vinegar run up the trail before dysentery empties the wall.

sq33-quartz-splinter-harvest.summary: Act II side quest from Alchemist Marta in Redmarsh, rewarding gold and experience for collecting charged crystal chips.
sq33-quartz-splinter-harvest.flavor: Following the army south taught Marta that desert quartz holds a far cleaner spark than northern slag. She pays well for hand-sized splinters knocked loose around the humming plateau spires.

sq34-pit-prop-timbers.summary: Act II side quest from Miner Tomas in Redmarsh, paying gold and experience for securing heavy quarry support beams.
sq34-pit-prop-timbers.flavor: The third basalt terrace groans every time a heavy cart rolls past, and half the old cedar props are split by dry rot. Tomas needs sound timbers hauled down before the gallery seals itself.

sq35-milestone-dispatch.summary: Act II side quest from Warden Hale in Redmarsh, granting gold and experience for inspecting the Four-Faced Milestone.
sq35-milestone-dispatch.flavor: Two couriers took the eastern fork last week and vanished without a trace. Hale suspects someone tampered with the old crossroads obelisk and wants a sharp pair of eyes on its carved faces.

sq36-caulking-oakum.summary: Act III side quest from Shipwright Kors in Oakhaven, rewarding gold and experience for gathering hemp hull-caulking.
sq36-caulking-oakum.flavor: A seaworthy hull leaks like a basket without miles of tarred hemp driven tight between every plank. Kors needs dry oakum bales recovered from the overrun rope-walks along the cliff road.

sq37-fumarole-glass.summary: Act III side quest from Healer Sera in Oakhaven, paying gold and experience for harvesting clean volcanic glass.
sq37-fumarole-glass.flavor: When steel scalpels dull and rust in the coastal salt air, freshly fractured fumarole glass cuts cleaner than any guild blade. Sera needs unchipped pieces gathered from the smoking vents inland.

sq38-semaphore-codebooks.summary: Act III side quest from Warden Lyra in Oakhaven, awarding gold and experience for recovering lost coastal signal books.
sq38-semaphore-codebooks.flavor: If blockade captains learn Harborwatch's flag-codes, they can lure incoming transports straight onto the shingle reefs. Lyra needs the missing signal slates pulled from fallen watch-posts immediately.

sq39-undertow-chains.summary: Act III side quest from the Harbor Pilot in Oakhaven, offering gold and experience for clearing fouled boom-chains.
sq39-undertow-chains.flavor: Heavy iron harbor chains are tangled with wreck-timber and crawling with armored sea-beasts at the cove mouth. Freeing the links lets the evacuation ships slip out on the evening tide.

sq40-mill-wheel-grease.summary: Act III side quest from Mudlark Pip in Oakhaven, rewarding gold and experience for delivering tallow to coastal mills.
sq40-mill-wheel-grease.flavor: Dry wooden gears scream loud enough to draw raiders from a mile away and snap teeth when grinding emergency flour. Pip pays handsomely for tubs of clean mutton tallow hauled to the mill-house.

sq41-lodestone-compasses.summary: Act III side quest from the Harbor Pilot in Oakhaven, paying gold and experience for retrieving magnetized ship needles.
sq41-lodestone-compasses.flavor: Sailing west into zero-visibility ash-fog without a true needle is just a slow way to drown. The pilot needs intact lodestone compasses salvaged from wrecked coastal cutters before the fleet weighs anchor.

sq42-barons-cellar-keys.summary: Act III side quest from Mudlark Pip in Oakhaven, granting gold and experience for finding keys to Baron Vane's vaults.
sq42-barons-cellar-keys.flavor: Everyone on the docks knows Baron Vane hoarded salted beef and lamp oil behind thick oak doors while refugees starved. Pip has a plan to redistribute the cellar, provided someone lifts the iron keys first.

sq43-sulfur-crust-markers.summary: Act IV side quest from the Ash-Scout in Ironcamp, rewarding gold and experience for staking safe highland trails.
sq43-sulfur-crust-markers.flavor: Yellow sulfur crusts look solid until a horse's hoof punches straight through into a boiling steam-pocket. Driving iron marker-stakes along the firm basalt ridges saves the next column from a grim surprise.

sq44-prism-dust-for-the-anvil.summary: Act IV side quest from Forgemaster Vok in Ironcamp, paying gold and experience for gathering crushed beacon crystal.
sq44-prism-dust-for-the-anvil.flavor: Sprinkling fine crystal dust onto white-hot meteoric iron draws out impurities that ordinary charcoal flux cannot touch. Vok wants sacks of ground prism shards swept up from the shattered highland towers.

sq45-pumice-mortar-breach.summary: Act IV side quest from the Siege Sapper in Ironcamp, awarding gold and experience for hauling volcanic mortar.
sq45-pumice-mortar-breach.flavor: Ordinary lime cracks the first time a caldera tremor shakes the parapet, whereas pumice mortar bends and holds. Bringing fresh barrels up to the sappers keeps the forward redoubt standing.

sq46-ashveil-cleft-wardens.summary: Act IV side quest from Penitent Elias in Ironcamp, offering gold and experience for clearing hostile sentinels.
sq46-ashveil-cleft-wardens.flavor: Silent armored figures have been blocking the narrow ash-drifts of the gorge, turning back supply runners without a word. Elias asks for a disciplined push to open the cleft.

sq47-magnetic-vein-spikes.summary: Act IV side quest from Commander Rowan in Ironcamp, granting gold and experience for grounding lodestone cliffs.
sq47-magnetic-vein-spikes.flavor: Driving heavy copper spikes into the magnetic rock faces bleeds off the pull that yanks iron weapons out of soldiers' hands. Rowan needs a squad to hammer them home under sniper fire.

sq48-ashes-of-the-first-watch.summary: Act IV side quest from Penitent Elias in Ironcamp, paying high gold and experience for recovering ancient watch relics.
sq48-ashes-of-the-first-watch.flavor: Scattered across the caldera approaches lie iron urns belonging to the forgotten sentinels who first guarded the Threshold. Elias believes returning their ashes to consecrated stone will steady the vanguard's nerve.

sq49-rusted-toll-chain.summary: Act I frontier side quest from the Ford Tollkeeper, rewarding gold and experience for clearing a jammed river chain.
sq49-rusted-toll-chain.flavor: The heavy iron chain stretched across the Alder shallows rusted solid after the last raid, blocking friendly boats while letting raiders wade right over it. Someone needs to break the padlock and clear the bank.

sq50-peat-spade-salvage.summary: Act I frontier side quest from the Fen Peat-Cutter, paying gold and experience for retrieving lost bog tools.
sq50-peat-spade-salvage.flavor: Good iron-shod turf spades are impossible to replace since the Salt Tithe emptied the smithies. The cutters dropped their whole rack in the reeds when mire wisps chased them off the boardwalk.

sq51-cellar-tally-books.summary: Act I frontier side quest from Captain Garrick, offering gold and experience for recovering mildewed muster rolls.
sq51-cellar-tally-books.flavor: Without the old cellar muster-books, Thornwick's bailiffs cannot tell which levies deserted and which ones died holding the fords. Garrick wants the damp rolls pulled out of the ruined watch-house.

sq52-tallow-for-lantern-pass.summary: Act I frontier side quest from the Ashbrook Watchman, awarding gold and experience for delivering lamp tallow.
sq52-tallow-for-lantern-pass.flavor: The third lantern-post along the foggy pass has been burning down to bare wick for two nights straight. Hauling a fresh tub of mutton tallow through the mist keeps the road from going completely blind.

sq53-crosscut-blades.summary: Act I frontier side quest from the Greywood Sawyer, rewarding gold and experience for reclaiming stolen saw blades.
sq53-crosscut-blades.flavor: Two-man steel crosscut saws take a master smith a week to tooth, and raiders carried off the mill's last three blades. Without them, Thornwick cannot cut fresh palisade logs before winter.

sq54-sleet-cairn-oil.summary: Act I frontier side quest from the Ravenwatch Runner, paying gold and experience for supplying ridge signal cairns.
sq54-sleet-cairn-oil.flavor: Freezing sleet snuffs out ordinary wood-fires on Craghorn Ridge within ten minutes. Pitch-soaked rags and oil jugs keep the warning cairns blazing so the valley knows when raiders cross.

sq55-chalk-bluff-stakes.summary: Act I frontier side quest from Captain Garrick, offering gold and experience for planting sharpened stakes on Alder Bluff.
sq55-chalk-bluff-stakes.flavor: Charging thorn-boars and pack rushers love the smooth slope above the river road. Hammering a row of fire-hardened ash stakes into the chalk turns their favorite ambush lane into a butcher's fence.

sq56-green-slag-cullets.summary: Act I frontier side quest from Alchemist Marta, granting gold and experience for gathering fused furnace cullets.
sq56-green-slag-cullets.flavor: Around the vitrified kilns, melted bronze and sand cooled into dense green lumps that hum faintly in wet weather. Marta needs a clean sackful to test how the kilns were fired so hot.

sq57-turnip-ditch-relics.summary: Act I frontier side quest from Smith Hobb, rewarding gold and experience for recovering stamped levy tags.
sq57-turnip-ditch-relics.flavor: Hobb stamped every northern recruit's iron neck-tag himself before they marched out to the turnip fields. Bringing the lost tags back lets families close their grief and lets Hobb cross names off his wall.

sq58-weir-pike-heads.summary: Act I frontier side quest from Smith Hobb, paying gold and experience for salvaging bent iron pike-heads.
sq58-weir-pike-heads.flavor: Scrap iron is worth its weight in bread on the northern border, and the muddy banks of Sunken Ford are littered with snapped polearms. Haul the bent heads back so Hobb can hammer them straight.

sq59-whale-rib-rawhide.summary: Act II frontier side quest from Warden Hale, awarding gold and experience for delivering rawhide lashing.
sq59-whale-rib-rawhide.flavor: Dry alkali wind shrinks and snaps the leather lashings holding Redmarsh's giant jawbone gate together. Freshly soaked rawhide strips tighten like iron hoops once they bake in the desert sun.

sq60-sniper-blind-tallies.summary: Act II frontier side quest from Scholar Zahra, offering gold and experience for inspecting canyon sniper nests.
sq60-sniper-blind-tallies.flavor: Desert hornbowmen leave behind charred signal-ash and notched range-sticks inside their cliffside blinds. Zahra wants samples from the eastern crag to determine who is supplying their powder and arrows.

sq61-hoodoo-signal-mirrors.summary: Act II frontier side quest from the Alkali Drover, rewarding gold and experience for salvaging broken heliographs.
sq61-hoodoo-signal-mirrors.flavor: Polished brass mirrors flash caravan warnings across ten miles of flat salt-pan in a single heartbeat. Raiders smashed the ridge stands, leaving valuable reflector plates scattered in the dust.

sq62-arroyo-firepot-oil.summary: Act II frontier side quest from Quartermaster Bram, paying gold and experience for securing intact naphtha jars.
sq62-arroyo-firepot-oil.flavor: Clay pots of desert fire-oil are nasty to carry in a bouncing saddlebag, yet nothing clears out a dune-lurker nest faster. Bram pays well for unbroken jars lifted from raider caches.

sq63-copper-horn-capacitors.summary: Act II frontier side quest from the Wardstone Surveyor, granting gold and experience for recovering monolith fittings.
sq63-copper-horn-capacitors.flavor: Flared copper horns bolted to the plateau obelisks bleed off excess storm-charge before the quartz cracks. Salvaging intact horns from the fractured spires keeps Redmarsh's remaining wards grounded.

sq64-bitter-well-skimming.summary: Act II frontier side quest from the Cistern Guard, awarding gold and experience for clearing fouled surface scum.
sq64-bitter-well-skimming.flavor: A thick, oily crust has settled over the milestone well, choking the buckets and sickening patrol mules. Skimming the taint while fending off thirsty desert beasts keeps the road passable.

sq65-redrock-silver-scales.summary: Act II frontier side quest from Water-Seller Tull, offering gold and experience for recovering assay balances.
sq65-redrock-silver-scales.flavor: In a town where silver buys water and clipped coin starts knife-fights, honest brass scales are priceless. Tull wants the precision balances rescued from the abandoned Redrock assay vault.

sq66-megalith-cauldron-soot.summary: Act II frontier side quest from Alchemist Marta, rewarding gold and experience for scraping ritual bitumen.
sq66-megalith-cauldron-soot.flavor: Around the Twelve Stones, desert hexers burned strange mineral tars that left a greasy black crust on the rock. Marta needs fresh scrapings to brew a counter-agent against bog-curses.

sq67-quarry-chain-keys.summary: Act II frontier side quest from Miner Tomas, paying gold and experience for lifting overseer shackle keys.
sq67-quarry-chain-keys.flavor: Cold-chiseling iron collars off exhausted miners takes half an hour and risks a broken collarbone. Taking the heavy iron key-rings straight off the third terrace guards frees dozens in minutes.

sq68-milestone-glyph-chisels.summary: Act II frontier side quest from Warden Hale, granting gold and experience for correcting defaced road markers.
