sq68-milestone-glyph-chisels.flavor: Someone hammered the safe-water arrows backward at the crossroads to steer green patrols into alkali quicksand. Bringing stone-chisels out to recut the true bearings saves the next relief column.

sq69-salt-crab-carapaces.summary: Act III frontier side quest from Shipwright Kors, awarding gold and experience for harvesting tough coastal shells.
sq69-salt-crab-carapaces.flavor: Thick, curved crab shells boiled in vinegar and bolted to ash frames make surprisingly sturdy pavises for boarding crews. Kors pays good silver for unbroken carapaces hauled off the tide-flats.

sq70-fumarole-sulfur-cakes.summary: Act III frontier side quest from Healer Sera, offering gold and experience for collecting sulfur deposits.
sq70-fumarole-sulfur-cakes.flavor: Burning yellow sulfur cakes in iron braziers keeps spore-matron clouds and biting marsh-flies out of the surgical tents. Sera needs fresh chunks pried from the smoking coastal vents.

sq71-split-tooth-cages.summary: Act III frontier side quest from Warden Lyra, rewarding gold and experience for breaking coastal prisoner cages.
sq71-split-tooth-cages.flavor: Raiders strung iron gibbet-cages along the Split Tooth crags to hold captured scouts and harbor pilots for ransom. Shattering the chains before the tide rises brings experienced hands back to Oakhaven.

sq72-chapel-linen-bales.summary: Act III frontier side quest from the Oakhaven Surgeon, paying gold and experience for delivering boiled bandage linen.
sq72-chapel-linen-bales.flavor: Clean, boiled cloth is rarer than gold plate inside the coastal chapel nave after three days of heavy skirmishing. Hauling fresh linen bales through the tree line keeps wounded veterans from losing limbs.

book-night-orchard-herbal.summary: Herbalist Maren's Act III field report from the Cider Orchard, documenting how coastal blight twisted the fruit trees.
book-night-orchard-herbal.flavor: Pressed between the stained pages are blackened apple blossoms that still crumble like soot when touched. Maren traces the rot from the lower irrigation ditches up into the terraces, noting with grim precision the exact week the roots first pulled free of the soil.

book-ironcamp-forge-rules.summary: Smelting ordinances written by Forgemaster Vok in Act IV Ironcamp, detailing heat quotas and foundry discipline.
book-ironcamp-forge-rules.flavor: Nailed to the main bellows-post with iron spikes because ordinary paste peeled off in the smelter heat. Vok lists the penalties for quenching star-iron in dirty water, leaving slag troughs unskimmed, or arguing with a senior smith while holding tongs.

book-heartland-road-survey.summary: Outrider Captain Bren's Act IV mile-log from Heartland March, charting ash drifts and ambushes along the basalt highway.
book-heartland-road-survey.flavor: Crisp, dusty entries scribbled in the saddle whenever the horses stopped to clear volcanic grit from their nostrils. Bren marks every broken culvert, sulfur fissure, and burned waystation between Highcrest and the northern ridge with soldierly thrift.

book-beacon-treason-confession.summary: Watchman Galt's Act IV testimony found in Shattered Beacons, explaining how the highland signal grid was compromised.
book-beacon-treason-confession.flavor: Written on the back of a ration chit with a blunt charcoal stub while Galt waited for a relief patrol that never came. He admits taking silver to tilt the focusing mirrors off-axis, swearing he was told it would only blind merchant spies.

book-besieged-wall-tally.summary: Engineer Haldor's Act IV structural log from Besieged Wall, recording masonry fractures along the outer curtain.
book-besieged-wall-tally.flavor: Column after column of mortar weights, cracked merlons, and timber bracing tallies kept through three days of ceaseless bombardment. Haldor's neat margin notes dryly observe that pumice stone absorbs impact well right up until the moment it turns to powder.

book-malrik-stolen-syllabus.summary: Annotated Act IV syllabus by Arch-Mage Malrik found in Flight of Malrik, outlining forbidden caldera channeling.
book-malrik-stolen-syllabus.flavor: Every printed Collegium theorem is slashed through with furious violet ink and replaced by blunt, ruthless corrections. Reading the margins feels like listening to a brilliant man lose his patience with caution one page at a time.

book-twofold-breach-plan.summary: Marshal Corin's Act IV assault orders from Twofold Assault, mapping synchronized strikes against the twin chasm gates.
book-twofold-breach-plan.flavor: Creased along the folds and smudged with oil from a field-lantern, these orders leave no room for hesitation on the suspension bridges. Corin warns his officers that taking one crag without pinning the other merely turns the crossing into a shooting gallery.

book-gauntlet-trench-diagram.summary: Ember Tactician Vael's Act IV fortification sketch from Gauntlet of Iron, detailing kill-zones and pitch trenches.
book-gauntlet-trench-diagram.flavor: Drawn with cold geometric relish on heavy waxed vellum that shrugs off soot and rain alike. Vael angles every parapet and mortar pit so advancing vanguard troops have nowhere to kneel without catching crossfire from the cliffs.

book-outer-rampart-soot-note.summary: Centurion Draven's Act IV standing orders recovered at Outer Rampart, governing watch rotations along the basalt glacis.
book-outer-rampart-soot-note.flavor: Blunt garrison rules written for men who sleep in their armor and eat cold hardbread under falling cinders. Draven forbids lighting cooking fires on the wall, reminding his sentries that the caldera glow already gives snipers plenty to aim at.

book-three-roads-dispatch.summary: Commander Thorne's Act IV siege log from Three-Roads Siege, tracking supply shortages and converging enemy columns.
book-three-roads-dispatch.flavor: Short, clipped dispatches stamped at hourly intervals as dust clouds rise along all three highland approaches at once. Thorne counts powder kegs, horseshoes, and unbroken halberds with the calm of an officer who intends to sell every yard dearly.

book-threshold-headless-kings.summary: Chronicler Zahra's Act IV epigraphic study from Threshold Choice, translating weathered carvings of ancient monarchs.
book-threshold-headless-kings.flavor: Charcoal rubbings reveal rows of sculpted rulers whose crowns were chiseled clean off their brows centuries before the current war. Zahra notes that whoever defaced the stonework did not act in rage—they worked with neat, patient mason's tools.

book-crown-colonnade-roll.summary: Imperial Herald Vex's Act IV ledger found in Crown of Order, enumerating ancient campaigns and tribute decrees.
book-crown-colonnade-roll.flavor: Inscribed in stiff ceremonial script that treats conquered provinces like entries in a grain inventory. Vex records exact bushels, iron ingots, and sworn oaths collected from border towns whose names no longer appear on any living map.

book-caldera-heart-testament.summary: First Warden Ashkarath's Act IV writ from Ember Reckoning, setting down the harsh philosophy of the furnace wardens.
book-caldera-heart-testament.flavor: Cut into thin sheets of dark bronze because ordinary parchment curls to ash inside the lower galleries. The testament reads less like a prayer and more like an ironfounder's manual, weighing mortal endurance against the heat required to purify it.

book-magnetic-canyon-warning.summary: Sapper Captain Orin's Act IV field survey from Magnetic Canyon, warning troops about lodestone veins pulling iron gear.
book-magnetic-canyon-warning.flavor: Orin advises every soldier entering the narrows to strap down loose daggers, leave spare horseshoes behind, and keep compasses in their pockets. Two mules reportedly bolted after their bit-chains snapped straight onto a cliff face.

book-west-beacon-prism-log.summary: Adept Solis's Act IV optical readings from West Beacon Crag, charting refraction angles across the smoky plateau.
book-west-beacon-prism-log.flavor: Dense tables of crystal alignment, midday glare, and copper-wire drift recorded during the final calm month before the grid broke. Solis complains repeatedly that highland winds rattle the mirror frames faster than apprentices can shim them.

book-anchor-seal-rubbing.summary: Act IV architectural rubbing by Chronicler Zahra from the Threshold Nave, documenting the seventh anchor valve.
book-anchor-seal-rubbing.flavor: Fine charcoal dust picks out interlocking rings of First-Dynasty script that match neither imperial law nor Collegium wardcraft. Zahra's hurried postscript observes that the valve housing was built to be turned from the inside, never sealed forever.

cdx-first-compact.summary: Act I lore codex unlocked at the Sunken Ford boundary stone, introducing the founding treaty of the northern border.
cdx-first-compact.flavor: Long before salt-tithe bailiffs rode north with iron shackles, three frontier barons met beside the Alder shallows to carve a plain promise into granite. The stone still stands half-buried in nettles, though few living clerks bother to read its terms.

cdx-salt-tithe.summary: Act I lore codex unlocked via a Border Mint tax writ, detailing the Crown's punishing wartime extraction levy.
cdx-salt-tithe.flavor: Sold to the northern parishes as a temporary emergency measure to shore up southern walls, the Salt Tithe quickly stripped barns, smithies, and strongboxes clean. Quartermasters weigh silver, iron, and grain on the same merciless scale.

cdx-wardstone-lattice.summary: Act II lore codex unlocked by inspecting a ruptured obelisk, explaining the quartz spires that steady Redmarsh.
cdx-wardstone-lattice.flavor: Built across the high plateau to break alkali storms and keep caravan roads passable, the three quartz monoliths hummed quietly for generations. Without steady copper grounding and clean runes, the desert reclaims its wind in a single afternoon.

cdx-third-dynasty-liens.summary: Act II lore codex unlocked from a Redmarsh funerary tablet, outlining ancient probate law that outlasts death.
cdx-third-dynasty-liens.flavor: Third-Dynasty magistrates considered dying an unconvincing excuse to default on silver owed to the treasury. Under their statutes, copper wire and stamped bitumen tablets kept a debtor's service active inside the salt vaults long after his funeral.

cdx-age-of-chains.summary: Act III lore codex unlocked after felling an Elder Juggernaut, recounting the ancient era of bound stone titans.
cdx-age-of-chains.flavor: Old highland ballads speak of artificers who shackled living rock to mountain cairns with iron-runed collars to guard passes without paying wages. Centuries of quiet rain rusted the chains, leaving the mountains full of irritable sleepers.

cdx-whale-oil-monopoly.summary: Act III lore codex unlocked at a burned Harborwatch pier, tracing how coastal charters controlled frontier lantern oil.
cdx-whale-oil-monopoly.flavor: Every fog-lantern from Fenwick Peat to Oakhaven's lighthouses depended on casks boiled down along the Western Sea. When guild factors hoarded the oil to drive up winter prices, inland crossings went dark one road-post at a time.

cdx-anchor-seals.summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked by reading an Anchor Seal inscription, explaining the ancient locks holding the caldera.
cdx-anchor-seals.flavor: Massive rings of star-iron and pale stone buried beneath the basalt peaks to bleed tectonic pressure harmlessly into the crust. Modern scholars can copy the outer markings, yet nobody alive remembers how to forge a replacement valve.

cdx-crown-of-order.summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked at the Threshold silver door, examining the austere First-Dynasty doctrine of immutable law.
cdx-crown-of-order.flavor: Carved into pale marble where dust never seems to settle, the doctrine argues that chaos is the sole author of human misery. Its keepers prized stillness above comfort, willing to freeze an entire realm rather than watch it fracture.

cdx-primal-ember.summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked near the molten seal in the Threshold, detailing the volcanic doctrine of cleansing fire.
cdx-primal-ember.flavor: Opposed in every syllable to the cold marble of Order, the Ember treatises view decay as a sickness cured only by white heat. Smelters and fanatics alike quote its lines whenever soft compromises fail under pressure.

cdx-ley-thermodynamics.summary: Act II lore codex unlocked through mages or Zahra, explaining how Collegium scholars measure mana as heat and pressure.
cdx-ley-thermodynamics.flavor: Frontier arcanists have little patience for poetic talk about spirits and starlight; they treat ley-lines like steam pipes that burst when over-pressured. Keep your circuits grounded and your margins wide, or your own staff will cook your knuckles.

cdx-mortuary-accounting.summary: Act I lore codex unlocked by witnessing spirit binding, detailing how parish clerks balance debt-rolls past the grave.
cdx-mortuary-accounting.flavor: In the lower parishes, a necromancer rarely wears dramatic black robes—he wears ink-stained sleeves and carries a brass scale. Every raised skeleton is logged by name, shift, and remaining balance until its tally finally clears.

cdx-schism-of-ash.summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked via Malrik's syllabus cylinders, tracing the bitter ideological split inside the Collegium.
cdx-schism-of-ash.flavor: What began as a dry faculty dispute over caldera survey numbers ended in burned libraries, expelled fellows, and stolen cipher-keys. Half the scholars fled toward the coastal fleet; the rest marched inland to study the fire up close.

cdx-thornwick-market.summary: Act I place codex unlocked upon entering Thornwick Market, profiling the palisaded river hub of the northern front.
cdx-thornwick-market.flavor: Tucked inside a muddy bend of the Alder River, Thornwick was built to trade timber, eels, and salt-pork rather than anchor a war. Between the ringing smithy, the crowded tavern, and the bailiff's hall, it remains the last dry roof for leagues.

cdx-alder-span.summary: Act I place codex unlocked by defending Alder Bridge, describing the three-arched stone crossing over the border river.
cdx-alder-span.flavor: Constructed from dressed grey granite anchored to twin ancient ley-piers, Alder Bridge is the only road capable of carrying heavy grain wagons south. Hold its arches and the northern parishes breathe; lose them and the river turns into a trap.

cdx-undervault-galleries.summary: Act I place codex unlocked upon descending into the Undervault, detailing the old dwarven drainage tunnels.
cdx-undervault-galleries.flavor: Cut cleanly beneath the southern ridges to keep spring meltwater from washing out the border highway. Centuries of neglect left the lead grates clogged with silt, turning dry service corridors into damp ambush alleys.

cdx-ashbrook-manor.summary: Act I place codex unlocked after surviving Ashbrook, profiling the fortified southern gatehouse facing the wastes.
cdx-ashbrook-manor.flavor: Once a proud toll-manor inspecting caravans bound for the wet northern pastures, Ashbrook's iron doors mark the sharp line where grass yields to red clay. Sentries stationed on its wall always keep wet rags handy for southern dust.

cdx-redmarsh-outpost.summary: Act II place codex unlocked on arriving at Redmarsh Stockade, describing the stilted desert hub above alkali flats.
cdx-redmarsh-outpost.flavor: Hoisted thirty feet clear of the boot-eating brine on limestone pilings and lashed to bleached leviathan ribs. Everything in Redmarsh creaks in the dry wind, and a polite greeting matters far less than whether you brought clean water.

cdx-plateau-spires.summary: Act II place codex unlocked upon climbing the Quartz Plateau, profiling the high tableland of climate obelisks.
cdx-plateau-spires.flavor: Blinding white limestone stretches flat toward the horizon, broken only by three fractured quartz pillars that hum loud enough to ache in the teeth. When the spires fall out of tune, alkali gales strip paint straight off wagon boards.

cdx-deep-quarry.summary: Act II place codex unlocked by liberating the terraces, describing the stepped basalt mine worked by northern debtors.
cdx-deep-quarry.flavor: Three sheer tiers cut deep into black ironstone, echoing day and night with sledgehammers, wooden crane winches, and iron collars. Half the fortifications in the South were built from stone pried out of this dusty pit.

cdx-fork-of-spears.summary: Act II place codex unlocked upon storming Ironheart Bastion, profiling the twin bridges guarding the mountain gates.
cdx-fork-of-spears.flavor: Two razor-thin stone causeways span a mile-deep gorge where freezing mist vents from rusted mountain pipes. Imperial engineers designed the approaches so a handful of armored men could hold back an entire starving province.

cdx-oakhaven-bastion.summary: Act III place codex unlocked upon entering Oakhaven, describing the cliffside timber port overlooking the Western Sea.
cdx-oakhaven-bastion.flavor: Ringed by ancient ironwood groves that built half the Crown's merchant fleet, Oakhaven smells perpetually of pine sap, oakum, and salt spray. Its stone bailiff's gate now serves as the main funnel for inland survivors seeking the coast.

cdx-sunken-citadel.summary: Act III place codex unlocked by breaching the water-gate, profiling the half-submerged fortress carved into sea-caves.
cdx-sunken-citadel.flavor: Built when the Western Sea sat ten feet lower, this slate stronghold now floods twice daily through corroded iron grates. Barnacle-crusted ramparts and knee-deep courtyards turn every advance into a treacherous race against the tide.

cdx-harborwatch-mole.summary: Act III place codex unlocked by retaking the seawalls, describing the granite fortress-harbor and war-docks.
cdx-harborwatch-mole.flavor: Massive breakwaters, heavy iron boom-chains, and swinging timber cranes project straight into the gray swells. Harborwatch is the last working anchorage on the Iron Coast, holding open the sea-lanes while inland roads burn.

cdx-obsidian-dais.summary: Act IV place codex unlocked upon reaching the Threshold Chamber, profiling the ancient subterranean hall of choice.
cdx-obsidian-dais.flavor: Deep beneath the caldera's outer ramparts, volcanic roar fades into an oppressive, echoing hush. Twin platforms of pale marble and glowing basalt face each other across the flagstones, waiting without haste for a mortal verdict.

cdx-thornwick-levy.summary: Act I faction codex unlocked via Sergeant Garrick, detailing the stubborn border militia holding the northern roads.
cdx-thornwick-levy.flavor: Farmers, sawyers, and river-ferrymen handed pitted pikes and told to look fierce whenever raiders cross the fords. They grumble about late wages and wet boots, yet when their own roofs are at stake, few regulars stand firmer.

cdx-salt-tithe-collectors.summary: Act I faction codex unlocked after clashing with bailiffs, profiling the Crown's ruthless fiscal extraction corps.
cdx-salt-tithe-collectors.flavor: Backed by stamped writs and hired steel, the commission's clerks arrive with brass scales and leave with everything that is not bolted to bedrock. They insist their ledgers are merely arithmetic, never personal cruelty.

cdx-ash-coven.summary: Act I faction codex unlocked at Mordred's altar, describing the shadowy cultists drawn to border ruins and pyres.
cdx-ash-coven.flavor: A loose rabble of disgraced chanters and hedge-necromancers who see the creeping southern warmth as a divine invitation. They nest in flooded crypts and burned kilns, trading dark favors for ash-stained relics.

cdx-sand-clans.summary: Act II faction codex unlocked after repelling a canyon ambush, detailing the nomadic raiders of the Redmarsh passes.
cdx-sand-clans.flavor: Lean, sun-baked skirmishers who know every blind gully and dry waterhole between the Ochre Ditch and the mountains. They care nothing for northern rights or southern crowns, selling their hornbows to whoever pays in coin and clean water.

cdx-oakhaven-guild.summary: Act III faction codex unlocked when negotiating coastal entry, profiling the shrewd merchant council ruling Oakhaven.
cdx-oakhaven-guild.flavor: Timber barons, ship-factors, and tariff clerks who spent decades squabbling over berth fees and whale-oil quotas. Faced with a burning continent, they still insist on counting every barrel of flour before opening the gate.

cdx-ironclad-company.summary: Act III faction codex unlocked in Clashing Banners, describing the heavy mercenary legion fighting for coastal spoils.
cdx-ironclad-company.flavor: Disciplined ex-regulars clad in uniform grey plate who turned freelance the day imperial pay-chests stopped arriving. They march in tight shield-walls and treat salvage rights as the only law left standing.

cdx-ashen-company.summary: Act III faction codex unlocked by breaking rival warbands, profiling the zealous free-company warring against the Ironclads.
cdx-ashen-company.flavor: Painted with sulfur stripes and armed with phosphor-tar pots, these reckless raiders despise formal charters and merchant councils alike. Where the Ashen Banner camps, timber yards usually end the night as charcoal.

cdx-black-blockade.summary: Act III faction codex unlocked after fighting marine boarders, detailing Vesperion's hostile fleet patrolling the coast.
cdx-black-blockade.flavor: Tar-hulled galleys flying no national flag, crewed by hard-bitten press-gang sailors and sea-hardened arcanists. They prowl the outer fogbanks beyond the boom-chain, preying on overloaded transports and coastal lighthouses.

cdx-ironcamp-foundrymen.summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked at Vok's forge, profiling the stubborn master smiths working beside volcanic vents.
cdx-ironcamp-foundrymen.flavor: Deafened by trip-hammers and scarred by flying sparks, the forge-guild stayed behind on the basalt ridge because nowhere else burns hot enough to smelt meteoric iron. They judge every soldier solely by how well he maintains his edge.

cdx-penitent-order.summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked via Brother Elias, describing the ash-marked zealots enduring the caldera approaches.
cdx-penitent-order.flavor: Former abbey clerks and scarred survivors who marched inland carrying iron censers and heavy chains to atone for the realm's sins. Unsettling to share a campfire with, yet strangely calm when lava rains from the sky.

cdx-first-watch.summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked by finding ancient plate, detailing the forgotten pre-schism order of the Threshold.
cdx-first-watch.flavor: Long before modern barons argued over tolls, the First Watch stood silent guard over the continent's deep tectonic locks. Only cracked armor, blank signets, and stern stone inscriptions remain to mark their centuries of vigil.

cdx-ember-vanguard.summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked upon facing a Dread Knight, profiling the heavy armored shock troops of the Iron Pact.
cdx-ember-vanguard.flavor: Sealed inside blackened steel tempered over slag channels, these elite fanatics march without banners, music, or mercy. They view ordinary mortal armies as soft ore waiting to be hammered clean in the caldera's heat.

cdx-briar-hound.summary: Act I creature codex unlocked at Sunken Ford, examining the thorn-matted pack rushers of the northern thickets.
cdx-briar-hound.flavor: Border woodsmen blame wet winters and unburied war-dead for turning ordinary stray dogs into gaunt, vicious curs. Tangled blackthorn twigs mat their coats into natural bramble-armor that tears at bare calves.

cdx-flintback.summary: Act I creature codex unlocked in the northern woods, studying the slow, chert-plated beasts blocking timber roads.
cdx-flintback.flavor: Broad, bad-tempered grazers whose dorsal scales calcify into grey flint hard enough to turn a woodcutter's hatchet. Wise hunters leave them to chew roots in peace unless a mage is handy to crack their backs.

cdx-mire-wisp.summary: Act I creature codex unlocked after a fen ambush, explaining the pale marsh-gas casters haunting bog boardwalks.
cdx-mire-wisp.flavor: Peat-cutters tell rookies never to trust a steady blue flame floating off the timber planks after dusk. Mire wisps mimic lantern-light to lure patrols into waist-deep muck before pelting them with freezing bolts.

cdx-dune-lurker.summary: Act II creature codex unlocked in Bracken Basin, profiling the sand-burrowing ambushers of the Redmarsh wastes.
cdx-dune-lurker.flavor: Flat-backed predators that shimmy beneath warm red grit until only a faint ripple betrays their hiding place. Caravan guards keep iron-shod prods moving ahead of the mules to force lurkers out before they strike.

cdx-basalt-brute.summary: Act II creature codex unlocked upon facing one in the wastes, examining the animated quarry giants of the frontier.
cdx-basalt-brute.flavor: Quarried from dense volcanic rock and bound with crude siege-runes to serve as tireless shock troops. Arrows splinter uselessly off their chests, leaving only lightning and arcane fire to split their heavy mineral seams.

cdx-crypt-embalmers.summary: Act II creature codex unlocked in the lower quarry gallery, studying the ancient linen-wrapped mages of the salt vaults.
cdx-crypt-embalmers.flavor: Preserved in dry bitumen and copper wire, Third-Dynasty embalmers still patrol their sunken archives with grim persistence. Left unchecked behind enemy lines, they stitch fallen raiders back upright faster than swords can drop them.

cdx-salt-crab.summary: Act III creature codex unlocked on the low-tide flats, profiling the armored coastal crustaceans blocking beach paths.
cdx-salt-crab.flavor: Heavy-shelled scavengers that clatter out of tide-pools whenever battle spills blood into the brine. Their wet carapaces conduct lightning cleanly, making storm-casters far more effective against them than ordinary swordsmen.

cdx-elder-juggernauts.summary: Act III creature codex unlocked after felling the ridge sentinel, studying the colossal bound titans of the highlands.
cdx-elder-juggernauts.flavor: Towering frames of anthracite and iron wedges that slept beneath highland cairns for generations until tectonic tremors snapped their tethers. Every footstep splits granite trails and sends boulders tumbling down the passes.

cdx-frost-bell.summary: Act III creature codex unlocked by shattering one on the coast, examining the hovering bronze bells of flooded crypts.
cdx-frost-bell.flavor: Cast from cracked abbey metal and animated by cold astral currents, these silent relics drift through damp halls tolling a freezing note. Bowstrings snap and fingers stiffen within paces of their chime.

cdx-night-orchard.summary: Act III creature codex unlocked by clearing the terraced grove, profiling the uprooted, ward-warped cider trees.
cdx-night-orchard.flavor: Gnarled coastal fruit trees that drank too much runoff from leaking grave-wards and pulled their knotted roots free of the loam. They stalk dimly lit terraces, snaring patrols in crackling astral brambles.

cdx-anvilmaw-smith.summary: Act IV creature codex unlocked by hunting one in the caldera, studying the slag-forged hammer titans.
cdx-anvilmaw-smith.flavor: Lumbering horrors born where volcanic vents fused abandoned foundry anvils into living metal. They swing white-hot hammers with terrifying reach, forcing frontline troops to chill their joints and kite between blows.

cdx-redglass-drake.summary: Act IV creature codex unlocked by spotting one in the highlands, examining the volcanic glass-scaled fire flyers.
cdx-redglass-drake.flavor: Swift winged reptiles whose hides vitrified into jagged crimson glass along the caldera rims. Roosting on basalt chimneys, they dive through cinder-snow to scorch supply trains and melt iron helmets.

cdx-sunken-ford-ambush.summary: Act I event codex unlocked after Blood at the Ford, recounting the gnoll raid that exposed border corruption.
cdx-sunken-ford-ambush.flavor: What looked at dawn like another routine raid across the Alder shallows quickly turned sour when dead gnolls spilled fresh southern copper into the mud. The skirmish proved Thornwick's real enemies were not all across the river.

cdx-ravenwatch-betrayal.summary: Act I event codex unlocked after Nightfall at Ravenwatch, recording how the northern keep fell from within.
cdx-ravenwatch-betrayal.flavor: No battering ram ever touched Ravenwatch's iron portcullis; the chains were filed through quietly from the inside before midnight. The breach taught border officers that unpaid debts can break a wall faster than siege engines.

cdx-alder-exodus.summary: Act I event codex unlocked after Alder Bridge, chronicling the desperate stand that saved Thornwick's refugees.
cdx-alder-exodus.flavor: Three ragged waves of deserters and brigands crashed against the three-arched stone span while farm carts rumbled south behind the shields. The bridge held by a hair, buying the northern parishes one more breath.

cdx-ashbrook-evacuation.summary: Act I event codex unlocked upon completing Act I, recording the fierce fighting that opened the southern road.
cdx-ashbrook-evacuation.flavor: Smoke rolled across the northern pastures as the gatehouse garrison fought to keep the heavy iron doors from sealing shut forever. Breaking through Ashbrook marked the moment a local tax war became a continental march.

cdx-plateau-rupture.summary: Act II event codex unlocked after Wardstone Rupture, detailing the sabotage and cleansing of Redmarsh's spires.
cdx-plateau-rupture.flavor: For weeks an unnatural alkali storm pinned caravans inside their stockades until field scholars uncovered reverse blood-runes chiseled into the monolith bases. Re-grounding the three stones cleared the sky in a single silent flash.

cdx-quarry-revolt.summary: Act II event codex unlocked after Deep Quarry, chronicling the uprising of chained northern debtors in the pits.
cdx-quarry-revolt.flavor: When crane counterweights crashed into the overseer barracks and iron collars snapped open across three terraces, the southern army lost its main stone supply overnight. Miners traded picks for pikes and never looked back.

cdx-dry-cistern-siege.summary: Act II event codex unlocked upon completing Act II, recording the shattering discovery behind Ironheart's gates.
cdx-dry-cistern-siege.flavor: Thousands crossed the blistering alkali flats trusting the old mountain reservoirs to save them from the coming heat. Breaking past the frozen sluice-gates revealed a harsher enemy than any army: fifty years of dry red silt.

cdx-oakhaven-charter.summary: Act III event codex unlocked after Pledge at Oakhaven, recounting the tense alliance forged at the timber port.
cdx-oakhaven-charter.flavor: Merchant factors and frontier soldiers seldom trust each other, yet the sight of inland raiders burning the pine road concentrated minds wonderfully. Steel bought harbor shelter, and shelter bought time to rig the fleet.

cdx-harborwatch-pyre.summary: Act III event codex unlocked upon completing Act III, chronicling the fiery rearguard defense of the war-docks.
cdx-harborwatch-pyre.flavor: Ash fell thick as winter sleet across the granite piers while overloaded caravels slipped past the iron boom-chain one by one. Those who held the burning flagstones traded their own passage for the fleet's clean wind.

cdx-malrik-defection.summary: Act IV event codex unlocked after Flight of Malrik, documenting the pursuit of the Collegium's grand conspirator.
cdx-malrik-defection.flavor: Cornered on the switchbacks of Ashveil Gorge with stolen cipher-keys stuffed inside his coat, Malrik proved how far a scholar will run when his arithmetic turns to treason. Recovering his ledgers exposed the Iron Pact's inner design.

cdx-three-roads-rout.summary: Act IV event codex unlocked after Three-Roads Siege, recording the breaking of the Iron Pact's flanking columns.
cdx-three-roads-rout.flavor: Three heavy siege columns converged simultaneously on the highland junction, aiming to starve the vanguard before it reached the inner ramparts. Holding the star-redoubt and counter-marching north shattered their reserve camp completely.

cdx-threshold-reckoning.summary: Act IV event codex unlocked upon completing Act IV, chronicling the decisive confrontation beneath the caldera.
cdx-threshold-reckoning.flavor: Beyond the outer walls and the screaming magma channels lies a quiet stone chamber where steel alone cannot settle the account. Whatever verdict is struck upon the Threshold alters every road and harbor across Thornvael.

cdx-m25.summary: Act III place codex unlocked by inspecting slag wedges in Cinder Wards, explaining how coastal pillars were sabotaged.
cdx-m25.flavor: Someone drove rough furnace-slag shims beneath the basalt ward-rings to invert their cooling draft into scorching vents. Field arcanists call it clumsy engineering, though it cleared the flats efficiently enough.

cdx-m26.summary: Act III place codex unlocked via the western bunker range-slate in Sundered Ranks, detailing moorland redoubts.
cdx-m26.flavor: Chalked distances and windage marks cover the slate bolted beside the arbalest slit, showing exactly where passing supply columns slow down on the grade. Renegade officers knew the ridge better than the men who built it.

cdx-m27.summary: Act III faction codex unlocked at the chapel medicine chest in Field Infirmary, profiling Sera's triage company.
cdx-m27.flavor: Inside the blood-spotted lid sits a neat list of boiled linen, willow-bark, and laudanum rations stretched across three times too many stretchers. Sera's helpers work without complaint, asking only that the perimeter shields hold.

cdx-m28.summary: Act III place codex unlocked at the brass tide-gauge in Sunken Citadel, explaining the sea-gate flood clock.
cdx-m28.flavor: Green verdigris cakes the dial face, yet the heavy counterweight chain still ticks reliably with the Western Sea's swell. Every veteran who enters the water-gate learns to read the gauge before stepping onto the lower flags.

cdx-m29.summary: Act III lore codex unlocked via parapet tally marks in Hourglass Rescue, commemorating a desperate tower stand.
cdx-m29.flavor: Fourteen deep knife-notches scored into wet granite beside a broken crossbow stirrup. Whoever held the watchtower while the tide crept up the shingle spit counted every last bolt before the iron bars went under.

cdx-m30.summary: Act III place codex unlocked at the dry rain tank in Starved Bastion, detailing the fortress's failed water supply.
cdx-m30.flavor: Lead-lined cisterns built to catch coastal squalls stand dusty and cracked after weeks of hot inland wind. Scraping dry rust off the bottom trough explains why the cliff garrison greeted four grain wagons like a miracle.

cdx-m31.summary: Act III place codex unlocked at the central sluice gear-housing in Riverlock Crossing, explaining the canal machinery.
cdx-m31.flavor: Heavy cast-iron teeth slick with sheep-tallow drive twin oak floodgates weighing ten tons apiece. Control the central island and you control both freshwater for the harbor docks and the footing of anyone crossing below.

cdx-m32.summary: Act III creature codex unlocked by inspecting an anthracite rib-plate, studying the construction of the Elder Juggernaut.
cdx-m32.flavor: Up close, the fallen titan's hide is not natural stone at all, but layered volcanic coal fused with ancient copper staples. Artificers of the Age of Chains built their guardians to outlast empires, not merely skirmishes.

cdx-m33.summary: Act III faction codex unlocked via the bullion manifest in High-Stakes Gambit, exposing Baron Vane's wartime profiteering.
cdx-m33.flavor: Stamped bars of northern silver sit neatly stacked beside extortion writs levied on desperate ship-captains. Even with the horizon glowing red, Baron Vane treated the collapse of the realm as a buyer's market.

cdx-m34.summary: Act III faction codex unlocked at the phosphor-tar casks in Clashing Banners, explaining the bloody mercenary feud.
cdx-m34.flavor: Half a dozen leaking barrels of naval fire-tar lie mired in the mud between two slaughtered camps. Both free-companies swore the salvage belonged to their banner, proving greed outlives discipline even at the end of the world.

cdx-m35.summary: Act III relic codex unlocked on the scorched quarterdeck in Burning Harbor, detailing Admiral Kael's copper sheathing.
cdx-m35.flavor: Thin sheets of hammered copper nailed below the waterline kept shipworms out and let naval hulls shrug off flaming pitch longer than bare oak. Scorched black now, the plates still gleam where boarding axes bit deep.

cdx-m36.summary: Act IV creature codex unlocked near Highcrest bluff in Heartland March, examining the predators adapted to ash-drifts.
cdx-m36.flavor: Lean highland beasts whose lungs developed thick mucus filters to breathe sulfurous air without coughing. Scouts check every carcass for burned collars, half expecting to recognize hounds that wandered south months ago.

cdx-m37.summary: Act IV relic codex unlocked on the north crag in Shattered Beacons, detailing the crystal lenses of the signal grid.
cdx-m37.flavor: Copper-bound quartz shards scattered across the granite still feel faintly warm hours after the tower collapsed. Linked together, three such prisms turned ordinary watch-fires into a lethal arcane curtain across the valley.

cdx-m38.summary: Act IV place codex unlocked on Greystone's curtain wall in Besieged Wall, explaining the fortress's volcanic masonry.
cdx-m38.flavor: Highland masons mixed crushed volcanic pumice into their lime mortar so the walls would flex slightly during caldera tremors without shearing clean through. Even chipped by siege-golems, the grey stone refuses to crumble easily.

uniq-willow-snare-bow.summary: Act I unique Archer shortbow from bosses and bounties, combining early damage, critical chance, and steady accuracy.
uniq-willow-snare-bow.flavor: Cut from a water-seasoned willow growing over the creek narrows where poachers set wire snares for river hares. The limb flexes quietly in damp air and never creaks when drawn behind a wet alder trunk. Bailiffs hated the sound of its string.

uniq-briar-stalker-hood.summary: Early Act I unique Archer leather cap from bosses and bounties, granting armor, dodge chance, and extra accuracy.
uniq-briar-stalker-hood.flavor: Stitched from tough, briar-scarred calfskin that turns aside blackthorn hooks when crawling through northern hedgerows. Scouts pull the brim low to hide their eyes from river glare. It smells faintly of wet moss and old gun-oil.

uniq-ferryman-gloves.summary: Tier-1 unique Archer leather gloves from Act I bosses and bounties, adding damage, critical chance, and accuracy.
uniq-ferryman-gloves.flavor: Worn smooth across the palms from decades of shoving heavy ash punt-poles against the rocky bed of the Alder River. The reinforced thumb-seam grips a bowstring as cleanly as wet rope, keeping shots steady in freezing drizzle.

uniq-hedge-clerk-rod.summary: Act I unique Mage oak staff from bosses and bounties, boosting spell damage, maximum mana, and faster cast speed.
uniq-hedge-clerk-rod.flavor: Notched along the shaft at every foot-mark so a wandering border assessor could measure flooded ditch-lines and tax-plots on sight. When pressed into a skirmish, the seasoned oak channels crisp bolts without draining a novice dry.

uniq-tallow-candle-focus.summary: Early Act I unique Mage glass focus from bosses and bounties, offering spell damage, mana regeneration, and fire resistance.
uniq-tallow-candle-focus.flavor: Salvaged from the leaded window of a collapsed roadside chapel and set in a crude pewter frame. Holding it near a brazier warms the knuckles without blistering, while the smoky glass gathers stray mana from the damp air.

uniq-peat-smoke-cowl.summary: Tier-1 unique Mage scholar hat from Act I bosses and bounties, providing armor, maximum mana, and spell critical chance.
uniq-peat-smoke-cowl.flavor: Cured over slow-burning Fenwick peat-fires until the coarse wool turned dark brown and shed rain like greased canvas. Rural tutors wore these hats while teaching illicit arithmetic by lantern-light, keeping their thoughts sharp in the cold.

uniq-creek-bone-wand.summary: Act I unique Necromancer willow wand from bosses and bounties, adding spell damage, minion health, and maximum mana.
uniq-creek-bone-wand.flavor: Peeled from a pale willow branch that grew straight through a forgotten pauper's grave along the creek bank. Lower-parish clerks found that skeletons raised with its tap held their ribs together through twice as many gnoll blows.

uniq-pauper-burial-robe.summary: Early Act I unique Necromancer cloth robe from bosses and bounties, granting armor, minion damage, and poison resistance.
uniq-pauper-burial-robe.flavor: Dusted permanently white along the hem from shoveling quicklime into wet border trenches. The heavy linen smells sharp enough to turn aside marsh-venom, and raised servants marching beside it swing with grim, tireless force.

uniq-knuckle-dice-ring.summary: Tier-1 unique Necromancer bone ring from Act I bosses and bounties, boosting maximum mana, minion health, and spell damage.
uniq-knuckle-dice-ring.flavor: Carved from a bleached knuckle-bone by a bored picket-guard who lost his boots to a probate clerk in a rainy dice game. The clerk etched a tiny binding-mark inside the band, turning a gambler's trinket into a sturdy summoner's seal.

uniq-bog-iron-cleaver.summary: Act II unique Warrior bearded battleaxe from bosses and bounties, delivering solid damage, armor penetration, and extra health.
uniq-bog-iron-cleaver.flavor: Smelted from dark, impure bog-iron dredged out of flooded Redmarsh ditches and hammered thick behind the beard. It is too ugly for an officer's parade belt, yet it splits alkali-crusted shields and timber barricades in one clean heave.

uniq-sunken-warden-plate.summary: Tier-2 unique Warrior ring mail from Act II bosses and bounties, offering sturdy armor, extra health, and poison resistance.
uniq-sunken-warden-plate.flavor: Each iron ring was dipped in boiled pitch before riveting so brackish mire-water could not chew through the links. Dike sentries wore it through three seasons of marsh-fever without losing a buckle or coughing up blood.

uniq-peat-trench-shield.summary: Act II unique Warrior iron shield from bosses and bounties, providing armor, high block chance, and poison resistance.
uniq-peat-trench-shield.flavor: Hammered from bolted canal-walk plates that once kept supply mules from sinking into the Ochre Ditch. Planted firmly in soft mud, its broad iron face turns away viper lunges and canyon arrows with a dull, reassuring clang.

uniq-reed-whistle-bow.summary: Tier-2 unique Archer recurve bow from Act II bosses and bounties, adding solid damage, high crit chance, and armor penetration.
uniq-reed-whistle-bow.flavor: Fitted with a hollow river-reed notch near the upper tip that lets out a thin, eerie shriek whenever an arrow flies hard. Sand raiders hate the sound, because by the time you hear the whistle, the bodkin is already through your jerkin.

uniq-leech-hunter-boots.summary: Act II unique Archer tracker treads from bosses and bounties, granting armor, high dodge chance, and strong poison resistance.
uniq-leech-hunter-boots.flavor: Stitched knee-high from slick, vinegar-cured hide so alkali leeches and marsh vipers cannot find a seam to bite. Scouts who patrol the brackish flats prize them for keeping footing sure where armored troops slide into the brine.

uniq-bog-fog-mask.summary: Tier-2 unique Archer stalker hood from Act II bosses and bounties, boosting armor, sharp accuracy, and critical strike chance.
uniq-bog-fog-mask.flavor: Fine horsehair netting drapes across the brow to keep biting midges and blowing alkali grit out of a marksman's eyes. Looking through the dark weave cuts the blinding noon glare off Redmarsh salt-pans, steadying every shot.

uniq-wisp-lantern-staff.summary: Act II unique Mage ash staff from bosses and bounties, offering spell damage, large maximum mana, and solid cold resistance.
uniq-wisp-lantern-staff.flavor: Capped with an empty iron cage where a clever arcanist once trapped a marsh-wisp until it burned down to a cold blue ember. The pale glow never warms your hands, yet it holds a deep mana reserve and turns aside freezing sleet.

uniq-quartz-fen-focus.summary: Tier-2 unique Mage quartz focus from Act II bosses and bounties, delivering spell damage, spell crit chance, and mana regen.
uniq-quartz-fen-focus.flavor: Cut from a cloudy crystal seam unearthed where the wet fens meet the dry alkali flats. Though flawed with tiny mineral streaks, the lens sharpens stray ley-light into biting bursts while keeping a caster's reserve topped up.

uniq-wormwood-robe.summary: Act II unique Mage weaver robe from bosses and bounties, providing armor, large maximum mana, and high poison resistance.
uniq-wormwood-robe.flavor: Steeped in bitter wormwood oil and dried over slow alkali-bush fires until the cloth turned stiff, dark, and waterproof. Field apothecaries wore these coats straight into spore-choked hollows without ever needing a handkerchief.

uniq-peat-marrow-wand.summary: Tier-2 unique Necromancer yew wand from bosses and bounties, adding spell damage, minion damage, and solid maximum mana.
uniq-peat-marrow-wand.flavor: Seasoned in a sunken bell-pit where bronze verdigris stained the yew wood pale green from grip to tip. Bound servants answering its call strike with a heavy, metallic rhythm that wears down even shielded frontliners.

uniq-bog-mummy-wraps.summary: Act II unique Necromancer novice wraps from bosses and bounties, granting armor, extra minion health, and faster cast speed.
uniq-bog-mummy-wraps.flavor: Strips of dark, tannin-soaked linen unwound from ancient bog-burials where peat preserved every stitch intact. Wrapped tight around the forearms, they keep a clerk's fingers nimble while reinforcing every skeleton he calls up.

uniq-carrion-talisman.summary: Tier-2 unique Necromancer bronze locket from Act II bosses and bounties, boosting maximum mana, minion health, and spell damage.
uniq-carrion-talisman.flavor: Holds three tiny, polished marsh-frog bones wired neatly inside a tarnished bronze frame. Desert hexers mock it as a ditch-digger's charm, yet it keeps skeletal ranks upright through the worst alkali storms.

uniq-anchor-chain-flail.summary: Act III unique Warrior heavy morningstar from bosses and bounties, delivering high damage, armor penetration, and extra health.
uniq-anchor-chain-flail.flavor: Forged by Harborwatch smiths from three corroded links of a sunken brig's anchor chain welded to a spiked iron head. Swinging it takes broad shoulders and room to clear, yet nothing plated survives a clean impact.

uniq-reef-plate-cuirass.summary: Tier-3 unique Warrior hardened brigandine from Act III bosses and bounties, offering high armor, extra health, and cold resistance.
uniq-reef-plate-cuirass.flavor: Scoured bright by shingle-reef surf before coastal marines riveted fresh oiled leather over the backing. The salt-pitted steel shrugs off freezing sea-spray and boarding pikes alike, smelling faintly of kelp and wet iron.

uniq-gale-wall-kite.summary: Act III unique Warrior steel kite shield from bosses and bounties, granting high armor, strong block chance, and lightning res.
uniq-gale-wall-kite.flavor: Hammered with a heavy central ridge modeled after Oakhaven's stone breakwater to split oncoming charges cleanly in half. Copper rivets along the rim ground stray storm-arcs before they can numb the shield-arm.

uniq-corsair-wind-bow.summary: Tier-3 unique Archer composite war bow from Act III bosses and bounties, adding high damage, critical chance, and accuracy.
uniq-corsair-wind-bow.flavor: Strung with braided ship-rigging hemp waxed against salt-rot, built for firing from pitching decks across fifty yards of chop. A marksman who masters its stiff draw can thread an arrow through a gun-port in a gale.

uniq-cliff-talon-grips.summary: Act III unique Archer reinforced vambraces from bosses and bounties, providing armor, bonus damage, and high dodge chance.
uniq-cliff-talon-grips.flavor: Worn by coastal wreck-divers who hauled salvage up slick granite faces with bare knuckles and iron hooks. The scarred leather braces steady a heavy bow-hand while letting a scout slip clear of clumsy blows.

uniq-salt-spray-striders.summary: Tier-3 unique Archer windrunner boots from Act III bosses and bounties, granting armor, high dodge chance, and cold resistance.
uniq-salt-spray-striders.flavor: Soled with roughened sharkskin and cork so coastal scouts can sprint across wet barnacle reefs without losing their footing. Freezing surf rolls right off the oiled cuffs, keeping legs warm through long cliff watches.

uniq-storm-beacon-staff.summary: Act III unique Mage rune staff from bosses and bounties, boosting spell damage, large maximum mana, and high lightning resistance.
uniq-storm-beacon-staff.flavor: Carved from an oak spar salvaged after lightning split Harborwatch's blind beacon tower in half. The charred wood still hums when storm-clouds roll off the Western Sea, drinking static and turning it into crisp arcane bolts.

uniq-brine-mirror-focus.summary: Tier-3 unique Mage astral sphere from Act III bosses and bounties, delivering spell damage, spell crit chance, and mana regen.
uniq-brine-mirror-focus.flavor: A hollow blown-glass globe sealed with clear, salty tide-water drawn at midnight from the Sunken Citadel's flooded nave. Casters peer into its swirling depths to read ley-currents and snap sharp critical volleys.

uniq-abyssal-velvet-robe.summary: Act III unique Mage mystic velvet mantle from bosses and bounties, offering armor, large maximum mana, and high cold resistance.
uniq-abyssal-velvet-robe.flavor: Heavy indigo velvet weighted with lead shot along the hem so coastal gales cannot whip it across a caster's face. It feels damp as a winter fogbank yet insulates the wearer cleanly against freezing spray and frost-bells.

uniq-whalebone-siphon.summary: Tier-3 unique Necromancer amber focus wand from Act III bosses and bounties, adding spell damage, minion damage, and large mana.
uniq-whalebone-siphon.flavor: Scrimshawed from a bleached leviathan rib washed ashore below Oakhaven and capped with a lump of dark sea-amber. Bound spirits answer its call with ferocious weight, tearing through armored ranks along the piers.

uniq-barnacle-skull-cowl.summary: Act III unique Necromancer sage cowl from bosses and bounties, providing armor, high minion health, and spell critical chance.
uniq-barnacle-skull-cowl.flavor: Worn by cliff-ossuary keepers who lowered iron cages into flooded sea-caves to tally drowned sailors. Pale calcified shells cling to the stiff wool shoulders, lending grim durability to every servant raised beneath its gaze.

uniq-drowned-gold-signet.summary: Tier-3 unique Necromancer insight ring from Act III bosses and bounties, boosting maximum mana, minion damage, and cast speed.
uniq-drowned-gold-signet.flavor: Pried from the swollen finger of a galley-master who went down with his payroll chest off Anchor Spit. The saltwater-pitted gold still commands obedience, hurrying dark incantations and sharpening skeletal blades.

uniq-cinder-throne-greatsword.summary: Act IV unique Warrior flamberge from bosses and bounties, delivering heavy damage, high armor penetration, and fire resistance.
uniq-cinder-throne-greatsword.flavor: Forged in Ironcamp's hottest slag-pits for executioners sworn to the Pyre-Marshal's vanguard. Its wavy blackened steel bites straight through basalt plate while turning aside caldera flames that blister ordinary blades.

uniq-slag-forged-plate.summary: Tier-4 unique Warrior gothic full plate from Act IV bosses and bounties, granting massive armor, high health, and fire resistance.
uniq-slag-forged-plate.flavor: Cast from volcanic ironstone and quenched in smoking cinder-troughs until the metal turned dull slate-red. Men sealed inside this cuirass march straight across glowing fissures without flinching or slowing their stride.

uniq-sovereign-aegis.summary: Act IV unique Warrior citadel aegis from bosses and bounties, offering high armor, massive block chance, and extra health.
uniq-sovereign-aegis.flavor: Stamped with a fractured crown-seal and reinforced with double-riveted meteoric iron bars along the rim. Planted in a caldera breach, it absorbs titan hammer blows that would shatter ordinary tower shields into splinters.

uniq-obsidian-greatbow.summary: Tier-4 unique Archer windpiercer greatbow from Act IV bosses and bounties, adding heavy damage, high crit chance, and armor pen.
uniq-obsidian-greatbow.flavor: Backed with thin, flexible strips of dark volcanic glass that snap back with terrifying velocity in dry highland air. Arrows loosed from its string punch clean through dread-knight pauldrons before the echo fades.

uniq-ash-wind-mask.summary: Act IV unique Archer shadow mask from bosses and bounties, providing armor, high critical strike chance, and sharp accuracy.
uniq-ash-wind-mask.flavor: Fitted with twin smoked-mica lenses and a dampened wool mouth-cloth to filter choking sulfur fumes. Inquisition scouts wore these masks in Ashveil Gorge, picking off targets cleanly through blinding cinder-snow.

uniq-cinder-stalker-gloves.summary: Tier-4 unique Archer shadowstrike grips from Act IV bosses and bounties, boosting damage, critical chance, and high dodge chance.
uniq-cinder-stalker-gloves.flavor: Stitched from heat-cured drake hide with rough ash-dusted palms that never slip on a sweaty bow-grip or dagger hilt. Scouts who run the glowing highland ridges trust them to keep every release crisp under fire.

uniq-star-forge-staff.summary: Act IV unique Mage star staff from bosses and bounties, delivering high spell damage, large maximum mana, and spell crit chance.
uniq-star-forge-staff.flavor: Crowned with a small iron basket that holds a single glowing shard of caldera cinder without ever burning the shaft. Senior archons wield it to focus devastating barrages across entire volcanic valleys.

uniq-cosmos-ember-lens.summary: Tier-4 unique Mage cosmos eye from Act IV bosses and bounties, granting high spell damage, strong mana regen, and fire resistance.
uniq-cosmos-ember-lens.flavor: Cast from bronze melted out of a fallen abbey bell and fitted with a dark volcanic prism at its center. The astrolabe spins steadily in scorching drafts, recycling ambient caldera heat straight back into mana.

uniq-archmage-cinder-robe.summary: Act IV unique Mage star robe from bosses and bounties, providing armor, massive maximum mana, and strong fire resistance.
uniq-archmage-cinder-robe.flavor: Woven with fine mineral threads that glow faint orange along the hem whenever a heavy spell is cast. Only the highest fellows of the Conclave could afford cloth that survived the furnace heat of the inner peaks.

uniq-chancellery-siphon-wand.summary: Tier-4 unique Necromancer archon wand from Act IV bosses and bounties, offering high spell damage, minion damage, and large mana.
uniq-chancellery-siphon-wand.flavor: Carried by senior Synod inquisitors who audited heresy and unpaid blood-debts with equal ruthlessness. Its blackened silver tip drinks ash and vitality alike, driving skeletal cohorts into a relentless frenzy.

uniq-crown-ossuary-diadem.summary: Act IV unique Necromancer archmage diadem from bosses and bounties, granting armor, massive minion health, and faster cast speed.
uniq-crown-ossuary-diadem.flavor: Hammered from cold, dull iron clinkers pulled from dead furnace grates and set with pale bone studs. Wearing it chills the brow against caldera madness while knitting raised servants into an unbreakable wall.

uniq-sovereign-pyre-medallion.summary: Tier-4 unique Necromancer colossus heart from Act IV bosses and bounties, boosting health, minion damage, and minion health.
uniq-sovereign-pyre-medallion.flavor: A heavy, fist-sized lump of dark slag bound in iron wire that beats faintly like a banked coal against the sternum. Raised legions fighting under its silent pulse refuse to crumble even beneath volcanic fire.

timeline.summary: Chronological record of forty key events shaping the Border, listed from the earliest founding compacts to the present crisis.
timeline.flavor: History on the Border is rarely written by poets; it is pieced together from water-damaged tax rolls, chipped boundary stones, and tavern arguments. Read from oldest to newest, these forty entries trace how a quiet frontier slowly caught fire.

book-ford-toll-daybook.summary: Act I lore book written by Toll-Clerk Brann, recovered during Blood at the Ford to shed light on border trade.
book-ford-toll-daybook.flavor: Rainwater has blurred the margin totals, yet Brann's cramped handwriting still tracks every grain-cart, sheep-drove, and sealed imperial wagon that crossed the Alder shallows. The final page breaks off mid-sentence beside a dark smudge.

book-fen-boardwalk-notice.summary: Act I lore book authored by Foreman Odo, discovered in Whispers in the Fen regarding the maintenance of bog crossings.
book-fen-boardwalk-notice.flavor: Nailed originally to a rotting cedar post above the peat-ditches, this oilcloth notice warns travelers which planks will hold a mule and which will swallow a man whole. Odo's last line begs Thornwick for whale oil that never came.

book-ravenwatch-duty-roster.summary: Act I lore book compiled by Corporal Hobb, found during Nightfall at Ravenwatch detailing the garrison's final shifts.
book-ravenwatch-duty-roster.flavor: A damp vellum roll listing watch-posts, lantern tallies, and four names scratched out twice with an angry iron nib. Hobb kept neat records to the very end, noting with dry bitterness that the relief column was three weeks overdue.

book-abbey-probate-register.summary: Act I lore book penned by Brother Anselm, uncovered in The Sunken Sanctum recording posthumous parish debts.
book-abbey-probate-register.flavor: Bound in mildewed calfskin and weighted with lead corners so it would not float away when the lower crypts flooded. Inside, Anselm meticulously logs every unpaid tithe, funeral fee, and lien carried past the grave.

book-hermit-wick-ledger.summary: Act I lore book kept by Keeper Soren, found in Lantern Passage chronicling oil rations and fog-watch shifts.
book-hermit-wick-ledger.flavor: Page after page of quiet, obsessive measurements: drops of whale oil burned per hour, wind direction off the fen, and the exact night the supply runners stopped answering his horn. Soren trusted his lanterns more than any lord.

book-greywood-tally-slate.summary: Act I lore book written by Factor Merrick, discovered in Greywood Supply detailing timber quotas and mill haulage.
book-greywood-tally-slate.flavor: Scratched onto hinged slate tablets wrapped in waxed twine to survive sawmill sawdust and autumn sleet. Merrick's figures show oak beams vanishing south by the hundred while Thornwick's own palisade rotted in the mud.

book-vanguard-march-orders.summary: Act I lore book drafted by Captain Velen's Adjutant, found in Split Vanguard outlining troop movements along the border.
book-vanguard-march-orders.flavor: Crisp military shorthand stamped with Southern Crown wax, ordering forced marches without baggage trains or proper winter boots. Even the adjutant's neat script betrays quiet unease over how thin the northern line was stretched.

book-alder-mason-plaque.summary: Act I lore book recorded by Master Mason Dorin, uncovered at Alder Bridge describing the ancient span's construction.
book-alder-mason-plaque.flavor: Copied from a weathered bronze survey plate bolted beneath the central arch. Dorin boasted that his three-arched stonework would outlast every king in the South, provided nobody was foolish enough to undermine the ley-piers.

book-trapper-boar-journal.summary: Act I lore book kept by Huntsman Corvus, found during Ironhide Hunt tracking the movements of Greywood beasts.
book-trapper-boar-journal.flavor: Stained with pine resin and dried mud, these folded sheets map thorn-boar wallows, broken snares, and strange tracks near the old quarry. Corvus noted that the woodland beasts stopped fleeing human scent weeks before the raids began.

book-undervault-seal-writ.summary: Act I lore book issued by Dwarven Factor Thrain, recovered in Undervault Links detailing the subterranean drainage tunnels.
book-undervault-seal-writ.flavor: Written in blunt, practical prose that wastes no ink on pleasantries. Thrain warns the human magistrates that sealing the lead drainage galleries to hide smuggling caches will eventually flood the entire southern approach.

book-ashbrook-steward-letter.summary: Act I lore book written by Stewardess Marta, found during Ashbrook Retreat capturing the final hours before evacuation.
book-ashbrook-steward-letter.flavor: Folded neatly and addressed to a sister in Oakhaven, yet never handed to a courier. Marta describes packing silver candlesticks into grain sacks while ash drifted over the southern ridge for the first time in living memory.

book-thornwick-guild-notice.summary: Act I lore book proclaimed by Bailiff Harken, located in Thornwick Market setting curfew and rationing rules.
book-thornwick-guild-notice.flavor: Posted beside the tavern door where half the town could read it and the other half could spit on it. Harken's decree forbids hoarding tallow, carrying unsheathed axes after dusk, or spreading rumors about the Salt Tithe.

book-border-mint-assay.summary: Act I lore book compiled by Assayer Pell, discovered at the Border Mint Ruins exposing debased coinage.
book-border-mint-assay.flavor: Hidden beneath a cracked crucible, Pell's private assay notes prove that fresh copper slugs were being struck underweight by order from above. Every column ends with the same grim question: where was the real silver going?

book-weir-courier-note.summary: Act I lore book scribbled by Scout Fenwick, salvaged from the Thornwick Weir inside a sealed tube.
book-weir-courier-note.flavor: A soaked, frantic scrap of parchment stuffed into a waxed reed-case before Fenwick had to swim the flooded eel-weirs. Half the ink has run, leaving only hurried warnings about gnoll scouts carrying southern copper.

book-quarry-kiln-formula.summary: Act I lore book penned by Alchemist Toren, found at the Vitrified Kilns studying strange green furnace slag.
book-quarry-kiln-formula.flavor: Toren's careful sketches document how intense arcane heat turned ordinary Greywood brick and melted bronze into humming green glass. His final margin note warns that local wolves have started sleeping beside the warm slag-heaps.

book-redmarsh-ration-log.summary: Act II lore book maintained by Quartermaster Bram, found in Redmarsh Outpost tracking scarce water rations.
book-redmarsh-ration-log.flavor: Every tin dipper of boiled vinegar-brine is accounted for down to the half-gill, signed with thumbprints by thirsty drovers and soldiers alike. Bram's ledger reads less like a supply book and more like a countdown.

book-boundary-stone-oath.summary: Act II lore book authored by Surveyor Lyra, discovered in Redmarsh Border mapping the shifting alkali ditches.
book-boundary-stone-oath.flavor: Lyra's dry, precise field notes record how the Ochre Ditch creeps three yards wider every dry season, swallowing old cedar road-markers whole. She writes with quiet anger about caravans ignoring her stakes and losing wagons to the brine.

book-twin-passes-ambush.summary: Act II lore book filed by Sergeant Kael, recovered in Twin Passes detailing canyon crossfire tactics.
book-twin-passes-ambush.flavor: A terse military after-action report scribbled on the back of a supply chit while pinned behind a sandstone boulder. Kael maps the exact blind spots of the chimney-spire snipers so the next column might actually make it through.

book-scattered-scout-scrap.summary: Act II lore book written by Outrider Joren, found in Scattered Scouts containing field signal codes.
book-scattered-scout-scrap.flavor: Darkened at one corner with dried blood and alkali dust, this folded card lists mirror-flashes and horn-blasts used by Redmarsh outriders. Joren's last scrawl warns that the desert raiders have learned to mimic the relief signal.

book-palisade-repair-tally.summary: Act II lore book kept by Carpenter Vane, uncovered in Outpost Palisade recording timber and pitch shortages.
book-palisade-repair-tally.flavor: Vane complains in blunt carpenter's prose that alkali brine eats through fresh cedar pilings in six months flat. Without black bitumen sealant and ironstone brackets, he predicts the whole stockade will tilt into the mud before winter.

book-wardstone-fracture-study.summary: Act II lore book written by Scholar Zahra, found during Wardstone Rupture analyzing the failing climate obelisks.
book-wardstone-fracture-study.flavor: Filled with crisp diagrams of crystal lattices and grounding wires, Zahra's study proves the quartz monoliths did not crack by accident. Someone deliberately carved reverse runes into their bases to whip the alkali flats into permanent storm.

book-mire-convoy-manifest.summary: Act II lore book signed by Wagon-Master Durn, recovered in Mire Convoy listing freight along the corduroy road.
book-mire-convoy-manifest.flavor: Six wagons of salt-pork, oats, and iron spikes logged neatly before departure—and three crates crossed out in a different hand. Durn's angry margin notes demand to know why half his flour was diverted toward the Deep Quarry.

book-granary-stilt-accounts.summary: Act II lore book maintained by Storekeeper Maren, found in Granary Raid detailing Redmarsh's food reserves.
book-granary-stilt-accounts.flavor: Maren tallies every sack hoisted up to the limestone stilt-granary, noting weevil losses, brine-damp spoilage, and armed guards posted on the ladders. Reading the totals makes it painfully clear how close the outpost sits to starvation.

book-hexer-cauldron-notes.summary: Act II lore book written by Hexer Saelen, uncovered in Hexer's Hollow outlining bitter oasis-cursing formulas.
book-hexer-cauldron-notes.flavor: Cramped, spiteful recipes written in green copper-ink on scraps of boiled hide. Saelen details how boiling debtor bones with alkali salts sours a clean aquifer, turning a caravan's last hope into a slow, burning fever.

book-quarry-slave-petition.summary: Act II lore book smuggled out by Miner Gorin, found in Deep Quarry listing chained northern debtors.
book-quarry-slave-petition.flavor: Written with a charred splinter on the inside of a flour sack, this roll names forty-seven Thornwick farmers and smiths worked to the bone in the basalt pits. Gorin's final line is not a plea for mercy, but a count of hidden pickaxes.

book-lean-garrison-diary.summary: Act II lore book kept by Lieutenant Corin, discovered in Lean Garrison chronicling a desperate blockhouse siege.
book-lean-garrison-diary.flavor: Short, exhausted entries written by tallow stub while sand-raiders prowl outside the shutters. Corin records boiling boot-laces for broth, counting his last twelve crossbow bolts, and listening for a relief horn that takes far too long.

book-refugee-column-writ.summary: Act II lore book issued by Magistrate Orin, found in Fleeing Column ordering the civilian evacuation.
book-refugee-column-writ.flavor: Stamped with a cracked municipal seal, Orin's writ commands every family in the upper basins to abandon their carts and march light toward the mountain gates. Even formal legal prose cannot hide the desperation between the lines.

book-ironheart-cistern-audit.summary: Act II lore book written by Engineer Vesper, recovered at Fork of Spears measuring the mountain reservoirs.
book-ironheart-cistern-audit.flavor: Cold, undeniable engineering measurements: flow rates, silt depths, and cracked glacier-conduits checked three times over. Vesper's final entry is blunt enough to break a kingdom's heart—the mountain is dead, and only the sea remains.

book-embalmer-jar-ritual.summary: Act II lore book penned by High Embalmer Seti, found in the Redrock Assay Vault explaining Third-Dynasty burial law.
book-embalmer-jar-ritual.flavor: Seti explains with dry bureaucratic pride how copper wire, bitumen, and stamped silver tally-tablets bind a debtor's estate cleanly across centuries. To a Third-Dynasty notary, death is merely a change of address, never a pardon.

book-milestone-defacement.summary: Act II lore book compiled by Chronicler Zahra, discovered at the Four-Faced Milestone documenting tampered road signs.
book-milestone-defacement.flavor: Charcoal rubbings taken from an ancient crossroads obelisk reveal fresh chisel marks reversing the safe-water glyphs. Zahra concludes that someone deliberately steered northern relief columns straight into the quicksand sinks.

book-oakhaven-guild-tariff.summary: Act III lore book maintained by Harbor-Master Tavin, found in Oakhaven listing maritime duties and timber quotas.
book-oakhaven-guild-tariff.flavor: Salt-stiffened pages detailing anchorage fees, ironwood tonnage, and emergency surcharges levied on every vessel entering the cove. Tavin's neat columns show ordinary merchant trade collapsing overnight into frantic evacuation logistics.

book-oakhaven-truce-articles.summary: Act III lore book drafted by Guild Speaker Corvus, recovered in Pledge at Oakhaven outlining the frontier pact.
book-oakhaven-truce-articles.flavor: Signed in haste by rival ship-captains and bailiffs who hated each other only slightly less than they feared the inland raiders. The articles trade harbor sanctuary for sworn steel along the northern timber road.

book-cinder-wards-eviction.summary: Act III lore book signed by Warden Lyra, found in Cinder Wards ordering the clearance of unstable coastal altars.
book-cinder-wards-eviction.flavor: A blunt eviction notice commanding squatters and hedge-cultists off the sulfurous flats before the fractured ward-rings blow. Lyra notes with grim humor that nobody listens to a parchment warning until the ground starts glowing.

book-sundered-ranks-aftermath.summary: Act III lore book filed by Captain Hale, discovered in Sundered Ranks assessing moorland artillery engagements.
book-sundered-ranks-aftermath.flavor: Hale's plain-spoken report counts broken carriage wheels, spent powder kegs, and the exact ridge-angles where renegade legions dug in. He advises any future commander to crack both flanks before touching the central crag.

book-infirmary-triage-notes.summary: Act III lore book kept by Surgeon Meris, found in Field Infirmary logging battlefield wounds and bandage shortages.
book-infirmary-triage-notes.flavor: Spotted with dried blood and vinegar stains, Meris's surgical roll sorts incoming borderers into those who can walk, those who need a saw, and those who only need quiet. The ink grows shakier as the raider packs close in.

book-sunken-citadel-tide-table.summary: Act III lore book compiled by Keeper Orin, recovered in Sunken Citadel charting flood intervals at the sea-gate.
book-sunken-citadel-tide-table.flavor: Carefully calculated high-water marks etched onto waterproofed vellum. Orin warns that anyone caught inside the lower sea-caves when the Western Sea surges will find the iron grates submerged in less than twenty minutes.

book-hourglass-spit-warning.summary: Act III lore book written by Pilot Bram, found in Hourglass Rescue detailing safe crossing times on the shingle bar.
book-hourglass-spit-warning.flavor: Bram's salty, no-nonsense rules for running the narrow gravel spit before the tide cuts off the tidal vaults. He adds a dry postscript: if you hear the surf ringing against the iron bars, drop your pack and run.

book-starved-bastion-log.summary: Act III lore book maintained by Castellan Vane, uncovered in Starved Bastion recording weeks of siege rationing.
book-starved-bastion-log.flavor: Day by day, the daily allowance shrinks from half a loaf to boiled oats, and finally to leather straps softened in rainwater. Yet Vane's handwriting stays steady, vowing the cliff-watch will hold until grain wagons reach the bridge.

book-riverlock-manual.summary: Act III lore book authored by Lock-Master Durn, found in Riverlock Crossing explaining the canal floodgate gears.
book-riverlock-manual.flavor: Detailed diagrams of greased iron counterweights, sluice-pins, and freshwater channels feeding Harborwatch's cisterns. Durn warns that opening both gates simultaneously will sweep armored men straight off the stone walkways.

book-juggernaut-binding-scroll.summary: Act III lore book inscribed by Arch-Artificer Sol, recovered in Elder Juggernaut detailing ancient titan bindings.
book-juggernaut-binding-scroll.flavor: Translated from cracked Age of Chains stone tablets, Sol's treatise describes how primeval granite colossi were shackled to highland cairns. He warns ominously that deep tectonic tremors can snap every binding rune at once.

book-cliff-battery-orders.summary: Act III lore book issued by Master Gunner Tor, found in High-Stakes Gambit outlining sea-cliff culverin firing arcs.
book-cliff-battery-orders.flavor: Smudged with black powder and tallow, Tor's orders list elevation wedges and iron shot allotments for guarding the coastal pass. He grumbles that noble speculators care more about guarding their vaults than feeding his gun crews.

book-mercenary-contract-dispute.summary: Act III lore book written by Paymaster Krell, discovered in Clashing Banners detailing the feud between rival warbands.
book-mercenary-contract-dispute.flavor: An exasperated legal summary of how the Ironclad Banner and the Ashen Company went from sharing a camp to slaughtering each other over disputed phosphor-tar casks. Krell concludes that neither side deserves a single copper.

book-harborwatch-lighthouse-log.summary: Act III lore book penned by Keeper Aldous, found in Burning Harbor recording the final night of the evacuation.
book-harborwatch-lighthouse-log.flavor: The last pages smell faintly of woodsmoke and sea-salt. Aldous logs the departure of every overloaded caravel slipping past the iron boom-chain, trimming his wick one final time while ash falls thick across the lantern glass.

book-vane-vault-inventory.summary: Act III lore book kept by Clerk Tibalt, uncovered in Baron Vane's Catacomb Lift listing contraband and bullion.
book-vane-vault-inventory.flavor: Double-columned accounts hidden behind a false wine-rack, proving Baron Vane skimmed timber, grain, and silver from the evacuation effort for months. Tibalt's tiny footnote dryly hopes the Baron sinks before his ledger surfaces.

uniq-tollkeeper-bill.summary: Act I unique Warrior handaxe dropped by Briar Hounds, pairing Body and accuracy with early lifesteal.
uniq-tollkeeper-bill.flavor: Clerk Brann kept this notched woodcutter's axe under his desk at Alder Ford for travelers who tried to dispute the bridge tariff. When the hounds overran the tollhouse, one carried it off by the leather wrist-loop. Its flat still bears a faint wax-stamp.

uniq-bren-dry-boot.summary: Act I unique all-class leather boots from questing, granting brisk speed, poison resistance, and extra health.
uniq-bren-dry-boot.flavor: Ford-Scout Bren swore a soldier only needed one dry boot to stay sane in the northern drizzle, provided he kept switching which foot suffered. The left sole is patched with boiled harness leather and smells strongly of mutton tallow and fen-mud.

uniq-mordred-tallow-wand.summary: Act I unique Mage willow wand dropped by Ash-Tongue Shamans, boosting Mind, maximum mana, and fire resistance.
uniq-mordred-tallow-wand.flavor: Carved from a willow root pulled out of the flooded sanctum and dipped repeatedly in consecrated tallow until it held a steady, greasy sheen. Hedge-casters argue over whether the wax protects the wood from rot or merely keeps the wielder's fingers from blistering.

uniq-ravenwatch-gate-door.summary: Act I unique Warrior buckler dropped by Quill Fiends, offering sturdy armor, extra health, and a Body bonus.
uniq-ravenwatch-gate-door.flavor: Hacked straight out of the shattered oak planking of Ravenwatch's inner gate after the night raid broke the hinges. Someone bolted a bent iron strap to the back and called it a shield. Two broken quill-tips remain wedged permanently in the grain.

uniq-greywood-poacher-bow.summary: Act I unique Archer ash shortbow from Gloom Stags, delivering sharp accuracy, critical chance, and movement speed.
uniq-greywood-poacher-bow.flavor: Confiscated three times by Thornwick bailiffs and stolen back from the evidence shed four times by the same unnamed hunter. The limb is rubbed dark with walnut oil so it never catches moonlight, and the grip fits a calloused thumb like an old grudge.

uniq-krag-jawbone.summary: Act I unique Warrior spiked cudgel dropped by Flintbacks, providing heavy Body, armor, and maximum health.
uniq-krag-jawbone.flavor: Originally a quarryman's tamping maul studded with horse-shoe nails after the Salt Tithe took the village's real iron. It is too clumsy for polite fencing, yet one solid swing against a shield-boss usually settles any wage dispute on the spot.

uniq-corin-dispatch-ring.summary: Act I unique all-class copper band found in chests, boosting speed, mana regeneration, and cold resistance.
uniq-corin-dispatch-ring.flavor: Worn by courier Corin to stamp wax seals on urgent dispatches that nobody in the capital ever bothered to open. The copper has turned green along the inner rim from three winters of rain, yet the band still hums with restless haste.

uniq-undervault-lantern-helm.summary: Act I unique Warrior iron helm dropped by Mire Wisps, granting solid armor, high poison resistance, and health.
uniq-undervault-lantern-helm.flavor: A battered dwarven miner's pot-helm fitted with a wire bracket over the brow where a tiny tin cage once hung. The canary is long gone, but the oiled cloth lining still filters out marsh gas and damp cellar rot.

uniq-morvessa-spindle.summary: Act I unique all-class bloodstone pendant from the Silk Widow, granting high health, poison resistance, and lifesteal.
uniq-morvessa-spindle.flavor: Heavy as a merchant's assay weight and hung on a braided cord of dark, unbleached silk. Quartermasters who recognize the stamp on the clasp lower their voices, remembering how neatly its former owner balanced blood against silver.

uniq-alkali-canteen-amulet.summary: Act II unique all-class bronze locket dropped by Sand Raiders, offering high health, fire resistance, and Body.
uniq-alkali-canteen-amulet.flavor: Hammered flat from a dented imperial canteen by a deserter who decided metal over his heart was worth more than warm brine. Shaking it still produces a faint rattle of dry salt crystals sealed inside the soldered seam.

uniq-kaelen-marrow-needle.summary: Act II unique all-class steel rondel dropped by Fen Hexers, pairing high accuracy and critical chance with lifesteal.
uniq-kaelen-marrow-needle.flavor: Hexer Saelen filed this narrow dagger from a broken apothecary's probe, using it to bleed bitter roots and careless travelers alike. The blade is stained dark near the bolster and slides between leather laces without making a sound.

uniq-quarry-overseer-maul.summary: Act II unique Warrior heavy morningstar from Pale Burrowers, granting Body, accuracy, and extra maximum health.
uniq-quarry-overseer-maul.flavor: Forged from melted debtor shackles in the Deep Quarry after a shift-boss pushed his luck one lash too far. The iron head is ugly, lopsided, and heavy enough to split a basalt block or a turnkey's skull with equal ease.

uniq-wardstone-shard-focus.summary: Act II unique Mage quartz focus dropped by Dune Scarabs, boosting Mind, maximum mana, and high lightning resistance.
