pref-brisk.summary: Tier-1 gear prefix for boots, weapons, and armor that adds a light bonus to movement or action speed.
pref-brisk.flavor: Trimmed of excess buckles and greased with mutton tallow by couriers who got paid by the mile. A brisk kit keeps a scout half a stride ahead of the mud and the dogs.

pref-fleet.summary: Tier-2 gear prefix for boots, weapons, and rings that provides a noticeable speed increase.
pref-fleet.flavor: Favored by Twin Passes outriders who learned that standing still in a sandstone canyon is a quick way to catch a hornbow shaft. Every ounce of dead weight is pared away for pure, nimble pace.

pref-galestrung.summary: Tier-3 gear prefix for boots, weapons, and amulets that grants a high speed bonus.
pref-galestrung.flavor: Strung with salt-cured sinew and wind-blessed copper wire along Oakhaven's stormy cliffs. Wearers move with the sudden, snapping urgency of a coastal squall, closing gaps before enemy archers can draw.

pref-hale.summary: Tier-1 gear prefix for armor, helms, shields, rings, and amulets that adds a small amount of maximum health.
pref-hale.flavor: Stitched with dried willow-bark charms and honest wool padding to keep winter chill out of the ribs. Frontier levies prize hale gear simply because it helps a man walk away from a bad morning.

pref-blood-warm.summary: Tier-2 gear prefix for armor, helms, shields, and amulets that provides a moderate maximum health bonus.
pref-blood-warm.flavor: Quenched in warm iron-rich spring water rather than cold river brine, leaving the metal oddly comforting against the skin. Soldiers on night picket swear it keeps their fingers nimble through sleet.

pref-sinew-bound.summary: Tier-3 gear prefix for armor, helms, shields, and rings that grants a strong maximum health increase.
pref-sinew-bound.flavor: Reinforced with layered rawhide and boiled ox-sinew by veteran camp-surgeons who grew tired of stitching open bellies. The binding flexes with the ribcage, absorbing impacts that would otherwise snap bone.

pref-immortal.summary: Tier-4 gear prefix for armor, shields, and amulets that delivers a massive boost to maximum health.
pref-immortal.flavor: Stamped with a stubborn First-Dynasty vitality seal recovered from deep coastal crypts. Veterans wearing undying kit have a habit of crawling back out of collapsed trenches long after their company wrote them off.

pref-wellspring.summary: Tier-1 gear prefix for weapons, helms, armor, rings, and amulets that adds a small pool of maximum mana.
pref-wellspring.flavor: Inlaid with a sliver of river-quartz that drinks stray dew and ambient ley-charge alike. Apprentice mages trade their supper rations for wellspring trinkets just to squeeze one extra bolt out of a skirmish.

pref-vessel.summary: Tier-2 gear prefix for weapons, helms, armor, and amulets that grants a moderate maximum mana increase.
pref-vessel.flavor: Hollowed and lined with thin silver foil by Redmarsh artificers who understood the value of a deep cistern. It holds arcane charge cleanly through dry desert marches where ambient mana runs thin.

pref-ley-steeped.summary: Tier-3 gear prefix for weapons, helms, armor, and rings that provides a strong maximum mana bonus.
pref-ley-steeped.flavor: Left buried for a full moon beside a humming plateau wardstone until the metal itself began to tingle. Casters feel a steady, cold pressure humming at their fingertips whenever they grip it.

pref-abyssal-font.summary: Tier-4 gear prefix for weapons, helms, armor, and amulets that delivers a huge maximum mana pool.
pref-abyssal-font.flavor: Tempered over deep coastal rifts where ocean currents cross ancient ley-lines. Even a senior arcanist rarely drains an astral-font piece dry before the battlefield falls quiet.

pref-riveted.summary: Tier-1 gear prefix for armor, shields, helms, and boots that adds a small amount of flat armor.
pref-riveted.flavor: Ugly, heavy-headed iron rivets hammered cold into worn leather and scrap plate. Thornwick smiths do not promise comfort, only that the seams will hold when a gnoll cleaver bites.

pref-bastion.summary: Tier-2 gear prefix for armor, shields, helms, and boots that grants a moderate armor increase.
pref-bastion.flavor: Built to the thick, squared-off specifications of Oakhaven's seawall garrisons. Bastion-grade kit turns aside crossfire and falling masonry alike, though it makes climbing ladders a noisy chore.

pref-citadel-plated.summary: Tier-3 gear prefix for armor, shields, and helms that provides a heavy armor bonus.
pref-citadel-plated.flavor: Layered with overlapping black steel salvaged from highland fortress armories. Men clad in citadel-plated harness advance like moving gatehouses, shrugging off volleys that shred ordinary mail.

pref-true-sighted.summary: Tier-2 gear prefix for weapons, helms, and rings that improves combat accuracy.
pref-true-sighted.flavor: Balanced with a surveyor's plumb-bob and polished until the sight-line catches no glare. Marksmen and duelists alike pay extra for true-sighted gear when fighting in thick bog-fog.

pref-unerring.summary: Tier-4 gear prefix for weapons, helms, rings, and amulets that grants a high accuracy bonus.
pref-unerring.flavor: Calibrated by Collegium lens-grinders using smoked quartz and star-silver wire. Whether loosing an arrow across a canyon or driving a spear through a visor slit, an unerring piece rarely wastes a strike.

suff-of-the-ford.summary: Tier-1 suffix for boots, armor, and shields that grants light cold resistance.
suff-of-the-ford.flavor: Greased with goose-fat and lined with rough sheep's wool by Alder River ferrymen. Anyone who has stood waist-deep in November meltwater knows why border troops guard these linings like silver.

suff-of-winter-watch.summary: Tier-2 suffix for armor, helms, boots, amulets, and rings that provides moderate cold resistance.
suff-of-winter-watch.flavor: Issued to highland pickets who kept watch over snow-choked passes long after the supply wagons stopped coming. The wool stays dry under sleet and keeps frostbite out of the knuckles.

suff-of-the-glacier.summary: Tier-4 suffix for armor, shields, amulets, and rings that delivers high cold resistance.
suff-of-the-glacier.flavor: Bound with pale alpine frost-wards recovered from ancient mountain cisterns. Even the bitter breath of a frost-bell or glacial titan slides off the rime-vault weave without numbing the skin.

suff-of-slag.summary: Tier-1 suffix for armor, shields, boots, and helms that adds light fire resistance.
suff-of-slag.flavor: Dusted with crushed furnace clinker and rubbed with wet clay by smelter apprentices. It leaves black smudges on everything you touch, yet keeps stray embers from chewing through your cloak.

suff-of-the-kiln.summary: Tier-2 suffix for armor, shields, helms, rings, and amulets that grants moderate fire resistance.
suff-of-the-kiln.flavor: Cured beside the vitrified brick ovens of Greywood until the leather toughened like old horn. Sappers wear kiln-treated gear when clearing burning barricades and cinderling nests.

suff-of-the-caldera.summary: Tier-4 suffix for armor, shields, amulets, and rings that delivers high fire resistance.
suff-of-the-caldera.flavor: Forged with asbestos weave and quenched in volcanic ash inside Ironcamp's deepest yards. Wearers can wade through blistering heat and magma spray that would cook ordinary plate.

suff-of-the-fen.summary: Tier-1 suffix for boots, armor, helms, and rings that grants light poison resistance.
suff-of-the-fen.flavor: Steeped in bitter bog-myrtle and peat-smoke by Fenwick ditch-cutters. It smells like an old wet cellar, which happens to be the best way to keep marsh-venom and biting flies at bay.

suff-of-alkali.summary: Tier-2 suffix for armor, helms, boots, amulets, and rings that provides moderate poison resistance.
suff-of-alkali.flavor: Treated with slaked lime and boiled vinegar by Redmarsh caravan guards. Alkali-cured gear shrugs off viper spit and toxic marsh brine that would rot untreated leather in a single afternoon.

suff-of-the-ossuary.summary: Tier-4 suffix for armor, shields, amulets, and rings that delivers high poison resistance.
suff-of-the-ossuary.flavor: Anointed with coastal abbey preservatives designed for men who spend their lives sealing plague-crypts. Even the vilest spore-matron cloud turns thin and harmless against a bile-ward seal.

suff-of-copper-wire.summary: Tier-1 suffix for boots, armor, helms, and shields that adds light lightning resistance.
suff-of-copper-wire.flavor: A braided strand of cheap copper tacked from collar to heel so stray static runs straight into the mud. Ugly work, yet it has saved more than one scout from a dune-scarab's bite.

suff-of-the-fulgurite.summary: Tier-2 suffix for armor, shields, helms, rings, and amulets that grants moderate lightning resistance.
suff-of-the-fulgurite.flavor: Inlaid with glassy tubes of sand fused by desert lightning strikes across the Quartz Plateau. The vitrified mineral drinks electrical surges with a dry crackle and leaves the wearer unscathed.

suff-of-the-storm-rod.summary: Tier-4 suffix for armor, shields, amulets, and rings that delivers high lightning resistance.
suff-of-the-storm-rod.flavor: Modeled after the heavy bronze lightning arrestors bolted atop Harborwatch's lighthouse. Storm-rod gear lets frontline soldiers stand right under a stormtree's boughs without smelling like burnt hair.

suff-of-spite.summary: Tier-1 suffix for weapons, rings, and amulets that adds a small critical strike bonus.
suff-of-spite.flavor: Filed with a deliberate, nasty burr along the edge by border brawlers who never fought fair. It catches on leather straps and turns ordinary grazing cuts into ugly, bleeding gouges.

suff-of-the-butcher.summary: Tier-2 suffix for weapons, rings, and amulets that grants a moderate critical strike bonus.
suff-of-the-butcher.flavor: Weighted like a Thornwick slaughterhouse cleaver so the blade drops straight through joint and gristle without bouncing. Quartermasters frown at the name, yet every mercenary asks for one.

suff-of-arteries.summary: Tier-3 suffix for weapons, rings, and amulets that provides a strong critical strike bonus.
suff-of-arteries.flavor: Honed by field surgeons turned mercenaries who knew every soft seam beneath a soldier's mail. A single clean thrust finds the gap where armor ends and panic begins.

suff-of-execution.summary: Tier-4 suffix for weapons, rings, and amulets that delivers a high critical strike bonus.
suff-of-execution.flavor: Balanced for one final, unanswerable stroke rather than polite fencing. Headsman-marked steel carries a grim reputation along the Border, as few enemies ever survive its first clean landing.

suff-of-the-tick.summary: Tier-1 suffix for weapons and rings that grants light lifesteal on hit.
suff-of-the-tick.flavor: Scratched with a crude fen-leech charm by desperate poachers who could not afford healing draughts. It draws only a thin trickle of vigor per strike, yet every drop counts in a ditch fight.

suff-of-the-leech.summary: Tier-2 suffix for weapons, rings, and amulets that provides moderate lifesteal on hit.
suff-of-the-leech.flavor: Tempered in brackish Redmarsh pools teeming with fat alkali leeches. The metal feels strangely clammy in the palm, drinking enemy vitality with every cut to keep its wielder upright.

suff-of-exsanguination.summary: Tier-3 suffix for weapons, rings, and amulets that grants strong lifesteal on hit.
suff-of-exsanguination.flavor: Stamped with the Salt-Tithe Commission's sharpest foreclosure mark, repurposed by mercenaries with a dark sense of humor. Every blow collects its due straight from the target's veins.

suff-of-the-strigoi.summary: Tier-4 suffix for weapons and amulets that delivers high lifesteal on hit.
suff-of-the-strigoi.flavor: Whispered to be forged by rogue abbey clerks who crossed the line from auditing the dead to feeding on the living. A blade of the crimson thirst turns reckless charges into eerie endurance.

suff-of-quietude.summary: Tier-1 suffix for helms, armor, rings, and amulets that adds light mana regeneration.
suff-of-quietude.flavor: Worn by country wayshrine keepers who needed peace of mind amid barking hounds and leaking roofs. It steadies the breath and lets a caster's mana trickle back between skirmishes.

suff-of-the-cistern.summary: Tier-2 suffix for weapons, helms, armor, rings, and amulets that grants moderate mana regeneration.
suff-of-the-cistern.flavor: Etched with the interlocking water-channels of Ironheart's old engineering blueprints. Even when the surrounding air is parched and dead, a cistern-marked piece keeps a steady stream of mana flowing.

suff-of-the-pendulum.summary: Tier-3 suffix for weapons, helms, rings, and amulets that provides strong mana regeneration.
suff-of-the-pendulum.flavor: Calibrated to the steady tick of Oakhaven's brass tide-clocks. Casters who wear it fall into a calm, relentless rhythm, recovering mana almost as fast as they can spend it.

suff-of-perpetual-ash.summary: Tier-4 suffix for weapons, helms, armor, and amulets that delivers high mana regeneration.
suff-of-perpetual-ash.flavor: Inscribed with the Collegium's closed-loop furnace glyph, recycling stray heat and spent charge back into fresh power. Senior archons treasure it during long caldera sieges where rest is impossible.

aff2-riveted.summary: Tier-1 prefix for armor and shields that adds flat physical armor.
aff2-riveted.flavor: Double-punched iron studs hammered straight through boiled hide in Thornwick's muddy smithy yards. It rattles when you run, yet it stops a gnoll hatchet from splitting your ribs.

aff2-bog-stained.summary: Tier-1 prefix for armor and boots that grants poison resistance.
aff2-bog-stained.flavor: Soaked in dark Fenwick peat-water until the leather turns permanently brown and smells of wet moss. Marsh-guides swear the tannin seals the pores against venom and ditch-rot alike.

aff2-notched.summary: Tier-1 weapon prefix that adds a modest flat damage bonus.
aff2-notched.flavor: Border veterans file shallow serrations into cheap blades so they bite into wool and leather instead of glancing off. Quartermasters hate sharpening them, yet nobody argues with the results.

aff2-waxed.summary: Tier-1 prefix for bows and gloves that improves accuracy.
aff2-waxed.flavor: Rubbed down with warm beeswax and pine pitch to keep rain from swelling the wood or slicking the grip. A dry, tacky hold keeps an archer's draw dead steady in a downpour.

aff2-tallow-sealed.summary: Tier-1 prefix for armor and boots that provides cold resistance.
aff2-tallow-sealed.flavor: Smeared thick with mutton tallow along every stitch-hole before marching into the northern drizzle. It attracts hungry camp dogs, yet it keeps freezing river-water from soaking through to the skin.

rune-rune-of-thulor.summary: Rank-10 low rune requiring level 23 from Acts I–II, adding elemental damage to weapons or high cold resistance in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-thulor.flavor: Chiseled from frost-split slate along the northern river bluffs where winter fog never quite lifts. Scouts socket Thulor into their cloaks before crossing high passes, claiming it keeps rime off their bowstrings and chill out of their knees.

rune-rune-of-amnir.summary: Rank-11 low rune (Req Lv 25) from Acts I–II, granting lifesteal in weapons, damage reduction in armor, or thorns damage in shields.
rune-rune-of-amnir.flavor: Border veterans prize Amnir above prettier gems because it pays its keep in ugly, drawn-out brawls. Hammered into a sword hilt, it seems to steady a bleeding man's grip; set into a shield, it leaves attackers nursing split knuckles.

rune-rune-of-solan.summary: Rank-12 mid rune (Req Lv 27) from Acts II–IV, raising minimum weapon damage or granting flat damage reduction in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-solan.flavor: Struck in heavy brass-toned stone by Redmarsh artificers who hated unpredictable blows. A Solan-socketed blade hits with stubborn consistency, while a breastplate bearing its mark turns aside glancing arrows like a stone wall.

rune-rune-of-shaela.summary: Rank-13 mid rune (Req Lv 29) from Acts II–IV, improving weapon accuracy, faster hit recovery in armor, or higher block chance in shields.
rune-rune-of-shaela.flavor: Light as pumice and slick to the thumb, Shaela stones are traded quietly among duelists and boarding marines. When a heavy club rattles your helm, this little glyph is often the difference between recovering your footing and eating mud.

rune-rune-of-dolur.summary: Rank-14 mid rune (Req Lv 31) from Acts II–IV, boosting weapon accuracy or providing steady health regeneration in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-dolur.flavor: Field surgeons in Oakhaven used to sew Dolur chips into stretcher-canvas when bandages ran short. It will not reattach a lost finger, but on a three-day march through salt-marsh heat it keeps old cuts from festering.

rune-rune-of-helva.summary: Rank-15 mid rune usable from level 1, dropping in Acts II–IV as a prized crafting component for specialized transmutations and runewords.
rune-rune-of-helva.flavor: Oddly blank to the naked eye, Helva stones carry no immediate blessing when hammered into plain iron. Quartermasters still lock them in the strongbox, knowing seasoned rune-smiths pay silver to use them as binders in heavier work.

rune-rune-of-ioran.summary: Rank-16 mid rune (Req Lv 35) from Acts II–IV, adding weapon damage or boosting strength and maximum health in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-ioran.flavor: Quarried from deep ironstone seams where miners work by tallow light until their shoulders knot like oak. Wearing Ioran in your harness lends the stubborn heft of a draft ox, letting tired men hold heavy pavises through long sieges.

rune-rune-of-lumix.summary: Rank-17 mid rune (Req Lv 37) from Acts II–IV, increasing weapon damage or granting intellect and maximum mana in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-lumix.flavor: Pale as chalked vellum, Lumix stones hum softly whenever a spellbook is opened nearby. Collegium clerks keep them tucked inside ink-stained cuffs to stay sharp through midnight audits and long ward-calibrations.

rune-rune-of-kord.summary: Rank-18 mid rune (Req Lv 39) from Acts II–IV, adding weapon accuracy or boosting agility and flat defense in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-kord.flavor: Named after a cliff-runner who outran three tax-cutters across wet shingle without dropping his pack. Kord runes are favored by archers and light scouts who prefer not to be standing where a basalt club lands.

rune-rune-of-falkor.summary: Rank-19 mid rune (Req Lv 41) from Acts II–IV, adding solid weapon damage or boosting strength when socketed into armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-falkor.flavor: Heavy, dark-veined stones stamped with a blunt hammer-mark by Ironcamp foundrymen. Mercenary captains hand Falkor runes to their best breachers, knowing a little extra shoulder behind a warhammer opens stuck gates faster than any key.

rune-rune-of-lemur.summary: Rank-20 mid rune (Req Lv 43) from Acts II–IV, dramatically increasing gold found from enemies in weapons, armor, and shields.
rune-rune-of-lemur.flavor: Every dishonest quartermaster on the Border dreams of a Lemur stone. Though it offers no help in a swordfight, companies that socket it into their gear always seem to pry twice as many crowns out of every fallen raider's purse.

rune-rune-of-pulon.summary: Rank-21 mid rune (Req Lv 45) from Acts II–IV, granting strong weapon damage and accuracy or high flat defense in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-pulon.flavor: Cut from dense coastal granite that has weathered a thousand winter gales without pitting. Pulon reinforces cheap plate and sharpens dull steel alike, making it one of the most fought-over prizes in any bounty chest.

rune-rune-of-umbra.summary: Rank-22 mid rune (Req Lv 47) from Acts II–IV, inflicting open wounds in weapons or granting all-element resistances in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-umbra.flavor: Dark as cooled pitch and cold even beside a smelter fire, Umbra stones leave jagged, weeping cuts when mounted in steel. Set into a shield, however, the same grim glyph drinks fire, frost, and lightning without complaint.

rune-rune-of-malcor.summary: Rank-23 high rune (Req Lv 49) from Act IV endgame, preventing enemy healing in weapons or reducing magic damage in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-malcor.flavor: Forged in the caldera approaches where shamans and embalmers refuse to let their dead stay down. A single Malcor-marked blade shuts down battlefield mending, turning stubborn cultists into ordinary, manageable corpses.

rune-rune-of-istari.summary: Rank-24 high rune (Req Lv 51) from Act IV endgame, boosting magic item find across weapons, armor, and shields.
rune-rune-of-istari.flavor: Talisman-hunters and relic-smugglers trade whole chests of silver for a single Istari chip. It glows faintly near buried vaults and forgotten armories, guiding its bearer toward rare steel that ordinary patrols walk right past.

rune-rune-of-guldan.summary: Rank-25 high rune (Req Lv 53) from Act IV endgame, adding high weapon accuracy or raising maximum poison resistance in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-guldan.flavor: Steeped in distilled alkali and sulfur fumes until the stone turns a sickly, indelible green. Veterans marching through spore-choked ruins prize Guldan for hardening their lungs against venoms that drop lesser men in three breaths.

rune-rune-of-vexor.summary: Rank-26 high rune (Req Lv 55) from Act IV endgame, granting mana steal in weapons or raising maximum fire resistance in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-vexor.flavor: Warm as a freshly banked coal, Vexor draws stray energy out of every strike to feed hungry casters. Mounted in a shield or cuirass, it lets frontline soldiers wade straight through caldera flames without blistering.

rune-rune-of-ohmar.summary: Rank-27 high rune (Req Lv 57) from Act IV endgame, adding heavy weapon damage or raising maximum cold resistance in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-ohmar.flavor: Struck from pale alpine quartz that never cracks under a sledgehammer. Weapons fitted with Ohmar cleave through heavy bone and iron alike, while armor bearing its seal shrugs off glacial frost that would snap ordinary steel.

rune-rune-of-loral.summary: Rank-28 high rune (Req Lv 59) from Act IV endgame, granting deadly strike in weapons or raising maximum lightning resistance in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-loral.flavor: Sharp-edged and humming with bottled static, Loral turns clean hits into devastating finishing blows. Storm-coast marines also socket it into their shields so stray lightning arcs ground harmlessly into the flagstones.

rune-rune-of-suran.summary: Rank-29 high rune (Req Lv 61) from Act IV endgame, adding solid weapon damage or a large maximum mana pool in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-suran.flavor: Deep indigo stones recovered from collapsed pre-schism observatories along the eastern ridge. Senior arcanists covet Suran above gold, as a single stone holds enough reserve mana to sustain an entire siege barrage.

rune-rune-of-beran.summary: Rank-30 high rune (Req Lv 63) from Act IV endgame, granting crushing blow in weapons or strong damage reduction in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-beran.flavor: Dense as lead and scarred with ancient siege-marks, Beran is the nightmare of stone golems and armored titans. One lucky swing with a Beran-socketed maul can crack a colossus wide open like a dropped clay jug.

rune-rune-of-jahkar.summary: Rank-31 high rune (Req Lv 65) from Act IV endgame, ignoring target defense in weapons or adding high maximum health in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-jahkar.flavor: A ruthless First-Dynasty war-glyph that refuses to acknowledge thick plate or clever parries. Soldiers who socket Jahkar into their armor seem to walk through volleys that should have pinned them to the dirt.

rune-rune-of-chamir.summary: Rank-32 high rune (Req Lv 67) from Act IV endgame, freezing foes in weapons or preventing the wearer from being frozen in shields.
rune-rune-of-chamir.flavor: Clear as glacier ice and painfully cold to bare fingers, Chamir locks enemies in brittle rime on contact. Set into a tower shield, it keeps a vanguard captain moving freely even when frost-bells toll overhead.

rune-rune-of-zodar.summary: Rank-33 pinnacle high rune (Req Lv 69) from Act IV endgame, granting massive weapon damage or top flat defense in armor and shields.
rune-rune-of-zodar.flavor: The rarest stone in the Border ledgers, whispered about in taverns by veterans who have never actually seen one. Hammered into steel, Zodar elevates ordinary frontier iron into a weapon worthy of the Threshold itself.

rw-stealth.summary: Level 17 armor runeword crafted with Rune of Talgor then Rune of Aeth, favored by scouts and nimble skirmishers.
rw-stealth.flavor: Border smugglers first paired Talgor and Aeth on oiled jerkins to slip past Thornwick toll-guards on foggy nights. The finished weave muffles clinking buckles and sheds marsh damp, making it a staple for early campaigners.

rw-steel.summary: Level 13 weapon runeword forged with Rune of Tyra then Rune of Eldun, offering reliable early-game martial punch.
rw-steel.flavor: An honest, no-nonsense forge recipe taught to apprentice smiths when the Salt Tithe left only scrap iron in the bins. It turns a pitted levy sword into a dependable workhorse that holds an edge through mud and bone.

rw-lore.summary: Level 27 helm runeword crafted with Rune of Orthan then Rune of Solan, prized by casters and tactical officers.
rw-lore.flavor: Collegium field-scholars etched this pairing inside battered leather caps to keep their heads clear amid cannon smoke and static storms. Wearers claim it quiets the ringing in your ears long enough to finish an incantation.

rw-rhyme.summary: Level 29 shield runeword formed with Rune of Shaela then Rune of Aeth, built for steady defense in harsh elements.
rw-rhyme.flavor: Harborwatch marines passed this two-rune pattern down from father to son for fighting on sleet-slick piers. A shield bound with Frost Ward feels lighter on the arm and refuses to lock up when freezing spray hits the iron.

rw-smoke.summary: Level 37 armor runeword crafted with Rune of Neph then Rune of Lumix, shrouding the wearer against heavy battlefield fire.
rw-smoke.flavor: Born in the soot-choked trenches outside Ironcamp, where survival depended on not being seen by cliffside arbalests. The armor smells faintly of wet peat-smoke and seems to blur the wearer's outline in poor light.

rw-leaf.summary: Level 19 weapon runeword forged with Rune of Tyra then Rune of Ralon, channeling fierce early fire power.
rw-leaf.flavor: Hedge-pyromancers carve this pairing into dry ash staves just before the autumn rains turn the northern roads to mire. Even in a downpour, a Blaze of Autumn staff sparks easily and keeps the bearer's knuckles warm.

rw-white.summary: Level 35 weapon runeword crafted with Rune of Dolur then Rune of Ioran, tailored for necromancers commanding bone and marrow.
rw-white.flavor: Probate clerks in the coastal abbeys originally used this pairing to reinforce brittle reliquary wands. In a necromancer's hand, the pale runes knit splintered bone together with terrifying speed and precision.

war-bulwark-1.summary: Tier-1 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 5) that steadily increases flat armor for frontline durability.
war-bulwark-1.flavor: Thornwick sergeants inspect every recruit's rivets before dawn, knowing a loose strap kills faster than a gnoll spear. Doubling the iron over the ribs adds weight on the march, yet nobody complains once arrows start falling.

war-bulwark-2.summary: Tier-1 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 5) that raises shield block chance against incoming attacks.
war-bulwark-2.flavor: Green soldiers flinch behind their shields and take the blow on the flat; veterans angle the oak rim to glance steel aside. A well-placed iron boss turns a fatal cleaver swing into nothing more than a bruised forearm.

war-bulwark-3.summary: Tier-2 Warrior Bulwark active skill (max rank 3) requiring Oak Rim Guard, stunning an enemy with a heavy shield slam.
war-bulwark-3.flavor: Nothing ends a shaman's sermon faster than forty pounds of tarred oak driven straight into his teeth. Levy instructors drill this move until recruits can land it ankle-deep in river mud without losing their footing.

war-bulwark-4.summary: Tier-2 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 4) requiring Riveted Plate, boosting resistance against ranged missiles.
war-bulwark-4.flavor: Holding a wet ditch under quill-fiend fire teaches a man to tuck his chin and angle his shoulders by instinct. What looks like cowering from afar is actually the reason half the Vanguard Company still has both eyes.

war-bulwark-5.summary: Tier-3 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 4) requiring Brace the Ditch, granting a substantial boost to maximum health.
war-bulwark-5.flavor: A high iron collar chafes the jaw and collects rainwater, yet veterans refuse to march without one. When a sand-raider's scimitar slides off your pauldron, that ugly strip of plate earns its weight in crowns.

war-bulwark-6.summary: Tier-3 Warrior Bulwark active skill (max rank 3) requiring Shield Bash, granting bonus armor to the entire party.
war-bulwark-6.flavor: One shield is a door; six shields overlapped at the knee are a stone wall. When the sergeant barks the order, even nervous militia remember to lean into their neighbor's rim and let the charge break itself.

war-bulwark-7.summary: Tier-4 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 2) requiring Gorget of Iron, giving a chance to survive fatal blows.
war-bulwark-7.flavor: Some borderers are simply too stubborn to die before their pay-chit clears. Even after a blow that should drop an ox, sheer grit and thick northern bone keep them upright long enough to swing back.

war-bulwark-8.summary: Tier-4 Warrior Bulwark capstone (max rank 2) requiring Lock Shields, sharply reducing incoming damage during heavy assaults.
war-bulwark-8.flavor: At the Alder Bridge stand, three pikemen held a collapsed arch for half an hour while refugees crossed behind them. Living Bastion is that same refusal to yield, honed into a discipline that laughs at siege engines.

war-reaver-1.summary: Tier-1 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 5) that increases base melee damage across all close-quarters strikes.
war-reaver-1.flavor: Border smiths leave a little extra iron behind the sweet spot of a blade because fancy balance does not split a flintback's shell. Put your hips into the swing and let gravity finish the argument.

war-reaver-2.summary: Tier-1 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 5) that adds armor penetration to break through plated foes.
war-reaver-2.flavor: Learned from escaped Deep Quarry miners who knew exactly where a basalt seam cracks under a pickaxe. Apply the same angle to an imperial breastplate and the rivets pop like dry peas.

war-reaver-3.summary: Tier-2 Warrior Reaver active skill (max rank 4) requiring Heavy Edge, sweeping melee damage across multiple nearby foes.
war-reaver-3.flavor: When briar-hounds or gnolls crowd your flanks, careful fencing gets you chewed to pieces. A wide, brutal arc clears breathing room in a single heartbeat and reminds the pack to keep its distance.

war-reaver-4.summary: Tier-2 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 4) requiring Quarry Swing, restoring health whenever you fell an enemy.
war-reaver-4.flavor: Veterans never wipe their leather grips mid-fight; the tackiness keeps the hilt from twisting in wet hands. Dropping a foe brings a cold rush of relief that steadies the pulse and dulls fresh bruises.

war-reaver-5.summary: Tier-3 Warrior Reaver active skill (max rank 3) requiring Cleaving Arc, stripping enemy armor to expose them to follow-up blows.
war-reaver-5.flavor: Heavy knights rely on buckles, straps, and shoulder pins to stay intact. Aim for the iron hinges instead of the thick chest-plate, and even a dread knight turns soft enough for a levy spear to finish.

war-reaver-6.summary: Tier-3 Warrior Reaver active skill (max rank 3) requiring Bloodied Grip, charging into enemies for heavy impact damage.
war-reaver-6.flavor: Developed by Ironcamp breachers who had to cross open ground before cliffside arbalests could wind their prods. Drop your shoulder, tuck your chin, and hit the enemy line like an unhitched supply wagon.

war-reaver-7.summary: Tier-4 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 3) requiring Sunder Hinges, increasing attack speed as combat intensifies.
war-reaver-7.flavor: Once a seasoned reaver finds his rhythm, the weight of the steel stops mattering. Each follow-through feeds directly into the next backswing, turning a slow two-handed maul into a relentless threshing flail.

war-reaver-8.summary: Tier-4 Warrior Reaver capstone (max rank 2) requiring Breaker's Rush, multiplying damage to finish weakened targets.
war-reaver-8.flavor: No mercy, no flourishes, and no wasted motion—just a single merciless cut meant to settle the account permanently. Quartermasters call it tidy work; survivors on the other side rarely call it anything at all.

war-banner-1.summary: Tier-1 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 5) that strengthens morale resistance against fear and battlefield panic.
war-banner-1.flavor: Fresh levies break at the first howl from the fog unless an officer stands where they can see his boots planted. Calm orders spoken at normal volume do more to hold a line than a dozen shouted threats.

war-banner-2.summary: Tier-1 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 5) that reduces fatigue buildup during prolonged marches and battles.
war-banner-2.flavor: Running uphill in chainmail is a fine way to collapse before the fighting starts. Old Vanguard sergeants teach their men to breathe through the nose, shorten their stride, and save their wind for the breach.

war-banner-3.summary: Tier-2 Warrior Banner active skill (max rank 3) requiring Muster Discipline, sharply boosting block chance while holding ground.
war-banner-3.flavor: Plant the boot, lock the elbow, and refuse to give up one inch of mud. Even poorly equipped militia can stop a cavalry rush when they trust the man beside them not to turn tail.

war-banner-4.summary: Tier-2 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 4) requiring Rationed Pace, improving the accuracy of hired mercenaries.
war-banner-4.flavor: Hired blades fight better when their commander actually calls targets instead of waving vaguely at the treeline. A sharp nod and a pointed gauntlet turn sloppy brawlers into disciplined flankers.

war-banner-5.summary: Tier-3 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 4) requiring Veteran's Eye, lowering the gold upkeep required for mercenary squads.
war-banner-5.flavor: Mercenaries charge double when they think their captain is an idiot who will get them killed in a ditch. Prove you know how to read terrain and keep them fed, and they suddenly ask far less silver at payday.

war-banner-6.summary: Tier-3 Warrior Banner active skill (max rank 3) requiring Hold the Line, restoring stamina to rally exhausted allies.
war-banner-6.flavor: A battered brass horn blown over the din of clashing steel cuts straight through exhaustion. Men who thought their arms were lead find strength for one more push when the company call echoes across the field.

war-banner-7.summary: Tier-4 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 3) requiring Hardened Pay, projecting a damage aura that empowers nearby allies.
war-banner-7.flavor: When the Vanguard standard pushes forward through ash and arrow-fire, the whole line leans in behind it. Soldiers strike harder simply because they refuse to look cowardly next to a commander who never flinches.

war-banner-8.summary: Tier-4 Warrior Banner capstone (max rank 2) requiring Rallying Horn, granting a powerful haste surge to the company.
war-banner-8.flavor: Torn by buckshot, scorched by caldera embers, and patched with saddle-leather, the company banner still flies. Seeing it planted in the breach drives every man in earshot into a relentless, double-time assault.

arc-deadeye-1.summary: Tier-1 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 5) that increases base ranged damage with bows and crossbows.
arc-deadeye-1.flavor: Hasty archers loose three shafts into the mud for every one that bites. Drawing cleanly to the jawbone and holding half a breath puts enough punch behind an ash arrow to punch straight through boiled hide.

arc-deadeye-2.summary: Tier-1 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 5) that improves ranged accuracy across open and stormy terrain.
arc-deadeye-2.flavor: Between river fog in Thornwick and alkali gales in Redmarsh, an arrow rarely flies straight on its own. Good marksmen watch the grass tips and chimney smoke, aiming two hand-breadths upwind before they ever loose.

arc-deadeye-3.summary: Tier-2 Archer Deadeye active skill (max rank 4) requiring Measured Draw, dealing heavy critical damage to vulnerable spots.
arc-deadeye-3.flavor: Even the heaviest dread knight has a thin seam between gorget and visor where leather shows through. Take your time, wait for him to raise his visor to shout, and end the battle with a single shaft.

arc-deadeye-4.summary: Tier-2 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 4) requiring Wind Reader, increasing ranged damage when firing from elevated ground.
arc-deadeye-4.flavor: Canyon raiders in Twin Passes proved how ugly a fight gets when bowmen hold the ridge. Firing downhill adds gravity to the draw weight and lets a sharp eye pick off casters hiding behind tower shields.

arc-deadeye-5.summary: Tier-3 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 4) requiring Aimed Throat-Shot, adding armor penetration to ranged attacks.
arc-deadeye-5.flavor: Broadheads are for deer; narrow, four-sided bodkin points are for imperial plate. Driven by a heavy warbow, a well-tempered bodkin wedges right between iron links and splits them apart with a dry snap.

arc-deadeye-6.summary: Tier-3 Archer Deadeye active skill (max rank 2) requiring High Ground, loosing multiple arrows in a rapid sequence.
arc-deadeye-6.flavor: Alder Ford toll-bowmen practiced holding a spare shaft between their bow-fingers to discourage bandits from rushing the gate. It ruins a proper stance, yet two arrows in the chest settle most arguments quickly.

arc-deadeye-7.summary: Tier-4 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 3) requiring Bodkin Penetration, reducing skill cooldowns on critical hits.
arc-deadeye-7.flavor: When every shot lands where you meant it, the whole battlefield slows down to a tidy rhythm. Draw, loose, watch the target fold, and nock again before the first feathered shaft stops quivering.

arc-deadeye-8.summary: Tier-4 Archer Deadeye capstone (max rank 2) requiring Double Nock, firing a devastating piercing shot through a line of foes.
arc-deadeye-8.flavor: An old border grimace about thrift: why waste three good arrows on a column of raiders when one heavy shaft will do? Drawn past the ear on a reinforced stave, it punches clean through shield, rib, and the man behind.

arc-stalker-1.summary: Tier-1 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 5) that increases movement speed for repositioning and kiting.
arc-stalker-1.flavor: Heavy boots sink into bog-peat and announce your approach from fifty paces. Greywood poachers wrap their soles in greased rawhide, skimming over wet roots and loose scree without leaving a clear print.

arc-stalker-2.summary: Tier-1 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 5) that raises evasion chance against incoming attacks.
arc-stalker-2.flavor: Rubbing bog-mud and crushed alder leaves into a cloak ruins the wool, yet it makes a scout vanish ten paces off the trail. Even in open combat, a low, shifting stance throws off enemy aim.

arc-stalker-3.summary: Tier-2 Archer Stalker active skill (max rank 3) requiring Light Footing, vaulting backward to escape melee threats.
arc-stalker-3.flavor: When a thorn-boar or sand-raider closes inside spear-length, standing your ground is just prideful suicide. Kick off the nearest rock, clear three paces in a single bound, and loose while they are still turning.

arc-stalker-4.summary: Tier-2 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 4) requiring Peat Camouflage, expanding vision range across fog and darkness.
arc-stalker-4.flavor: Most travelers stare straight at the boardwalk and walk right into an ambush. Fen-stalkers scan the waterline for disturbed reeds and unnatural ripples, spotting threats long before the lantern-light reaches them.

arc-stalker-5.summary: Tier-3 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 3) requiring Backstep Vault, boosting damage when striking enemies from the flank.
arc-stalker-5.flavor: Hitting a shielded man from the front is work for a warrior with a heavy mace. Slip around his blind side while he trades blows with your vanguard, and every rib is wide open.

arc-stalker-6.summary: Tier-3 Archer Stalker active skill (max rank 3) requiring Fen Sightlines, deploying a trap that roots pursuing enemies.
arc-stalker-6.flavor: Adapted from iron wolf-gins used along the northern timberlines, scaled up with notched jaws to catch charging beasts and raiders. Nothing ruins a berserker's momentum like stepping into hidden teeth in the grass.

arc-stalker-7.summary: Tier-4 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 3) requiring Flanking Instinct, granting temporary stealth to break enemy focus.
arc-stalker-7.flavor: Drop low into the sedge, let the smoke drift across your shoulders, and stay motionless for two heartbeats. By the time the enemy archers figure out where you went, you are already behind their casters.

arc-stalker-8.summary: Tier-4 Archer Stalker capstone (max rank 2) requiring Hamstring Trap, unleashing a multi-arrow ambush volley.
arc-stalker-8.flavor: The signature trick of Greywood's most wanted poachers when cornered by bailiff patrols. Step out of cover with five shafts fanned between your fingers and turn a quiet clearing into a wall of fletching.

arc-fletcher-1.summary: Tier-1 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 5) that increases ranged attack speed for faster volleys.
arc-fletcher-1.flavor: Crooked feathers wobble in crosswinds and slow down the draw. Trimming stiff grey goose-pinions by hand lets an archer nock and loose cleanly without ever glancing down at the quiver.

arc-fletcher-2.summary: Tier-1 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 5) that reduces mana costs for archer skills and special shots.
arc-fletcher-2.flavor: Wet hemp stretches and snaps in the Thornwick drizzle, ruining a bowman's rhythm. Rubbing beeswax and pine resin into the cord keeps the draw crisp and conserves strength through long skirmishes.

arc-fletcher-3.summary: Tier-2 Archer Fletcher active skill (max rank 4) requiring Goose-Wing Fletch, firing burning arrows that deal fire damage over time.
arc-fletcher-3.flavor: Wrap tow-rag behind the iron head, dip it in wagon-pitch, and touch it to a trench brazier. It ruins the arrow's range slightly, yet nothing clears out a crypt embalmer or spore-matron faster.

arc-fletcher-4.summary: Tier-2 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 4) requiring Waxed Bowstring, restoring mana when looting or recovering arrows.
arc-fletcher-4.flavor: Good shafts are too expensive on the Border to leave sticking out of dead gnolls. Pulling unbroken arrows back out of the mud keeps a practical hunter supplied long after the baggage train falls behind.

arc-fletcher-5.summary: Tier-3 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 4) requiring Pitch-Tipped Shaft, amplifying poison damage dealt by ranged attacks.
arc-fletcher-5.flavor: Redmarsh vipers and fen-toads yield a thick green bile that clings well to notched broadheads. Even a shallow scratch across a raider's wrist turns nasty before he can cross the clearing.

arc-fletcher-6.summary: Tier-3 Archer Fletcher active skill (max rank 3) requiring Salvage Quiver, firing flint-tipped arrows that burst into shrapnel.
arc-fletcher-6.flavor: When iron runs short, border fletchers knap brittle grey chert into jagged heads that shatter on impact against shields. The target takes the shaft; everyone standing elbow-to-elbow beside him takes the splinters.

arc-fletcher-7.summary: Tier-4 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 3) requiring Bile-Dipped Broads, granting broad bow mastery and improved performance.
arc-fletcher-7.flavor: Years of seasoning yew staves, scraping horn bellies, and balancing draw weights teach a hunter every quirk of his weapon. In a master bowyer's hands, even a salvaged frontier bow shoots like a guild prize.

arc-fletcher-8.summary: Tier-4 Archer Fletcher capstone (max rank 2) requiring Shatter-Flint Head, raining multiple waves of arrows over an area.
arc-fletcher-8.flavor: Borrowed from Oakhaven's seawall drills, where a single veteran archer had to pin down an entire boarding boat alone. Loose high into the wind in rapid waves until the flagstones look like a harrowed field.

mag-pyro-1.summary: Tier-1 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 5) that increases all fire spell damage.
mag-pyro-1.flavor: Collegium apprentices spend their first winter learning that fire is not magic—it is just impatient heat. Push the gradient sharp enough and damp wool catches flame even in a northern downpour.

mag-pyro-2.summary: Tier-1 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 5) that grants fire resistance to weather heat and enemy flames.
mag-pyro-2.flavor: Every practicing pyromancer eventually burns off his eyebrows and ruins two good sleeves. The ones who survive learn to weave a thin thermal cushion around their wrists before calling anything hotter than a candle.

mag-pyro-3.summary: Tier-2 Mage Pyromancy active skill (max rank 4) requiring Thermal Gradient, hurling a piercing lance of condensed flame.
mag-pyro-3.flavor: Wide fireballs waste mana on empty mud and risk scorching your own pikemen. Condensing the blaze into a narrow white-hot spear punches cleanly through armored ranks without singeing the vanguard.

mag-pyro-4.summary: Tier-2 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 3) requiring Singed Cuffs, amplifying burning damage over time on ignited foes.
mag-pyro-4.flavor: Oil-soaked leather, dry linen wrappings, and pitch-tarred shields all burn wonderfully once you know how to feed the draft. A skilled pyromancer lets the enemy's own gear finish the work for him.

mag-pyro-5.summary: Tier-3 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 3) requiring Cinder Lance, restoring mana whenever a burning enemy dies.
mag-pyro-5.flavor: Collegium thermodynamicists insist no heat is ever truly lost—it merely changes hands. Reclaiming the dying flare from a fallen target lets a caster keep firing long after his mana flasks run dry.

mag-pyro-6.summary: Tier-3 Mage Pyromancy active skill (max rank 3) requiring Dry Tinder, raising a lasting wall of fire to block and scorch foes.
mag-pyro-6.flavor: Inspired by Ironcamp's slag-channels, which turn narrow alleys into impassable trenches of glowing rock. Drop a burning barrier across a bridge arch and watch charging beasts think twice about crossing.

mag-pyro-7.summary: Tier-4 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 3) requiring Exothermic Surge, expanding the area of effect of fire spells.
mag-pyro-7.flavor: The Collegium forbids widening a combustion radius past three paces inside city walls for obvious reasons. Out in the ash-wastes, however, letting the blast bloom wide clears entire packs in one cast.

mag-pyro-8.summary: Tier-4 Mage Pyromancy capstone (max rank 2) requiring Slag Conduit, triggering a massive volcanic eruption for heavy fire damage.
mag-pyro-8.flavor: Channeling the raw pressure pulsing beneath the Obsidian Caldera is reckless work that leaves boots smoking. When the ground splits and white-hot cinders geyser skyward, nothing left standing remembers why it charged.

mag-temp-1.summary: Tier-1 Mage Tempest passive (max rank 5) that increases storm and lightning spell damage.
mag-temp-1.flavor: Fools try to throw lightning with bare heels in a puddle and end up smoking beside their own staff. A length of copper wire stitched down the boot-sole lets a caster push twice the voltage without cooking himself.

mag-temp-2.summary: Tier-1 Mage Tempest passive (max rank 5) that accelerates spell casting speed.
mag-temp-2.flavor: By holding a light charge across the knuckles, a tempest mage keeps his fingers snapping through gestures faster than the eye can follow. The only drawback is that metal door-latches bite back for hours afterward.

mag-temp-3.summary: Tier-2 Mage Tempest active skill (max rank 3) requiring Copper Grounding, unleashing lightning that jumps between multiple foes.
mag-temp-3.flavor: Armored soldiers standing shoulder-to-shoulder make a lovely circuit. One sharp snap from the fingertips leaps from breastplate to helm down the line, leaving the whole formation twitching in the rain.

greater-mummy.summary: Durable earth-element caster in Act II quarries and vaults that revives fallen allies; burn its pitch-soaked wrappings with fire.
greater-mummy.flavor: Third-Dynasty embalmers sealed themselves inside the dry salt-vaults to guard unpaid probate ledgers. They shuffle slowly through the dust, stitching fallen raiders back upright with copper wire. A single fire pot ends both their sermon and their paperwork.

hollow-king.summary: Heavy water-element undead melee lord haunting Act III locks and gambits; kite its slow swings and melt it down with fire magic.
hollow-king.flavor: Petty coastal barons who drowned with their tax-coffers chained to their waists sometimes refuse to stay under the tide. They march onto the stone quays dripping black brine, swinging corroded broadswords at anyone who dares cross their old toll-lines.

hollow-knight.summary: Disciplined undead melee soldier found across Act III strongholds and infirmaries; shatter its rusted plate with blunt weapons or fire.
hollow-knight.flavor: Once garrison regulars bound by ironclad indentures, these silent husks still answer a trumpet call long after their flesh has rotted away. They hold narrow corridors with infuriating steadiness, never breaking morale and never asking for back pay.

imp.summary: Fragile, quick allied spellcaster unit with fire-like skirmish utility, easily downed by frost bolts and fast ranged volleys.
imp.flavor: Conjured by desperate frontier arcanists who needed cheap ranged support without paying tavern wages. Spite imps bicker constantly, steal brass buttons from the baggage train, and hurl sparks at anything taller than a boot until someone swats them.

ironbark.summary: Slow, high-health earth-element treant guarding Act III wards and rescues; cut it down with fire magic and sustained slashing blows.
ironbark.flavor: Ancient oaks rooted over leaking ley-lines grow bark harder than cast pig-iron. Woodcutters who sink an axe into an ironbark usually lose the blade and a week's wages. They wake only when smoke or trespassers disturb their grove.

lantern-eel.summary: Fast air-element bog caster in Act III citadels and canals; counter its arc strikes with earth attacks and insulated ranged fire.
lantern-eel.flavor: Long, pale predators that coil around submerged lock-chains and discharge pale blue sparks through the brackish water. Canal keepers wear rubberized leather boots and poke every sluice grate with a dry ash pole before reaching in.

mage.summary: Allied spellcasting unit with low health and steady speed, delivering ranged arcane damage unless ambushed by fast melee rushers.
mage.flavor: Dispatched from the Conclave halls with a travel stipend that barely covers dry socks and lamp oil. They grumble about mud on their hems, yet a single well-placed volley from an arcanist saves a dozen levy pikemen from a bad afternoon.

maggot-swarm.summary: Earth-element burrowing melee swarm encountered in Act II convoys and hollows; clear the writhing mass with area fire and cleaves.
maggot-swarm.flavor: Bred in the warm alkali mud beneath overturned supply wagons, these pale larvae boil out of the ground whenever boots vibrate the crust. Teamsters carry buckets of quicklime on the tailboard specifically to salt the ruts behind their wheels.

mire-wisp.summary: Fragile, swift water-element caster lurking in Act I fens and sanctums; bring them down quickly with physical arrows and steel.
mire-wisp.flavor: Pale lanterns of marsh gas that drift just off the rotting boardwalks, mimicking the whale-oil lamps of the Fenwick passage. Travelers who follow their glow end up chest-deep in black peat while the wisp pelts them with freezing sleet.

night-orchard.summary: Tough astral-element ward weaver prowling Act III bastions and harbors; counter its dark spells with fire and heavy axes.
night-orchard.flavor: Gnarled cider trees watered for decades by grave-runoff and spilled ward-ink eventually pull their roots free of the loam. They stalk the coastal terraces at dusk, tangling unwary scouts in thorny branches that hum with cold astral static.

pale-burrower.summary: Earth-element melee tunneler infesting Act II quarries and passes; slow its lunges with frost and finish it off with fire.
pale-burrower.flavor: Blind, chalk-skinned diggers that chew straight through loose sandstone and timber pit-props. Quarry overseers listen for the dry scraping behind the rock face, knowing a tunnel collapse usually follows a burrower's ambush by three heartbeats.

quill-fiend.summary: Ranged sniper beast found across Act I bridges and keeps; absorb its rapid volleys with shielded frontliners and close into melee.
quill-fiend.flavor: Bristling, hound-sized nuisances that rattle their spines like dry reeds before loosing a hail of barbed quills. Border levy troops hate them more than gnolls, because a quill-fiend never stands still long enough to take a proper halberd swing.

redglass-drake.summary: Swift, durable fire-element highland caster in Act IV marches and ramparts; ground it with frost magic and focused ranged volleys.
redglass-drake.flavor: Winged lizards whose scales fused with molten caldera glass during the first tremors. They roost on basalt chimneys above the highland trails, swooping down to scorch supply mules and melt iron helmets onto the heads of careless sentries.

rift-moth.summary: Fast astral-element flyer haunting Act IV beacons and thresholds; swat it out of the ash with physical projectiles and fire.
rift-moth.flavor: Drawn to leaking mana-beacons like ordinary moths to a tallow candle, these dusty-winged pests drink arcane charge straight out of a caster's veins. Arcanists keep iron-mesh veils in their packs whenever they march near broken ward-grids.

rootbound.summary: Slow, high-health earth-element sentinel in Act I fens and bridges; break through its tangled bulk with fire and lightning.
rootbound.flavor: Dead borderers left unburied in the peat sometimes get claimed by bog-willow roots that knit their bones into a walking thicket. They plod across the bridges with terrible patience, swinging knotted limbs thick enough to stove in a buckler.

ruin-mite.summary: Fragile swarming melee burrower infesting Act I keeps and undervaults; sweep the pack clear with area damage and fire.
ruin-mite.flavor: Chitinous scavengers the size of a soldier's boot that nest in damp mortar and chewed grain sacks. One mite is a nuisance you crush with a heel; a hundred pouring out of a collapsed cellar wall will strip a pack-horse to bare ribs.

salt-crab.summary: Durable water-element melee blocker patrolling Act II borders and coastal flats; crack its wet shell with blunt weapons and lightning.
salt-crab.flavor: Armored scavengers that haul themselves out of the alkali flats whenever a caravan spills brine or blood. Their pincers can shear through a leather stirrup, though cooks in Redmarsh swear the leg meat tastes decent if boiled in vinegar.

sand-raider.summary: Rapid dual-scimitar melee fighter in Act II passes and outposts; blunt their speed with frost slows and braced armored troops.
sand-raider.flavor: Desert outlaws who wrap their faces in salt-stiffened linen and strike from canyon blinds before the dust settles. They travel light, carry no banners, and sell their blades to whichever paymaster still has silver left in his chest.

silt-colossus.summary: Massive, slow earth-element citadel guardian in Act IV assaults; kite its heavy swings and shatter its frame with lightning magic.
silt-colossus.flavor: Constructed from compressed river-silt and iron slag by imperial siege-wrights who needed a battering ram that could walk up a hill. Its footsteps crack cobblestones, yet its sluggish turning radius leaves its back wide open to nimble casters.

spore-matron.summary: Earth-element poison hexer lurking in Act III wards and infirmaries; burn her out with fire and ranged bursts from upwind.
spore-matron.flavor: Bloated fungal husks that drift out of damp cellars, puffing clouds of yellow spores that turn a soldier's lungs to wet rags. Field healers burn sulfur braziers around the tents specifically to keep matrons from wandering into the wards.

storm-kite.summary: Very fast air-element ranged caster in Act II outposts and garrisons; shoot it down with archers and earth-grounded wards.
storm-kite.flavor: Skin-winged scavengers that ride the thermal updrafts above Redmarsh, spitting arcs of static at anything carrying bare steel. Sentries learn to keep their pikes lowered during dry winds lest they turn themselves into lightning rods.

stormtree.summary: High-health air-element melee colossus in Act IV beacons and vaults; burn it with fire from outside its static discharge range.
stormtree.flavor: Lightning-struck pines that drank too much stray ward-current and refused to fall. Their split trunks crackle with blue fire, and any warrior who steps too close without grounded boots ends up smoking in the ash.

thorn-boar.summary: Fast melee charger roaming Act I woods and supply roads; stop its rush with braced spears, heavy strikes, and fire.
thorn-boar.flavor: Ill-tempered Greywood tusker whose hide is matted with dried mud and blackthorn spines. A charging boar hits a levy line like a runaway timber cart, though once downed it feeds a whole company for two nights.

warrior.summary: Reliable allied melee man-at-arms with solid health and balanced speed, best holding lines against rushers while avoiding ranged kiting.
warrior.flavor: The unglamorous spine of the Vanguard Company, trained to keep his shield up, his boots dry, and his mouth shut during long marches. He may not understand ley-geometry, but he knows exactly how to hold a muddy bridge until relief arrives.

wendigo-bruiser.summary: Slow, durable water-element freezing brawler in Act III highlands and bastions; keep your distance and melt it with fire magic.
wendigo-bruiser.flavor: Hulking alpine scavengers driven down from the frozen peaks by the caldera tremors. Their breath coats iron armor in brittle rime, and their heavy fists hit hard enough to send a shielded veteran skidding across the gravel.

witch-doctor.summary: Earth-element marsh hexer found in Act II outposts and hollows; shut down its tribal curses quickly with focus fire and stuns.
witch-doctor.flavor: Bitter elders who trade bone-charms and swamp poisons along the edge of the alkali flats. They rattle dried gourds to sour a squad's stamina, preferring to watch imperial patrols collapse from fever rather than risk a fair fight.

elder-juggernaut.summary: Act III earth-element boss guarding the Highland Cairn; shatter its glowing rune-seams with arcane fire and armor-breaking strikes.
elder-juggernaut.flavor: An ancient granite titan bound during the Age of Chains and shaken awake by the dying continent's tremors. Ordinary arrows bounce off its anthracite ribs like hail on a slate roof, and every stomp splits the mountain trail wide open.

lord-captain-korvus.summary: Act III physical and fire boss of the Eastern War Pier; stay clear of burning pitch pools and spread out against his anchor pulls.
lord-captain-korvus.flavor: Known along the coast as the Iron Anchor, Korvus traded his naval commission for blackened plate and twin hooked ship-anchors. He despises the evacuation fleet, determined that if Thornvael must burn, no coward should sail away dry.

arch-mage-malrik.summary: Act IV astral and fire boss in Flight of Malrik; push swiftly up the switchbacks and interrupt his cipher casts before he escapes.
arch-mage-malrik.flavor: Once a respected Collegium fellow who defected to the Iron Pact with stolen border ledgers and cipher-keys. Cornered in Ashveil Gorge, he relies on violet teleportation wards and scorched-earth spells to outrun the reckoning he earned.

arch-warden-korrath.summary: Act IV water and astral boss of the Crown Vault; sunder both Resonance Anchors to strip his invulnerability and cleanse Stasis.
arch-warden-korrath.flavor: Three centuries of unbroken vigil in the pale marble vault turned Korrath's flesh into petrified granite. He swings twin blades of white stone with mechanical calm, convinced that frozen law is the only mercy a chaotic realm deserves.

ember-overlord-vorak.summary: Act IV fire boss ruling the Furnace Heart; shatter both Obsidian Conduit Pillars to halt his molten regeneration and dodge meteors.
ember-overlord-vorak.flavor: Vorak looks at mortal cities the way a smelter looks at impure ore. Draped in slag-forged plate that drips liquid rock, he channels the caldera's magma directly through his veins to burn the old world down to bare iron.

su-pyre-chanter-malgath.summary: Act I tier-4 fire Super Unique shaman with magic resistance, backed by five cinderlings that overwhelm careless squads.
su-pyre-chanter-malgath.flavor: Malgath preached from a burning peat-rick until his own robes fused to his ribs. He wanders the soggy northern passages surrounded by cackling sparks, turning damp timber bridges into funeral pyres for anyone carrying Crown papers.

su-volt-stalker-krazak.summary: Act I tier-4 air Super Unique briar-hound with lightning enchantment and extra speed, leading five swift packmates.
su-volt-stalker-krazak.flavor: A lean grey hound that slept too close to a cracked smelter conduit and woke up crackling with green static. Krazak runs down couriers in the rain, leaving nothing behind but singed leather and the sharp stink of ozone.

su-frostquill-skara.summary: Act I tier-4 water Super Unique quill-fiend with cold enchantment and extra strength, escorted by four lesser snipers.
su-frostquill-skara.flavor: Nesting beneath the frozen mill-wheel of Greywood, Skara grew barbed spines coated in permanent hoarfrost. Her volleys chill a soldier's sword-arm stiff before he can even cross the clearing to reach her.

su-bramblefist-oakhulk.summary: Act I tier-5 earth Super Unique ironbark with stone skin, curses, and extra strength, guarded by three rootbound sentinels.
su-bramblefist-oakhulk.flavor: An ancient quarry-edge oak whose bark grew around rusted debtor chains tossed into the pit decades ago. Thornmaw uproots itself whenever iron boots trespass on its ridge, swinging iron-studded boughs with terrifying reach.

su-arc-carapace-vekor.summary: Act II tier-4 air Super Unique dune-scarab with lightning enchantment and stone skin, flanked by four crackling scarabs.
su-arc-carapace-vekor.flavor: Fed directly on the ruptured quartz wardstones of the plateau, Vekor's shell hardened into conductive mineral glass. Its static discharges arc cleanly from shield to shield, forcing veterans to pick it apart from long range.

su-venomscale-ssorath.summary: Act II tier-5 earth Super Unique viper with extra speed, lightning, and spectral hits, leading four venomous packmates.
su-venomscale-ssorath.flavor: A bloated desert patriarch that coiled around the oasis aquifers until the water turned bitter and green. Caravan scouts claim Ssorath strikes faster than a whip-crack, leaving both venom and cold burns in the same bite.

su-ash-embalmer-khepri.summary: Act II tier-5 earth Super Unique crypt embalmer with extra speed, curses, and mana burn, guarded by four hollow knights.
su-ash-embalmer-khepri.flavor: Chief notary of the sunken Third-Dynasty vaults, Khepri still enforces posthumous debt-liens with copper wire and dry venom. Casters dread his touch, as his curses drain mana faster than a cracked cistern leaks water.

su-crimson-prowler-zara.summary: Act II tier-4 fire Super Unique dune-lurker with extra strength, curses, and fire enchantment, backed by four sand raiders.
su-crimson-prowler-zara.flavor: A notorious canyon ambusher who dips her blades in naphtha before dropping from the sandstone ledges of Twin Passes. Zara takes imperial coin to turn back refugees, laughing as her fire-pots seal the narrow ravines.

su-bog-hexer-zulmar.summary: Act III tier-5 fire Super Unique fen hexer with magic resistance and a blessed aura, leading six dart-blowing skirmishers.
su-bog-hexer-zulmar.flavor: Exiled from the inland marshes, Zulmar set up his smoking fetishes along the wet coastal approaches. His chants harden his dart-blowers against steel and flame alike, turning simple road clearances into costly slogs.

su-thunderbough-elder.summary: Act III tier-5 air Super Unique stormtree with lightning, extra speed, and stone skin, escorted by four rootbound brutes.
su-thunderbough-elder.flavor: The oldest lightning-split pine on the coastal bluffs, humming loud enough to rattle teeth a hundred paces away. Sailors use its blue crown as a storm warning; soldiers know it means grounding their spears or dying.

su-cinderweb-arachna.summary: Act III tier-4 fire Super Unique spore-matron with extra strength, curses, and fire enchantment, trailing five maggot swarms.
su-cinderweb-arachna.flavor: Lurking near smoldering pitch-pits, Ignisweb spins sticky threads soaked in sulfur resin that ignite at the slightest spark. Anyone caught in her cursed webs gets dragged down by her burrowing brood.

su-rimewing-valkor.summary: Act III tier-4 water Super Unique glasswing with cold enchantment, teleporting, and extra speed, backed by four rift moths.
su-rimewing-valkor.flavor: A pale sea-cliff predator that blinks through the freezing spray like a flash of sleet. Valkor dives straight for exposed arcanists, chilling their fingers numb before vanishing back into the coastal fog.

su-fallen-warden-azrael.summary: Act IV tier-5 water Super Unique hollow king with cold enchantment, stone skin, and extra strength, leading three dread knights.
su-fallen-warden-azrael.flavor: Once a senior keeper of the highland watch, Vaelor froze to death refusing to abandon a breached post. Now he patrols the ash-drifts in rime-caked granite plate, punishing anyone who dares march past his broken standard.

su-hellforger-kragg.summary: Act IV tier-5 fire Super Unique anvilmaw with extra strength, speed, spectral hits, and magic resistance, plus three basalt brutes.
su-hellforger-kragg.flavor: Overseer of the caldera's deepest slag-pits, Kragg swings a glowing foundry hammer faster than a man can swing a hatchet. His soot-blackened hide shrugs off ordinary spells, forcing squads to coordinate frost and heavy steel.

su-dreadlord-malakor.summary: Act IV tier-5 astral Super Unique dread knight with curses, blessed aura, and extra strength, commanding five dread knights.
su-dreadlord-malakor.flavor: Sworn to guard the inner seals of the Threshold, Lord Varakh speaks no words and offers no quarter. His cursed banner saps the courage of seasoned veterans while his armored retinue advances in lockstep.

su-soulblight-archon.summary: Act IV tier-5 fire Super Unique cinderhorn with extra speed, fire enchantment, and spectral hits, flanked by five cinderhorns.
su-soulblight-archon.flavor: Gorgath harvests the dying embers of collapsed siege-walls to feed its own furnace-belly. It charges across the basalt flagstones at terrifying speed, leaving scorched bootprints and shattered shields in its wake.

gem-chipped-garnet.summary: Tier-1 socketable gem from Act I nodes and chests, adding physical damage in weapons or extra maximum health in armor.
gem-chipped-garnet.flavor: Pried out of wet river gravel along the Alder Fords by soldiers looking to pad their meager pay. Flawed and dull as dried blood, a chipped garnet still gives a levy blade a little extra bite when hammered into the pommel.

gem-flawed-beryl.summary: Tier-1 socketable gem from Act I nodes and chests, improving weapon accuracy or expanding maximum mana when set in armor.
gem-flawed-beryl.flavor: Cloudy green pebbles dredged from Fenwick ditches and sold by hedge-scholars for a handful of coppers. They rarely cut cleanly, yet even a milky beryl steadies a tired archer's aim or holds a spare drop of mana.

gem-peat-amber.summary: Tier-2 socketable gem from Acts I–II, infusing weapons with lingering poison damage or granting armor poison resistance.
gem-peat-amber.flavor: Fossilized pine resin pulled from deep bog-trenches, often trapping tiny marsh midges inside its yellow glow. Apothecary apprentices grind the scraps into poultices, while mercenaries socket the whole lumps to weather fen-venom.

gem-river-jade.summary: Tier-2 socketable gem from Acts I–II, boosting attack speed in weapons or increasing movement speed when socketed in armor.
gem-river-jade.flavor: Smooth, cold stones tumbled for centuries along the rocky bed of the Alder River. Ferrymen keep one in their pockets for nimble footing on wet planks, and duelists pay well to have them set into sword hilts.

gem-quartz-prism.summary: Tier-3 socketable gem from Acts II–III, adding lightning damage to weapons or granting lightning resistance inside armor.
gem-quartz-prism.flavor: Chipped from the humming obelisks of the Quartz Plateau after the great storm-rupture. Even a finger-sized prism tingles against bare skin, bleeding off stray static or snapping a bright arc down a spear shaft.

gem-bloodstone-cabochon.summary: Tier-3 socketable gem from Acts II–III, providing lifesteal in weapons or a solid boost to maximum health in armor.
gem-bloodstone-cabochon.flavor: Dark green jasper flecked with iron-red veins, smuggled out of the Deep Quarry in miners' lunch tins. Pit-fighters prize it above silver because a blade set with bloodstone seems to keep its wielder upright long after he should drop.

gem-rime-sapphire.summary: Tier-3 socketable gem from Acts II–III, adding cold damage and chill to weapons or cold resistance when fitted into armor.
gem-rime-sapphire.flavor: Cold as a winter well-bucket, these deep blue stones were traded down from the northern peaks before the passes closed. Set into a breastplate, a single sapphire makes the blistering heat of Redmarsh almost bearable.

gem-cinder-ruby.summary: Tier-4 socketable gem from Acts III–IV, packing heavy fire damage into weapons or strong fire resistance into armor.
gem-cinder-ruby.flavor: Formed in the slag-cracks of the Obsidian Caldera where volcanic heat cooks ordinary corundum into glowing crimson. Smiths handle them with iron tongs, as a freshly cut cinder-ruby can scorch a dry leather glove.

gem-astral-opal.summary: Tier-4 socketable gem from Acts III–IV, adding astral damage to weapons or mind resistance when set into armor.
gem-astral-opal.flavor: Milky coastal stones that flash violet whenever the tide turns or a ward-circle hums nearby. Coastal abbeys set them into iron mirrors to steady the nerves of novices keeping watch over restless crypts.

gem-lodestone-heart.summary: Tier-4 socketable gem from Acts III–IV, granting armor penetration in weapons or substantial extra armor when socketed in gear.
gem-lodestone-heart.flavor: Dense black iron-ore pulled from the Magnetic Narrows, strong enough to tug nails straight out of a boot heel. Weaponsmiths wedge slivers of lodestone behind blade edges so strikes bite cleanly through riveted plate.

gem-starfall-diamond.summary: Tier-5 endgame gem from Act IV and Hard+, boosting critical strike chance in weapons or granting all resistances in armor.
gem-starfall-diamond.flavor: Harder than anything forged since the First Dynasty, these clear stones were pried from pre-schism foundation markers. A jeweler can ruin three iron files trying to facet one, yet veterans kill for a single mounted stone.

gem-obsidian-sun.summary: Tier-5 endgame gem from Act IV and Hard+, adding heavy fire and astral damage in weapons or large health and mana in armor.
gem-obsidian-sun.flavor: Black volcanic glass shot through with a trapped thread of golden ley-light from the Threshold anchors. Quartermasters lock them in lead boxes, claiming they make nearby compasses spin and old wounds ache.

rune-tal.summary: Tier-1 Act I rune that increases gold dropped from kills in weapons or reduces fatigue when socketed into armor.
rune-tal.flavor: Scratched onto copper slugs by Thornwick tax-clerks who believed a tidy ledger brought good fortune. Mercenaries hammer the Tally mark into their hilts, joking that if they have to bleed in the mud, the coin better add up.

rune-kor.summary: Tier-1 Act I rune granting armor penetration in weapons or extra physical armor when fitted into defensive gear.
rune-kor.flavor: The simplest smithy stamp on the border, denoting pig-iron that passed a cold hammer test without cracking. Levy soldiers press Kor-marked studs into their shields and axe-heads before marching out to the fords.

rune-ven.summary: Tier-2 rune from Acts I–II, boosting mana regeneration in weapons or increasing healing received when set in armor.
rune-ven.flavor: Carved on clay cistern-markers to bless dry wells with steady seepage. Field healers and arcanists alike trade silver for Ven stones, appreciating anything that keeps a draught flowing when supplies run thin.

rune-silt.summary: Tier-2 rune from Acts I–II, extending slow duration in weapons or boosting evasion when socketed into armor.
rune-silt.flavor: Born among the Redmarsh surveyors who learned how easily wet alkali swallows a careless boot. Bound into gear, the Silt glyph makes an enemy's stride drag like mud while helping its wearer slip clear of heavy swings.

rune-gale.summary: Tier-3 rune from Acts II–III, accelerating cast and attack speed in weapons or improving missile block in armor.
rune-gale.flavor: Etched onto bronze weathervanes along the Oakhaven cliffs to measure sea-squalls. Boarding marines love the Gale mark for turning away arbalest bolts on exposed decks, while casters prize its brisk rhythm.

rune-lien.summary: Tier-3 rune from Acts II–III, amplifying damage-over-time and curses in weapons or extending curse duration in armor.
rune-lien.flavor: The jagged notary sign of the Third Dynasty, stamped onto unpaid debt-rolls to bind a debtor's estate past the grave. Necromancers etch it onto wands so their hexes cling like compound interest.

rune-ward.summary: Tier-3 rune from Acts II–III, increasing damage against summons in weapons or granting shadow and astral resistance in armor.
rune-ward.flavor: Chiseled into abbey lintels and lighthouse doors to keep restless spirits from crossing the threshold. Veterans marching toward the sunken crypts stitch Ward-stamped discs straight into their gambesons.

rune-slag.summary: Tier-4 rune from Acts III–IV, boosting critical damage in weapons or adding heavy physical armor when set in defensive gear.
rune-slag.flavor: Cast from cooled furnace dross in Ironcamp's smoky yards, rough-edged and ugly as a broken tooth. Sappers swear a Slag rune hits harder than polished steel simply because it refuses to glance off.

rune-oath.summary: Tier-4 rune from Acts III–IV, strengthening raised servants in weapons or boosting aura effectiveness when set in armor.
rune-oath.flavor: A double-knotted sigil once sworn over crossed halberds by the Vanguard Company's founders. Whether commanding living levies or bound skeletons, officers socket Oath stones to keep their ranks steady under fire.

rune-flux.summary: Tier-4 rune from Acts III–IV, reducing skill cooldowns in weapons or lowering spell mana costs when fitted into armor.
rune-flux.flavor: Collegium thermodynamicists developed the Flux mark to vent excess pressure from overheated ward-rings. In the field, it lets exhausted casters cycle spells without burning through their last blue draught.

rune-crown.summary: Tier-5 endgame rune from Act IV and Hard+, boosting boss damage in weapons or granting high all-resistances in armor.
rune-crown.flavor: Modeled after the old First-Dynasty seal of immutable law, struck in cold pale metal that never tarnishes. Only elite vanguard commanders and threshold archivists ever see a genuine Order rune outside a vault.

rune-ash.summary: Tier-5 endgame rune from Act IV and Hard+, granting lifesteal and weapon damage or massive health and armor in defensive gear.
rune-ash.flavor: Drawn in glowing soot inside the caldera's inner redoubts, humming with the stubborn heat of a banked forge. Those who socket the Ember rune fight like they have nothing left to lose and everything to burn.

gem-chipped-diamond.summary: Tier-1 chipped diamond from Act I shrines and elites; adds undead damage in weapons, an attribute in armor, or all resistances in shields.
gem-chipped-diamond.flavor: Tiny, sharp splinters knocked loose from old shrine-markers and swept up by parish sextons. Even a speck of clear diamond makes an undead horror recoil when pressed into a sword fuller or shield boss.

gem-flawed-diamond.summary: Tier-2 flawed diamond from Acts I–II shrines and cube upgrades; boosts undead damage, armor attributes, or shield resistances.
gem-flawed-diamond.flavor: Clouded by hairline fractures yet hard enough to scratch glass, these stones circulate through border pawnshops after every graveyard skirmish. Shield-bearers prize them as cheap insurance against elemental hexes.

gem-diamond.summary: Tier-3 regular diamond from Acts II–III shrines and cube upgrades; strong undead damage in weapons and balanced resistances in shields.
gem-diamond.flavor: Cleanly faceted by guild lapidaries in Oakhaven before the evacuation stripped the workshops bare. Set into a kite shield, a regular diamond turns aside fire, frost, and lightning with quiet reliability.

gem-flawless-diamond.summary: Tier-4 flawless diamond from Acts III–IV shrines and cube upgrades; high undead damage, armor stats, or shield all-resistances.
gem-flawless-diamond.flavor: Clear as winter ice and worth a small ship's cargo in peacetime. Harborwatch officers traded entire chests of silver for flawless diamonds to fortify their shields against the caldera's elemental storms.

gem-perfect-diamond.summary: Tier-5 endgame perfect diamond from Act IV and Hard+; massive undead damage in weapons, strong armor stats, and top shield resistances.
gem-perfect-diamond.flavor: Cut with mathematical precision that only First-Dynasty masters or a transmutation cube can achieve. Light passes through it without a single flaw, burning away grave-rot and grounding the fiercest elemental blasts.

gem-chipped-amethyst.summary: Tier-1 chipped amethyst from Act I shrines and elites; improves weapon accuracy, armor strength, or shield defense.
gem-chipped-amethyst.flavor: Pale purple shards found in rocky creek beds north of Thornwick. Recruits glue them into buckler rims or bow grips, swearing the dull violet gleam keeps their hands steady when gnolls howl in the fog.

gem-flawed-amethyst.summary: Tier-2 flawed amethyst from Acts I–II shrines and cube upgrades; grants accuracy in weapons, body stats in armor, or shield defense.
gem-flawed-amethyst.flavor: Slightly deeper in hue than creek-bed chips, these stones turn up in quarry tailings and smugglers' pouches. Mercenaries use them to add a little extra heft to their plate without adding weight to their packs.

gem-amethyst.summary: Tier-3 regular amethyst from Acts II–III shrines and cube upgrades; solid weapon accuracy, armor body bonus, and shield defense.
gem-amethyst.flavor: Cut into neat six-sided prisms by Redmarsh lapidaries who learned to polish quartz in alkali grit. A regular amethyst sits comfortably in a heavy helm or warhammer, steadying both blow and stance.
